results.notes:
SOURCES USED: out/verify/mech_dims.json (2026-09-02, FreeCAD Mesh.BoundBox, 47 meshes) = dimensional truth; out/stress/report.json (cecad.stress, gmsh+CalculiX, PLA, 20 N); out/print/slice.json (BambuStudio 02.08.02.61 via ce-slice 0.1.0, Bambu Lab H2S 0.4 nozzle, 0.20mm Standard, sliced 2026-09-02) = real slicer grams/times; out/refcheck/<slug>/r*/compare.json = shape fidelity; out/measure/foot/probe_foot{,2}.txt, probe_sole{,2}.txt, floor_table.txt and out/measure/ankle/{fits_ankle_left.txt,mirror-test.json} = raw probes; ce-parts/<slug>/iterations/v0.0.x/cad/part.py = every constant with its probe citation; docs/DFM.md, docs/PARTS.md, docs/BOM.md, docs/PRODUCTION.md; ce-connections/{press-fit-bearing-15x10x3,spline-xl330-horn,threaded-m2}/connection.json; ce-cad/cecad/data/materials.json (PLA and TPU property rows); research/kinematics-tables.txt (MJCF body/joint/mass tables).

GROUP TOTALS (out/print/slice.json, per robot, qty from docs/PARTS.md): PLA 46.2704 g / 2.3093 h across 2 shins + 2 ankles + 2 feet = 21.20 % of the robot's 218.29 g PLA and 23.24 % of its 9.93 h. TPU 14.1381 g / 1.3856 h across 2 soles = 53.96 % of the robot's 26.20 g TPU and 57.47 % of its 2.41 h. This group is one fifth of the printed mass and carries 100 % of the ground reaction.

FINDING A — THE ANKLE'S PRINT ORIENTATION IS WRONG AND IT IS THE LOWEST-MARGIN PART IN THE ROBOT. out/stress/report.json gives microduck-ankle-left SF 2.021 at 20 N — against shin 7.511 and hip-bracket 6.424. That SF is computed on the PLA row in ce-cad/cecad/data/materials.json, whose own source field says "fits.py's yield 50 MPa / modulus 3.5 GPa are ALONG-LAYER printed-part values" and whose notes say verbatim: "ANISOTROPIC. These are along-layer figures; across layers a printed part is bonded, not continuous, and typically well under half this. Orientation is not modelled anywhere in ce-cad." out/print/slice.json orients the ankle "auto-orient: bearing bore vertical", i.e. build Z along the part's X = the ankle axis = the exact bearing-wall -> 2.500 mm plate -> horn-wall load path the FEA loads. Every layer bond plane is normal to the primary load. 2.021 x (<0.5) => effective SF < 1.01. FIX: re-slice both ankles with the bore HORIZONTAL (part Z up, docs/DFM.md's "upright"), accept the bridged Ø15.000/Ø14.000 bores and ream. A reamed bore is minutes; a delaminated ankle is a fallen robot. The exact knockdown factor is CANNOT DETERMINE (nothing in this workshop has measured PLA Z-strength) — that is precisely why the recipe must not rely on it.

FINDING B — CRITICAL FINDING #4 IS MIS-STATED IN THE REPO AND MUST BE CORRECTED. ankle_l_v1 / ankle_r_v1 are NOT "two ankle revisions". research/kinematics-tables.txt:47,58 shows both are LIVE BODIES in pollen-robotics_microduck_rl/.../robot_allcollisions_rollers.xml, each carrying geoms ['roller_blade','seeed_bearing__configuration_default','ankle_*_v1'] plus two 'tire'/'rim' children on passive_LF/LR (and RF/RR) wheel hinges, with the left_foot/right_foot MJCF sites moved onto them and NO foot_* / sole_* geom at all. docs/PARTS.md §4 files them correctly as the ROLLER ACCESSORY, sold as "2 x Rollers" in the Accessory Pack (€33 / $39), driven by policy.mode="roller" (roller.onnx). ce-parts/microduck-ankle-left/component.json's why_this_folder_exists says they are "an OLDER variant ... that no MJCF body references" — that sentence is FALSE and is the origin of the "two revisions" framing. They are a mutually-exclusive variant SKU: fitting one replaces the ankle AND the foot AND the sole. Correct component.json.

FINDING C — MESH TRUST. All nine meshes are Pollen's DECIMATED visual assets (onshape-to-robot config simplify_stls:true, max_stl_size 1.0 MB — research/02-repos-and-code.md:85). Seven of the nine were recovered by parametric rebuild and graded by cad-refcheck; ranked by p95 ref->ours / max: ankle_left 0.0117/0.0807, ankle_right 0.0119/0.0807, sole_left 0.0520/0.3648, sole_right 0.0521/0.3398, foot_right 0.3693/2.4587, foot_left 0.4497/2.4280, shin 1.0000/2.8484. THE SHIN PASSES ONLY BECAUSE ITS p95 LANDS EXACTLY ON THE 1.00 mm TOLERANCE (out/refcheck/microduck-shin/r4/compare.json; r1-r3 all FAIL), with a 2.8484 mm maximum deviation — two orders of magnitude looser than the ankles. Its bbox is exact (delta 0.0000 mm, out/verify/mech_dims.json) but its SHAPE is the weakest match in the group. ankle_l_v1/ankle_r_v1 have no folder, no part.py, no refcheck, no FEA, no slice, no wall measurement — only a bbox and a mirror test: DO NOT TRUST for tooling. Separately: out/photomatch/ contains head views only (mesh_head_*.png, mesh_headonly_*.png, one mesh_STAND_left.png), so the mesh-vs-photograph check that FAILED on top_head_shell HAS NOT BEEN RUN on any part in this group. That check is an open work item, not a pass.

FINDING D — THE FOOT/SOLE SOCKET HAS ZERO NOMINAL CLEARANCE. Foot lower body x 31.600..68.400 / y -9.900..39.900 equals the sole cavity x 31.600..68.400 / y -9.900..39.900 to 0.000 mm on both axes (foot part.py LB_X0/LB_X1/LB_Y0/LB_Y1 vs sole part.py CAV_X0/CAV_X1/CAV_Y0/CAV_Y1, both read off the meshes; rib bottoms = sole outer floor + 2.000 mm at 5 stations, max deviation 0.005 mm). Both meshes agree to 0.005 mm, so this is Pollen's CAD intent, not decimation noise. But 0.000 mm is not a tolerance, and on FDM the extrusion width and elephant's foot both add material on both halves. RESOLUTION (executable, do not escalate): put the clearance on the RIGID half — cut the foot's lower body to x 31.750..68.250 / y -9.750..39.750 (0.150 mm per side), leave the TPU sole at nominal, and write the fit on both drawings. Then print one pair and measure the seating force and whether the rib bottoms actually land on the cavity floor (they must, or the ground load runs through the 1.594-2.142 mm side walls instead of the 2.000 mm floor).

FINDING E — TWO REPO LEDGERS DISAGREE ON PRINT ORIENTATION AND ONE IS STALE. docs/DFM.md (measured with cecad.printed.printability against a prusa_mk4 bed) says the shin prints "upright, Z-up (58 mm tall)" with "15 holes all on X (horizontal) Ø2.2-6.0 bridge". out/print/slice.json (the later, actually-sliced job on the Bambu H2S) uses "8 mm plate flat, rim walls up", which puts all 15 holes VERTICAL (they print round, no bridging) and the 42.000 mm knee->ankle load path IN the build plane. slice.json is right for the shin and DFM.md's shin row is stale. The opposite is true for the ankle (Finding A). Reconcile the two files before anyone prints from either.

FINDING F — NO FEA EXISTS FOR THE FOOT OR THE SOLE. out/stress/report.json has exactly four entries: shin (PASS 7.511), upper-leg-left (CANNOT DETERMINE, gmsh "Invalid boundary mesh (overlapping facets) on surface 350"), ankle-left (PASS 2.021), hip-bracket (PASS 6.424). The foot cap is unanalysed. The sole CANNOT be analysed and ce-cad refuses to pretend otherwise — materials.py's TPU note says verbatim "AND THE FEA IS STILL NOT VALID HERE. 500% elongation means the useful range of a TPU part is enormous strain; linear small-strain elasticity describes the first fraction of a percent of that and nothing beyond." Also unmodelled anywhere: PLA CREEP ("PLA CREEPS under sustained load at ROOM temperature ... Nothing in this repo models creep") — a 737 g robot standing still for a month is exactly that load case, on the ankle at SF 2.02.

FINDING G — MATERIAL SPECS ARE NOT PURCHASABLE. PLA: no grade, no spool, no MPN (materials.json "NO GRADE, NO SPOOL"); the class figures used are 50 MPa / 3.5 GPa / nu 0.36. TPU: "NO GRADE, NO SPOOL, NO SHORE HARDNESS"; docs/PARTS.md row 79 and SPEC §6 mark TPU as INFERRED (community 90-95A, [R2 §1c]) while out/print/slice.json's own flag records that the parts were actually sliced at Bambu TPU 85A. 85A vs 95A moves the modulus by more than an order of magnitude and the sole is the ONLY thing that touches the ground (MJCF left_foot_collision / right_foot_collision, condim 3, friction 1.000 — microduck_constants.py:133-138 via docs/PARTS.md). Nothing in this group can be ordered until a grade and a durometer are named. No sourced filament price exists in the repo (docs/BOM.md:150 "Maybe 500 g €20" is an estimate, not a quote), so per-part material cost is CANNOT DETERMINE.

FINDING H — FASTENING IS UNPROVEN AT ITS WEAKEST POINT. The foot hangs off the ankle on ONE M2 self-tapped into a Ø1.600 x 5.500 blind pilot in PLA (foot part.py PILOT_D/PILOT_Z0/PILOT_Z1; ankle SCREW_D Ø2.200 at (50.000, 4.502) — same axis to the micron). ce-connections/threaded-m2 records "pull-out of an M2 formed thread in a printed Ø1.6 pilot" as CANNOT DETERMINE. docs/BOM.md:116 lists 60 M2 heat-set inserts with the insert-vs-tapped decision open; PRODUCTION.md §2.1 already sources them (Prusa / CNC Kitchen / Vector3D, $0.12 / €0.099 / £0.097, in stock). RECOMMENDATION: specify a heat-set insert here. It is the single cheapest reliability fix in the group.

TOLERANCE BASIS, stated once for the whole group. No as-printed FDM feature carries an ISO 286 class and the repo says so: ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-15x10x3 — "the reference design's actual seats are FDM PLA and carry no class, which is why the folder's fit verdict on those pairs is per-measurement, not per-class." Therefore: (a) general envelope ISO 2768-m for PLA parts, ISO 2768-c for the TPU sole; (b) any fit-critical bore gets an ISO class only AFTER a post-process — Ø15.000 H7 (+0.018 / 0) for the ankle bearing pocket, reamed; the published IT7 at the 10-18 mm step is 18 um where the ISO 286-1 formula (i = 0.45*cbrt(D) + 0.001*D, D = sqrt(10*18) = 13.4164, i = 1.0827 um, 16i = 17.32 um) gives 17.32, and the repo transcribes rather than derives it (compat.PUBLISHED_IT7_UM); (c) the horn interface is Ø12.001 PCD (= the 8.486 mm square's diagonal) +/-0.10 mm, per ce-connections/spline-xl330-horn; (d) every M2 tapped/pilot hole is drill-and-form-tap after printing, per docs/DFM.md's recurring-risk block.

MOULDING (1,000 units). docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.2 already names the ankles and feet among the 9 visible parts to mould at 1,000 units "after a DFM redesign", keeping the 22 small grey brackets FDM, and states the obstacle in its own words: "a moulded version needs draft, uniform walls and side-actions for the bearing bores and M2 counterbores" (tooling $13,455 Protolabs floor to $90,000 aluminium => $13-90/robot, + $4.50-45 parts). Measured today: the ankle's two outer faces ALREADY carry usable draft about +z (6.474 deg bearing wall, 7.129 deg horn wall) and the foot's flange sides carry 6.470 deg and its snap faces 6.334 deg; the sole's outer heel carries 6.051 deg. Everything else in this group is 0 deg — including the sole's entire 12.907 mm-deep cavity, whose walls the probes read as vertical at every z. That zero-draft TPU core is the hardest single obstacle to the mould route in this group.

RECOMMENDED ACTIONS, in priority order: 1) re-slice both ankles bore-horizontal and re-verify (Finding A); 2) correct ce-parts/microduck-ankle-left/component.json's roller-variant sentence and stop calling ankle_*_v1 a revision (Finding B); 3) put 0.150 mm/side on the foot's lower body and write the fit on both drawings (Finding D); 4) reconcile docs/DFM.md against out/print/slice.json (Finding E); 5) name a PLA grade and a TPU durometer before any order (Finding G); 6) specify M2 heat-set inserts at the foot (Finding H); 7) re-slice foot_left/right and both ankles WITH SUPPORTS ENABLED — slice.json's own flag says "the 0.20mm Standard preset slices without supports, production plates should enable them", so the four support-warned parts' grams and hours in this group are floors, not production numbers; 8) run FEA on the foot cap; 9) run a photomatch on the lower leg before any tooling.

CNC/SLA unnecessary; injection only at the 1,000-unit tier and docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.2 keeps this size of grey bracket printed (17 mm parts break even at ~2,000 units [XM1]).
parts.dims_mm: 7.9500 x 20.0000 x 58.0000 (X thickness x Y width x Z length, Pollen mesh frame; x 32.500..40.450, y 12.000..32.000, z -12.223..45.777). out/verify/mech_dims.json: ref 7.95 / 20.0 / 58.0, our rebuild identical, delta 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.0000 mm, max_delta 0.0000 mm, dim_verdict PASS — the ONLY part in this group with a bbox-verified parametric rebuild.
parts.function: The single plate of each shin (MJCF body `leg`, placed once per side as a visual geom plus a self-collision copy — docs/PARTS.md:50-55 corrects the x4 double count; component.json still says qty_per_robot 4, open item #1). It carries the ankle XL330 servo, takes the knee horn at the top and hands the load to the ankle bearing at the bottom. Knee axis to ankle axis = 42.000 mm exactly (Z_KNEE 35.777 to Z_ANKLE -6.223). MJCF body mass 21.5844 g including its servo (research/kinematics-tables.txt, robot_walk.xml).
parts.material: PLA (ce-parts/microduck-shin/component.json). Class properties only: yield 50 MPa, E 3.5 GPa, nu 0.36 (ce-cad/cecad/data/materials.json) — 'NO GRADE, NO SPOOL'. Recommendation: keep PLA. It is the correct choice here because the sliced orientation puts the whole 42.000 mm load path in the build plane, so the along-layer figures the FEA used actually apply, and SF 7.511 leaves room for the grade variance. PETG or ASA would only be needed if the 55 degC PLA glass transition became a use case.
parts.tolerance_class: ISO 2768-m general envelope. Controlled separately: 42.000 +/-0.10 mm knee-ankle axis pitch; Ø10.000 bearing boss and Ø2.700 through-hole concentric to the ankle axis within 0.05 mm; horn pattern Ø12.001 PCD +/-0.10 mm (ce-connections/spline-xl330-horn: 8.486 x sqrt(2) = 12.001, the two spellings agree to 0.001 mm). No as-printed FDM feature carries an ISO 286 class.
critical_features: Knee-to-ankle axis pitch 42.000 mm — the shin length in SPEC.md §3 and the single dimension that sets the gait; MJCF shank vector |(0, 0.042, -0.026)| = 49.4 mm (research/02-repos-and-code.md:152)
Ø10.000 x 3.2 bearing boss on the back face (X_BOSS_BACK 32.500 to X_BACK_PLATE 35.700) — the INNER-ring seat of the 15x10x3 ankle bearing (ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-15x10x3)
XL330 horn interface at the knee: Ø15.900 disc, Ø6.000 centre bore, 4 x Ø2.200 on an 8.486 mm square (= Ø12.001 PCD), Ø4.400 x 4.500 counterbores from the back
Ankle end: Ø10.000 ring standing 0.500 proud with a Ø8.000 x 0.500 recess, Ø4.920 x 2.300 locating pin, Ø2.700 through + Ø5.500 x 3.500 counterbore
Central slot 5.000 wide x 11.500 long, R1.500 corners, z 15.000..26.500 — reduces mid-span section, already inside the FEA
Two side holes Ø2.400 at z 16.277, y 14.000 / 30.000, counterbored Ø4.840 back to x 36.200
Four 1.000 mm rim walls at y 13.500 / 17.500 / 25.500 / 29.500 — the thinnest true wall on the part
Central rib 12.400 wide x 2.500 deep behind the 2.300 plate over z 5.000..41.500
dfm_issues: ANISOTROPY — RESOLVED CORRECTLY BY THE SLICED ORIENTATION, and this is worth protecting. out/print/slice.json orients it '8 mm plate flat, rim walls up' = build Z along part X. The 42.000 mm knee->ankle load path then lies IN the build plane, so the FEA's along-layer PLA figures apply and SF 7.511 stands. Do not let anyone 'improve' this to a vertical print.

STALE LEDGER: docs/DFM.md's shin row says 'upright, Z-up (58 mm tall)' with '15 holes all on X (horizontal) Ø2.2-6.0 bridge; tall thin section 8x20x58'. In the sliced orientation those 15 holes are VERTICAL and print round with no bridging. DFM.md's shin row is superseded by slice.json (2026-09-02) and must be corrected before anyone prints from it.

SHAPE FIDELITY IS THE WEAKEST IN THE GROUP. out/refcheck/microduck-shin/r4/compare.json: p95 1.0000 mm ref->ours and 1.0000 mm ours->ref against a 1.00 mm tolerance — exactly on the ceiling — with max deviation 2.8484 mm; r1 (2.12/2.67), r2 (1.33/1.33) and r3 (1.0108/1.0989) all FAIL. Compare ankle_left at 0.0117 mm. The bbox is perfect; the surface is not. Before tooling, find where the 2.8484 mm sits (component.json says 20/20 holes and bosses matched, so it is on a face, not a feature).

THIN WALL, NO MARGIN: the four 1.000 mm rim walls are 2.5 perimeters at a 0.4 mm nozzle. docs/DFM.md's two-perimeter floor is 0.800 mm, so there is 0.200 mm of margin and nothing more. The 0.028 mm 'thinnest wall' in DFM.md is a knife-edge (a tapered face reaching a tangent line), NOT a wall — DFM.md says so explicitly and the slicer rounds it off.

BEARING SEAT ENGAGEMENT: the Ø10.000 boss is 3.2 mm long carrying a 3.000 mm-wide inner ring. Interference is CANNOT DETERMINE — ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-15x10x3 refuses it by name because a printed PLA seat has no ISO class and the unnamed ring has no vendor tolerance sheet. Measure the as-printed boss with calipers and dress it; do not assume Ø10.000.

NO TRAPPED VOLUME, NO UNDERCUT for the print. For a mould: the rib, the 0.500 proud ring, the recess and the four rim walls all sit on one side and would pull along +/-x, but the Ø4.400 back counterbores and the Ø4.840 side counterbores are opposed to the front features — a two-plate tool cannot make both. Needs a redesign or two side-actions, exactly as docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.2 anticipates.
SLENDERNESS is a non-issue in the sliced orientation (7.95 mm tall on a 20 x 58 footprint) — another reason to keep it. In DFM.md's assumed upright it was a 58 mm-tall 8 mm blade needing a brim.
Small holes print undersize: Ø2.200 clearance and Ø2.400 side holes both close in on FDM. Drill to size after printing (docs/DFM.md recurring-risk block).

parts.part: ankle_left (slug microduck-ankle-left) — left ankle U-bracket, qty 1
parts.process: FDM print, PLA. Sliced 6.1845 g / 1316.99 s (0.3658 h), slicer_warning 'floating regions - enable supports' (out/print/slice.json) — so both the grams and the time are floors, not production numbers. docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.2 puts the ankles in the 9-part mould set at 1,000 units, after a DFM redesign.
parts.dims_mm: 39.4891 x 36.5000 x 25.5000 (x 30.364..69.854, y 0.163..36.663, z -22.523..2.977, Pollen mesh frame; X runs ACROSS the bracket between its walls, Y is width, Z is up). out/verify/mech_dims.json ref row, 4978 tris, rebuilt:false in that file. The parametric rebuild is graded elsewhere: out/refcheck/microduck-ankle-left/r3/compare.json PASS, p95 0.0117 / 0.0115 mm, max 0.0807 mm, bbox delta [0.001, -0.000, 0.000] mm, 13/13 holes matched — the best shape match in the group. Solid volume 7877.8 mm3 (out/measure/ankle/mirror-test.json). MJCF body mass 30.0246 g including sole, foot and bearing.
parts.function: The U-bracket that straddles the shin/ankle-servo stack and carries the entire robot to the ground. One wall holds the 15x10x3 bearing (idler side of the ankle hinge), the other bolts to the XL330 horn; a 2.500 mm plate joins them; an R16.300 under-hull about the ankle axis is the heel the foot cap cradles. MJCF joint left_ankle, hinge, range -90 to +90 deg.
parts.material: PLA (component.json). RECOMMENDATION: change to PETG or ASA, or keep PLA only with the orientation fix below. Reasoning, all sourced: this is the lowest-SF structural part in the robot (2.021 vs shin 7.511, hip-bracket 6.424 — out/stress/report.json); the PLA row in ce-cad/cecad/data/materials.json warns that PLA 'CREEPS under sustained load at ROOM temperature' and that 55 degC 'is the number that kills PLA parts in the real world'; and a standing robot is exactly a sustained load on this bracket. PETG's tougher layer bond directly attacks the anisotropy problem below. The specific grade for either is CANNOT DETERMINE — no spool is named anywhere in this repo.
parts.tolerance_class: ISO 2768-m general envelope. Fit-critical, AFTER post-processing only: bearing pocket Ø15.000 H7 (+0.018 / 0, ISO 286 10-18 mm step; the repo transcribes 18 um rather than deriving 17.32 um from 16i — ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-15x10x3 compat.PUBLISHED_IT7_UM), reamed. Horn pattern Ø12.001 PCD +/-0.10 mm on R6.000 (ce-connections/spline-xl330-horn). Hull R16.300 concentric to the ankle axis within 0.10 mm (it is the mating surface for the foot's cradle). No as-printed FDM feature carries an ISO 286 class.
critical_features: Ankle axis at (y 22.000, z -6.223) — the single datum; every bore, the R16.300 hull and both wall arcs are concentric to it, and the shin's bearing boss sits on the same line
Bearing pocket Ø15.000 x 2.300 deep (x 32.500..34.800) with a 0.500 x 45 deg lead-in opening to Ø16.000 at the inner face x 35.300, behind a Ø14.000 window from outside — the outer-ring seat
Horn interface: Ø5.000 centre bore + 4 x Ø2.200 on an R6.000 diamond at (22,-12.223), (22,-0.223), (28,-6.223), (16,-6.223), with Ø4.400 counterbores from x 66.500 outward
Connecting plate 2.500 mm thick (z -15.842..-13.342) — the whole ankle torque passes through it
Under-hull R16.300, x 33.000..67.000, bottom z -22.523 — mates the foot cap's R16.300 cradle at 0.000 nominal clearance
Vertical foot screw Ø2.200 at (50.000, 4.502) with Ø4.400 x 1.000 counterbore — same axis to the micron as the foot's Ø1.600 pilot
Two +y blocks 5.000 x 4.000 x 5.500 at x 34.100..39.100 / 60.900..65.900 (y 31.663..35.663, down to z -21.342) — locate in the foot's 5.200 x 4.200 pockets at 0.100 mm total clearance
Two roofed slots 2.000 x 1.000 inside those blocks, roof from (34.163, -17.07) to (33.163, -18.10)
Two edge notches 1.400 deep x 12.000 long (x 44.000..56.000, floor z -14.640)
dfm_issues: ANISOTROPY VS THE LOAD DIRECTION — THIS IS WHY THE PART FAILS. out/print/slice.json orients it 'auto-orient: bearing bore vertical', putting build Z along part X = the ankle axis = the bearing-wall -> plate -> horn-wall load path the FEA loads (fixed bearing_seat, loaded horn_face). Every layer bond plane is normal to the primary load. The FEA's SF 2.021 is computed on ALONG-LAYER PLA (materials.json: yield 50 MPa, E 3.5 GPa, nu 0.36) whose own note reads 'across layers a printed part is bonded, not continuous, and typically well under half this. Orientation is not modelled anywhere in ce-cad.' 2.021 x (<0.5) => effective SF < 1.01 on the lowest-margin part in the robot. FIX: re-slice with the bore HORIZONTAL (part Z vertical), accept the bridged Ø15.000/Ø14.000 and ream them.

BEARING RETENTION WEB IS 1.044 mm THICK. The outer face is an inclined plane x = 32.1622 + 0.11348z (fit residual 0.0000, out/measure/ankle/fits_ankle_left.txt), so at the axis z = -6.223 the outer face sits at x 31.456 and the Ø15.000 pocket floor at x 32.500 — 1.044 mm of PLA, i.e. 5 layers at 0.20 mm, pierced by the Ø14.000 window. The retaining lip is a 0.500 mm radial annulus. That thin ring is all that stops the bearing walking out under side load.

PARTIAL BEARING ENGAGEMENT, DELIBERATE BUT UNPROVEN: pocket 2.300 mm deep for a 3.000 mm ring = 76.7 %. ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-15x10x3 records this as Pollen's own design ('the proud 0.7 mm clears the shin boss') and refuses both verdicts: 'whether 77% engagement holds the press is a bench question'. Interference is likewise CANNOT DETERMINE — no ISO class on a printed seat, no vendor sheet on the unnamed ring.

HORN CLAMP PATH IS 1.800 mm. The Ø4.400 counterbores start at x 66.500 and the horn face is at x 64.700, so the four M2 heads bear on 1.800 mm of PLA — and that clamp is what transmits the ankle torque. Outboard of the counterbore at the axis there is 2.151 mm (outer face x = 67.8723 - 0.12507z gives 68.651 at z -6.223).
FOOT SCREW LEAVES 1.500 mm: Ø2.200 through a 2.500 mm plate with a Ø4.400 x 1.000 counterbore from the top.

BRIDGING, IF RE-ORIENTED AS RECOMMENDED: the Ø15.000 / Ø14.000 bores and the 4 x Ø2.200 horn holes then lie on a horizontal axis. docs/DFM.md is right about the consequence — 'a bridged Ø15 comes out oval and undersize' — so REAM the pocket to Ø15.000 H7 and drill the Ø2.200. This is the accepted cost of fixing the anisotropy.

TRAPPED VOLUME: none. The U is open on both faces and the channel between the walls is cut clear to the plate bottom with a 52 deg chamfer (CH_Y_TOP 10.178..33.822 at z -13.342 narrowing to CH_Y_BOT 12.105..31.895 at z -15.842).

UNDERCUTS PREVENTING TOOL RELEASE (mould route): (a) the Ø15.000 pocket sitting BEHIND a Ø14.000 window is a classic undercut — no straight pull makes it; (b) the two roofed slots in the +y blocks; (c) the Ø4.400 horn counterbores oppose the bearing pocket across the part. docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.2 already names the requirement: 'side-actions for the bearing bores and M2 counterbores'. Expect two side-actions plus a lifter, on top of a redesign.

DRAFT, PARTIAL: the two outer faces already carry usable taper about +z — bearing wall 0.11348 mm/mm = 6.474 deg, horn wall 0.12507 mm/mm = 7.129 deg, both converging upward so a +z cavity pull works. Every other face — channel walls, blocks, slot flanks, plate faces, notches — is 0 deg and needs draft added.

dfm_issues: ZERO-CLEARANCE SOCKET, AND IT IS THE PART'S DEFINING FIT. The foot's lower body x 31.600..68.400 / y -9.900..39.900 equals the sole cavity to 0.000 mm on both axes (foot part.py LB_* vs sole part.py CAV_*, both read off the meshes; the two agree to 0.005 mm so it is CAD intent, not decimation). 0.000 mm is not a manufacturable specification: extrusion width and elephant's foot both add material on both halves. RESOLUTION: cut the foot's lower body to x 31.750..68.250 / y -9.750..39.750 (0.150 mm per side, clearance owned by the rigid PLA half), leave the TPU sole at nominal, and print one pair to measure the seating force and confirm the rib bottoms reach the cavity floor. Until that measurement exists this part cannot be graded PASS.

ONE M2 SELF-TAPPED INTO PLA IS THE ONLY FASTENER. Ø1.600 x 5.500 blind pilot, thread-formed. ce-connections/threaded-m2 records 'pull-out of an M2 formed thread in a printed Ø1.6 pilot' as CANNOT DETERMINE and docs/DFM.md's recurring-risk block says these holes 'print undersize on any FDM machine ... heat-set inserts preferred for M2 into PLA.' Specify a heat-set insert: docs/BOM.md:116 already carries 60 of them as an open decision and docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.1 has them sourced at $0.12 / €0.099 / £0.097 (Prusa / CNC Kitchen / Vector3D, in stock).

SNAP FINGERS ARE THIN, CANTILEVERED AND MOVING — the same feature class docs/DFM.md calls 'the single most fragile feature on the part' for power-support: 'FDM layer lines run across the flex axis; the tongue is a fatigue/delamination risk ... expect it to be the first thing that breaks.' Here there are two, 10.000 mm wide, with 1.000 mm barbs, drafted 0.111 mm/mm (6.334 deg). In the sliced 'sole face down' orientation their flex axis is across the layers.

RIB SLENDERNESS AND SUPPORT: the ribs are 1.750 mm thick and reach 10.854 mm tall at y = 10 (top z -17.236 at R16.300 from the axis, bottom z -28.090) — a 6.20:1 aspect; 6.517 mm (3.72:1) at y = 16 in the R16.500 relief band; 5.819 mm (3.33:1) at y = 22. The 1.750 mm gaps between them are deep, narrow pockets. slicer_warning 'floating regions - enable supports' fires here, and slice.json's own flag states the 0.20mm Standard preset sliced WITHOUT supports and 'production plates should enable them'. THE 13.3514 g / 0.5481 h FIGURES ARE THEREFORE FLOORS, NOT PRODUCTION NUMBERS.

PRINT ORIENTATION IS UNRESOLVED. 'sole face down, toes up' rests the part on a comb whose bottoms follow the sole's floor, which itself slopes 0.08697 mm/mm (4.971 deg) heel-to-toe — so first-layer contact is a growing footprint along a curve, not a plane. The alternatives (flange down, or on its side) each trade the rib supports for support inside the pockets or on the cradle. Re-slice all three with supports enabled and pick on measured time and surface, not on the auto-orienter.

TRAPPED VOLUME: none by design — the comb is open downward and the sole closes it. That is the intent, but it also means any support material left in the comb prevents the sole from seating. Note it on the drawing.

UNDERCUTS PREVENTING TOOL RELEASE (mould route): the two snap barbs, the two roofed pockets, the R16.500 relief cut UNDER the R16.300 cradle, and the through pockets are all undercuts. A tool needs a core-pull for the comb plus lifters for the barbs. docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.2's 'after a DFM redesign' is doing real work in that sentence.
DRAFT, PARTIAL: flange sides 6.470 deg, snap faces 6.334 deg — already usable. The rib flanks, the ledges, the pockets and the boss are all 0 deg.

NO FEA EXISTS FOR THIS PART. out/stress/report.json has four entries (shin, upper-leg-left, ankle-left, hip-bracket) and the foot is not among them. Everything above about its load path is geometric reasoning, not a solved model.

SHAPE FIDELITY IS MID-PACK: p95 0.4497 mm but max 2.4280 mm — the rebuild departs from Pollen's mesh by up to 2.428 mm somewhere. Locate it before tooling; the two holes matched, so it is on a face or a rib tip.
TAPPED HOLE PRINTS UNDERSIZE: docs/DFM.md — 'drill to tapping size and form-tap after printing'.

dfm_issues: DUROMETER IS UNSPECIFIED AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL UNKNOWN IN THE GROUP. 85A (as sliced) versus 95A (as inferred) moves the modulus by more than an order of magnitude (materials.json TPU note). The walking policy, the sim's friction 1.000, the wear rate and the assembly force over the foot cap all sit on this number. Nothing can be ordered until a grade and a durometer are named.

FEA IS NOT AVAILABLE AND MUST NOT BE FAKED. materials.py's TPU note, verbatim: 'AND THE FEA IS STILL NOT VALID HERE. 500% elongation means the useful range of a TPU part is enormous strain; linear small-strain elasticity describes the first fraction of a percent of that and nothing beyond. A TPU result from stress.py is a lower bound on stiffness at the origin of the curve, not a prediction.' It also records that stress.py assumed nu = 0.30 for every material where an elastomer needs 0.48. Correctly, out/stress/report.json contains no sole entry. Structural confidence here comes from a bench test or from nowhere.

THE GROUND FACE IS THE FIRST LAYER, AND ITS FINISH IS AN UNCONTROLLED PROCESS VARIABLE. Printed 'sole tread face down, dead flat', the surface that touches the world is whatever the build plate imprints on it — smooth PEI and textured PEI give materially different friction, and there is no tread pattern anywhere on the part to fall back on (the ground face is a smooth blended plane; friction comes from the material alone). SPECIFY THE BUILD PLATE TEXTURE ON THE DRAWING. It is the tread.
ELEPHANT'S FOOT LANDS EXACTLY ON THE CONTACT FACE and will round the R7.204 heel and R6.884 toe arcs that set how the foot rolls. On TPU at 0.20 mm this is not a rounding error.

ZERO-CLEARANCE CAVITY (the other half of Finding D): x 31.600..68.400 / y -9.900..39.900 equals the foot cap's lower body to 0.000 mm. The TPU is the compliant half so it can absorb the interference, but one drawing must own the number. Recommendation: leave the sole at nominal and take the 0.150 mm/side out of the PLA foot.

ZERO DRAFT ON THE CAVITY — the blocking issue for the mould route. The probes read the cavity walls as vertical at every z through a 12.907 mm depth (sole part.py: 'cavity: vertical walls'). A zero-draft core that deep in TPU will not release cleanly; it needs >= 1 deg per side. The OUTER faces are already drafted (heel 6.051 deg) so only the core is the problem. Otherwise the part is mould-friendly: no undercut, no trapped volume, a straight +z core pull.

SLOPED GROUND FACE vs 'dead flat' ON THE BED: the ground plane rises 0.08697 mm/mm, i.e. 3.574 mm across the 41.099 mm length. Either the part is tipped to bring that plane parallel to the bed (and the rim is then not level) or the first layer is a growing footprint. The slicer raised no warning, so it accepted the arrangement — but the geometry says someone should look at the plate before a production run.

WEAR IS UNSPECIFIED. This is the only wearing part on the robot and there is no wear allowance, no tread, no replacement interval and no spare-part line in docs/BOM.md. At 2.000 mm of floor the whole wear budget is 2.000 mm. Product-level open item.

TPU IS 54 % OF THE ROBOT'S SOFT-MATERIAL BUDGET IN THIS ONE PAIR: 14.1381 g of 26.20 g and 1.3856 h of 2.41 h (out/print/slice.json totals). TPU prints slowly; the two soles alone take longer than the two feet and two ankles combined.
CANNOT BE MACHINED — materials.json: 'it deflects away from the tool. It is printed or moulded.' CNC and SLA are both off the table for this part.

PAIR CONSISTENCY IS A REQUIREMENT, NOT A NICETY: same spool, same durometer, same build plate texture, same orientation. The soles are the robot's only contact with the world; any asymmetry between them shows up directly in the gait.

results.notes:
DFM REVIEW — GROUP "HIP & UPPER LEG" — 2026-09-02. 8 named entries resolve to 6 real parts, 10 pieces per robot.

SOURCES READ (all paths absolute-rooted at /Users/leifrydenfalk/dev/ce-workshop/ce-designs/microduck):
out/verify/mech_dims.json + out/verify/mech.log (dimensional truth, generated 2026-09-02 21:05) · out/stress/report.json · out/print/PRINT.md + out/print/stl_manifest.json (ce-slice 0.1.0 / BambuStudio 02.08.02.61, Bambu H2S, 0.4 nozzle, 0.20 mm Standard, PLA Basic 1.26 g/cm3) · docs/DFM.md · docs/PARTS.md · docs/BOM.md · docs/PRODUCTION.md · docs/MANUFACTURING-REQUIREMENTS.md · SPEC.md · out/drawings/*/result.json + the six SVG sheets · out/refcheck/*.log · ce-parts/microduck-{yaw2roll,bearing-roll,hip-bracket,upper-leg-left,upper-leg-right,upper-leg-rigidity-plate}/iterations/v0.0.1/{cad/part.py,cad/interfaces.json,trust.json,component.json} · ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4/{connection.json,iterations/v0.0.1/{compat.py,evidence/bearing-22x16x4-geometry.json}} · reference/pollen-microduck-rl/{kin_robot_walk.xml,robot_walk.xml,stl_list.txt,assets/*.stl} · /Users/leifrydenfalk/dev/ce-workshop/ce-cad/cecad/data/materials.json + cecad/fits.py.

MEASUREMENTS I MADE IN THIS SESSION (not read from a file):
1. md5 + welded-vertex comparison of the four thigh assets. left_upper_leg.stl is BYTE-IDENTICAL to upper_leg_left.stl (md5 6554f2eeba9e3045d99ba7e457371303). right_upper_leg.stl has a different md5 (a07aa504…) from upper_leg_right.stl (5db2f669…) but an IDENTICAL vertex set and bbox — 12250 tris, 6123 unique vertices, x -70.5000..-42.5000, y -13.4674..34.1920, z -12.1975..48.7992 — i.e. the same solid with the triangles reordered. And upper_leg_right is the exact x-mirror of upper_leg_left: all 6123 vertices coincide at 0.000000 mm both ways. CONCLUSION: left_upper_leg / right_upper_leg are duplicate asset names from the mjlab RL package (reference/pollen-microduck-rl/stl_list.txt) for the same two thighs the visual MJCF calls upper_leg_left / upper_leg_right. Two parts, not four. No extra BOM line, no extra print, no extra tool.
2. Mesh integrity of the six release STLs in out/print/stl/PLA/. ALL SIX are closed 2-manifold: every edge used exactly twice, 0 degenerate triangles, 0 duplicate triangles (upper-leg L/R 22172 tris / 33258 edges; yaw2roll 10618/15927; bearing-roll 5956/8934; hip-bracket 20970/31455; rigidity-plate 3600/5400). The upper-leg FEA CANNOT DETERMINE is therefore a gmsh failure on the CAD surface tessellation ("Invalid boundary mesh (overlapping facets) on surface 350"), NOT a bad print file.
3. Ligament arithmetic off each part.py's own measured constants, and a numeric polygon-distance scan of the rigidity plate. Every one of my computed minima independently reproduces the cecad.printed thinnest-wall figure in docs/DFM.md, which is the cross-check that they are real: hip-bracket 0.800 (docs 0.80), bearing-roll 0.900 (docs 0.900), rigidity plate 1.000 thick / 1.499 in-plane (drawing prints "1.49 WALL").

THREE PACK-LEVEL DEFECTS THAT BLOCK MANUFACTURE (these are the reason for the FAIL verdicts, not the geometry):

A. THE HIP-BRACKET DRAWING IS A DRAWING OF THE COLLAPSED r1 SOLID. out/drawings/microduck-hip-bracket/result.json records bbox [1.96, 16.0, 16.0], 5 holes, "verified": true, "verify_sheet": true; the sheet's own title block prints 1.96 x 16.00 x 16.00, 0.30 cm3, 0.4 g. The correct part is 32.450 x 34.500 x 19.000 mm, 22 holes, 4.53 cm3 (docs/BOM.md), 3.81 g (out/print/PRINT.md). Timeline: sheet written 02:33, the r2 fix refchecked 02:57 (out/refcheck/microduck-hip-bracket-r2.log, PASS p95 0.16/0.25 mm, 21/21 features, bbox delta 0.000), component.json rewritten 03:00. The sheet is 6.7 % of the part by volume (r1 volume ratio 0.067) and carries 5 of the 22 holes. Anyone cutting from it makes scrap. verify_sheet passed because it only asks "does the ink match the solid I was handed", not "is this the solid the shelf blessed".

B. TWO OF THE SIX RELEASE STLs ARE POLLEN'S CC BY-SA-NC VENDOR MESHES, NOT OUR REBUILDS. out/print/stl_manifest.json: microduck-hip-bracket src = reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/hip_l.stl, 20970 tris, "vendor mesh (Pollen reference asset, loaded as-is)"; microduck-upper-leg-rigidity-plate src = reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/upper_leg_rigidity_plate.stl, 3600 tris, same string. out/print/PRINT.md states the licence consequence in its own words: "22 parts are Pollen's vendor meshes as shelved (CC BY-SA-NC - fine to print, NOT licensed for sale)." SPEC.md §1 confirms the sim assets are CC BY-SA-NC and that "mechanical CAD, BOM, PCBs: not published". So the two pieces the pack would actually print for this group are licence-blocked for a product, and both parts HAVE a passing rebuild sitting unused (hip-bracket r2; rigidity-plate r3).

C. THE RIGIDITY PLATE EXISTS IN THREE DIFFERENT SIZES ACROSS THREE RELEASED RECORDS. out/verify/mech_dims.json — the file this review is told is dimensional truth, regenerated 2026-09-02 21:05 — records our rebuild at 1.0000 x 45.5000 x 58.7770 mm, delta [0.0000, +0.5035, +0.7193] vs the reference, verdict PASS. The part's own evidence (out/refcheck/plate_r3.log and plate_ev.log, 02:48) records 1.000 x 44.999 x 58.060, delta [0.0, 0.003, 0.002], and component.json quotes exactly that. The released drawing (out/drawings/…/result.json, 02:21) prints 1.00 x 45.00 x 58.06. So the "truth" file is 0.7193 mm longer than the drawing and the ledger on a 58 mm part whose smallest structural ligament is 1.499 mm — the disagreement is 48.0 % of the critical ligament. Which build is current cannot be settled from the repo; it needs a fresh bin/cad build of part.py, a re-measure, and one number driving drawing + STL + mech_dims together. Related: mech_dims.json records hip_l as "rebuilt": false and counts "rebuilds: 9", so it silently omits the hip-bracket rebuild that does exist and does pass.

CROSS-CUTTING FINDINGS:

D. NO TOLERANCE BASIS EXISTS ANYWHERE. All six sheets carry the same honest note, verbatim: "2. GENERAL TOLERANCE: CANNOT DETERMINE - THIS PART DECLARES NO PROCESS THIS REPO CAN READ." Grepping the six SVGs for H7/H8/g6/h6/p6/ISO 2768/± returns zero hits besides that line. cecad/fits.py's own comment block records this as a known repo-wide failure ("grep it for H7, g6, p6, +-, ISO 2768 … and you get ZERO HITS"). Every tolerance class I give below is ASSIGNED BY THIS REVIEW as engineering judgement, not read from a source — except the ISO 286 fits, which are sourced: ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4/iterations/v0.0.1/compat.py derives and reproduces the published 16 k6 = +0.001/+0.012 mm and 16 h6 = -0.011/0.000 mm. The numeric bands of ISO 2768-m are CANNOT DETERMINE from this repo — the standard's table is not held here and must be taken from the issued standard before a sheet prints it.

E. THE BEARING SEAT IS THE GROUP'S HARDEST FIT AND IT IS UNRESOLVED THREE WAYS. The ring is measured (ce-connections/…/evidence/bearing-22x16x4-geometry.json, off seeed_bearing__configuration__22x16x4.stl): bore 16.000, OD 22.000, width 4.000 mm, 11 placements. The seats are Ø16.000 x 1.950 bosses (yaw2roll yaw_bearing_seat; hip-bracket roll_boss and pitch_boss). (i) ENGAGEMENT: 1.950 / 4.000 = 48.75 % — the ring is supported on under half its width and spans the joint gap onto the mating part. connection.json refuses both verdicts on this and calls it a bench question. (ii) FIT CLASS: a printed boss has no ISO 286 class; connection.json says so in terms. (iii) VENDOR: docs/PARTS.md row 33 and docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.1 both leave the MPN CANNOT DETERMINE (alias MR1622-ZZ / ET2216ZZ; "not a 6700-family size"), so the ring's own bore tolerance is unknown. Until the MPN is fixed, no interference can be computed — only the seat's produced diameter can be controlled.

F. MATERIAL — MOVE THE WHOLE GROUP OFF PLA. /Users/leifrydenfalk/dev/ce-workshop/ce-cad/cecad/data/materials.json is explicit that PLA is CLASS-TIER with no grade and no spool, and its $vocabulary.tiers rule is that "a check may FAIL on it … but may NOT PASS on it unless the caller explicitly accepts class-tier data". The out/stress/report.json PASSes (shin SF 7.51, ankle SF 2.02, hip-bracket SF 6.42) are all computed in PLA, so by the repo's own rule they are not verdict-grade. PLA's row also carries: max_service_c 55, elong 6 %, and the note "PLA CREEPS under sustained load at ROOM temperature. A static FEA says nothing about a bracket that has held 3 kg for a month." These six parts hold a standing 737.2 g robot (SPEC.md §2) for hours at a time. PETG is the only printed row in the file with confirmed: true and grade tier — Bambu PETG Basic, Bambu Filament TDS V3.0 (doc created 2026-01-26, retrieved 2026-08-19, PDF sha256-verified byte-identical to the store's): tensile X-Y 51 ± 1 MPa, Z 35 ± 6 MPa, tensile modulus 2780 MPa (fits.py carries 2.55 GPa), HDT ISO 75 at 1.8 MPa = 68 °C, breaking elongation Z 5.2 %, density 1.25 g/cm3. Recommendation: PETG for all six, and re-run the FEA matrix in PETG so a PASS can stand. Do NOT reach for PETG-CF or PA6-CF: materials.json records that plain PETG came out 1.67x stronger than PETG-CF by FEA on this repo's own parts, that PA6-CF at 4 % elongation is brittle by the file's own 5 % line, and that CF is abrasive.

G. ANISOTROPY, QUANTIFIED. The one sourced number in the repo is PETG Z 35 ± 6 MPa against X-Y 51 ± 1 MPa = 68.6 % of in-plane, and the file's note names Z as "the through-layer allowable and the direction a printed part lets go". Every part in this group is printed with its principal load path crossing layers somewhere (per part below). materials.json's PLA note is blunter: "across layers a printed part is bonded, not continuous, and typically well under half this. Orientation is not modelled anywhere in ce-cad." No FEA in out/stress/ models orientation. Treat every SF in out/stress/report.json as an in-plane number and divide by ~1.5 (PETG) before believing it in the layer-normal direction.

H. THE REFCHECK TOLERANCE IS NOT A MANUFACTURING TOLERANCE. cad-refcheck passes at p95 surface distance <= 1.00 mm. The thighs' walls are 1.000 mm and the rigidity plate is 1.000 mm thick. A 1 mm acceptance band on a 1 mm wall is 100 % of the feature. Six of the group pass far inside it (bearing-roll 0.002, yaw2roll 0.050, hip-bracket 0.162/0.242, thighs 0.200, plate r3 0.008) — but the standard itself does not qualify a part for tooling. Also: the reference is a DECIMATED VISUAL mesh, not CAD (SPEC.md §1: 38 decimated STLs), so every arc in it is a chord approximation and no radius in this group has a CAD-authored value.

I. UNMODELLED FILLETS ON THE THIGH, IN THE EXACT PLACES AN FDM PART CRACKS. out/refcheck/ul_r1.log: volume ratio ours/ref 0.9247. component.json names the cause verbatim: "the reference's sub-mm inner fillets (rim base, plate-to-wall) are not modelled". So the solid that will be printed is 7.5 % lighter than Pollen's, and the missing material is the fillet radius at the root of every 1.000 mm wall — the stress raiser that decides whether the thigh survives. Fix before tooling or a second FEA attempt.

J. PRINT-FARM LOAD FOR THIS GROUP (out/print/PRINT.md, slicer's own numbers): 10 pieces, 26.59 g PLA, 1 h 44 m 35 s of per-piece time = 12.18 % of the robot's 218.29 g and 17.55 % of its 9.93 h. Colours (SPEC.md §4 / docs/PARTS.md): yaw2roll #a5a5a5 grey, bearing_roll #43484d dark, hip_l #e6e6e6 light, thighs #dddddd, rigidity plate #89dad3 mint — FIVE filaments for ten pieces in one sub-assembly. Whether any of these five is visible on the finished robot is CANNOT DETERMINE from the repo; if they are internal, consolidating to one grey removes four AMS slots or four spool changes per plate.

K. MOULDING. docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.2 sources the break-even and it says keep this group printed: "17 mm parts break even at 2,000 units [XM1] so the brackets stay printed", and the 1,000-unit decision moulds only the 9 visible parts while "the 22 small grey brackets stay FDM". It also states the redesign cost honestly: "a moulded version needs draft, uniform walls and side-actions for the bearing bores … a redesign, not a re-quote [PL4]". One genuinely interesting measurement against that: THE THIGH ALREADY CARRIES DRAFT. part.py DRAFT = tan(3.0°) = 0.052408/mm, measured off the mesh by probe D/E as 1.252 mm of wall movement over 23.9 mm of depth, on both the side wall and the top flange, plus a 1.86° flange tilt. The locating pins and the bearing-roll pegs are conical at 2.8624° per side. That is the strongest evidence in the asset set that Pollen drew these parts expecting a mould, and it means the thigh is the one part in the group that would need the least work to tool.

RESOLUTION LIST, IN ORDER (all are work items, none is a question for anyone):
1. Rebuild part:microduck-hip-bracket through bin/cad and regenerate out/drawings/microduck-hip-bracket/* from the r2 solid; re-run verify_sheet; confirm the title block reads 32.45 x 34.50 x 19.00 and the hole table carries 22 holes.
2. Re-export out/print/stl/PLA/microduck-hip-bracket.stl and …-rigidity-plate.stl from our own refcheck ours.stl (as the other four already are) and update out/print/stl_manifest.json; re-slice. This clears the CC BY-SA-NC blocker for the group.
3. Rebuild part:microduck-upper-leg-rigidity-plate, re-run bin/verify mech, and make out/verify/mech_dims.json, the drawing and the STL agree on one length. Until they do, no plate is cut.
4. Add the sub-mm inner fillets (rim base, plate-to-wall) to microduck-upper-leg-left/part.py; the mirror inherits them; re-run refcheck (volume ratio should move from 0.9247 toward 1.0) and re-run the FEA that currently fails to mesh.
5. Re-run the whole out/stress matrix in PETG and record the material tier in the report, so a PASS is verdict-grade.
6. Declare a general tolerance on all six sheets and declare ISO 286 classes on the three Ø16.000 bearing seats and the four Ø1.60/1.80 locating pins.

Every newton that reaches the ground through the left or right foot passes through this plate. MJCF body mass 23.0131 g including the servo (SPEC.md §3).

Currently specified PLA, which is class-tier only, tops out at 55 °C and carries the file's own room-temperature-creep warning — wrong for a part that holds a standing robot for hours.
parts.tolerance_class: General: ISO 2768-m ASSIGNED BY THIS REVIEW (no tolerance is declared anywhere today — the sheet prints 'GENERAL TOLERANCE: CANNOT DETERMINE'); the numeric bands are CANNOT DETERMINE from this repo and must come from the issued ISO 2768-1 table. Sourced fits: Ø16.000 bearing seat → ISO 286 k6 (+0.001/+0.012 mm) if turned or reamed after printing, per ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4/iterations/v0.0.1/compat.py which derives and reproduces that row. An as-printed boss has no ISO class and the connection folder says so.
dfm_issues: ZERO DRAFT ANYWHERE, and three orthogonal hole axes. The 4 × Ø2.2 horn holes run along Z, the ear taps / servo screws / idler bore run along Y, and the counterbores open from both the plate underside (−Z) and the front face (+Y). A mould needs the main pull plus at least two side actions, and ≥1° on the two 1.400 mm walls (they form a 20 mm-deep pocket) and ≥0.5° on the plate faces. This is the redesign docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.2 warns about, not a re-quote.

0.900 mm ANNULUS UNDER THE BEARING SEAT. Computed off part.py's own constants: BOSS_D 16.0 → R8.000; the four Ø2.2 horn holes sit on HORN_PCD_R 6.000, so their outer edge is at R7.100 and the wall to the boss OD is 8.000 − 7.100 = 0.900 mm, in four places, directly under the surface a steel inner race sits on. At a 0.4 mm nozzle that is 2.25 perimeters — effectively two walls and no infill.

0.975 mm EAR LIGAMENT. The Ø2.05 ear tap (EAR_HOLE_Z 12.5) is 0.500 mm off the centre of the ear's R2.5 semicircular top (EAR_Z_C 13.0), leaving 2.500 − 0.500 − 1.025 = 0.975 mm of crescent to the outer edge, on both ears.

1.080 mm TO THE OUTSIDE AT THE SERVO-SCREW COUNTERBORES. Ø4.84 counterbore centred x 9.500 reaches x 7.080 against an outer face at x 6.000 → 1.080 mm; mirrored at x 25.500. This is the wall a screwdriver loads sideways during assembly.

EIGHT HORIZONTAL BORES BRIDGE (docs/DFM.md: '8 horizontal holes Ø2.05–5.5 bridge'). The tops sag; small ones come out undersize AND oval. The Ø2.05 ear taps are modelled as tap-into-plastic and will not thread straight off the bed.

THE PACK REPORTS THREE DIFFERENT 'THINNEST WALLS' FOR THIS PART AND LABELS NONE OF THEM: 0.198 mm (cecad.printed, a chamfer sliver — docs/DFM.md), 0.50 mm (the sheet's own section scan at X=17.50, Y=9.75, Z=−2.73), and 0.900 mm (the real structural annulus, computed above). A shop reading the sheet will control the wrong number.

ANISOTROPY: printed 'servo pocket up, bearing bore vertical' (out/print/PRINT.md), i.e. build axis = mesh Z = the yaw axis. The leg's weight cantilevers the front block off the plate, and the wall-to-plate junction is then loaded across the layers — PETG's 35 ± 6 MPa direction, 68.6 % of in-plane.

BEARING RING SUPPORTED ON 48.75 % OF ITS WIDTH: a 4.000 mm ring on a 1.950 mm boss, spanning the joint gap onto the mating part. ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4/connection.json refuses both verdicts on this and calls it a bench question.
critical_features: Ø16.000 × 1.950 bearing boss on the hip-yaw axis (17.500, −2.000, z 12.500→14.450), and the Ø19.000 × 0.500 shoulder beneath it that is the inner race's thrust face. Roundness and diameter here decide whether the joint runs or wobbles.
Ø12.000 horn bolt circle: 4 × Ø2.2 at (±6.000, 0) and (0, ±6.000) about the yaw axis, with Ø4.4 counterbores from below leaving a 2.950 mm grip length into the horn (cad/interfaces.json).
Hip-roll axis line x 17.500, z 0.000 along Y — the Ø5.000 × 1.800 idler stub, Ø2.7 through, Ø5.5 counterbore. Its perpendicularity to the yaw axis sets the leg's squareness.
The two 1.400 mm side walls and the 27.6° sloped bottom edge — the only thing carrying bending between the front block and the plate.
Ear tap centres x 8.500 and 26.500 at z 12.500: they must land on bearing_roll's Ø2.2 ear holes at the same (x, z), or the two parts will not bolt together.

parts.part: bearing_roll (part:microduck-bearing-roll, qty 2 per robot — one identical print per leg)
parts.process: FDM print. Best moulding candidate in the group if volume ever justifies it (1 mm draw depth, single pull, no side action). Also the group's only true sheet candidate apart from the rigidity plate — but the two 2.000 mm conical pegs would have to become pressed dimples or inserted dowels, so keep it printed.
parts.dims_mm: 23.0000 × 3.0000 × 40.0000 (out/verify/mech_dims.json). Rebuild delta [0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000], dim_verdict PASS. Note the 3.000 mm Y is the ENVELOPE, not the plate: the plate itself is 1.000 mm thick (part.py Y_BACK −14.5 to Y_FRONT −13.5) plus 2.000 mm of locating peg standing off one face. docs/PARTS.md row 7 calls it a '3 mm idler plate', which is wrong by 3× if a shop reads it as thickness. refcheck r1: p95 0.002 mm both ways, max 0.021/0.012, volume ratio 0.9995, 5/5 features. 0.62 cm³, 0.85 g/piece, 2m43s/piece.
parts.function: Closes the hip-roll XL330 on its horn side. It screws to yaw2roll's two ears, screws into the servo's two lower through-holes, locates in the servo's two upper through-holes on its own conical pegs, passes the Ø16 horn through a Ø19.000 window, and presents its back face as the thrust face the 22×16×4 hip-roll bearing runs on. It is a shear-and-clamp plate, not a bending member.
parts.material: PETG (Bambu PETG Basic, as above). A 1.000 mm printed plate is 5 layers at 0.20 mm; PLA's Z-direction bond in a 5-layer plate is the worst combination in the group and PETG's 35 ± 6 MPa Z is the sourced improvement.
parts.tolerance_class: General: ISO 2768-m ASSIGNED BY THIS REVIEW (bands CANNOT DETERMINE from repo — see group note D). Add a FLATNESS callout on the back face (assigned: ≤0.10 mm over the Ø22 bearing contact annulus) because that face is a running thrust face and nothing in the pack currently controls it. Ø19.000 window is clearance, not a fit.
dfm_issues: 0.900 mm LIGAMENTS IN FOUR PLACES, IN A 1.000 mm PLATE. Computed off part.py: the Ø2.2 ear holes at (8.500, 12.500) and (26.500, 12.500) sit 0.500 mm below the centres of the R2.5 top corner arcs at (8.500, 13.000)/(26.500, 13.000) → 2.500 − 0.500 − 1.100 = 0.900 mm of crescent; and the Ø2.2 servo holes at (9.500, −22.500)/(25.500, −22.500) sit 2.000 mm above the z = −24.500 bottom edge → 2.000 − 1.100 = 0.900 mm. Cross-section at each is 0.900 × 1.000 = 0.900 mm². These are the four points the plate tears at, and none is dimensioned on the sheet — the sheet's own section scan reports 1.00 mm at (28.81, −14.00), which is just the plate thickness at the edge and misses all four.

THE Ø19 BORE BRIDGES. docs/DFM.md: 'Ø19 bore on Y bridges — REAM if it seats a bearing/roll shaft.' It does not seat a bearing here (it is a horn clearance window), so a bridged, slightly oval Ø19 is tolerable — but only once someone confirms that, and the drawing does not say it. Add the note.
2 × Ø2.2 ON Y ALSO BRIDGE and print undersize.
TINY AND SLENDER (23 × 40 × 1 mm, 0.85 g). Handle after printing; expect warp on a 1 mm plate even lying flat.

THE PEGS ARE THE ONLY UNDERCUT-FREE FEATURE AND THEY ARE ALREADY DRAFTED: Ø1.800 base → Ø1.600 tip over 2.000 mm = 2.8624° per side. They enter the XL330's Ø2.000 through-holes (measured off xl330.stl, cad/interfaces.json), so the diametral clearance is 0.200 mm at the root — an FDM peg that prints 0.15 mm oversize consumes nearly all of it and the plate will not sit down. Control the peg root diameter.
ANISOTROPY: printed '3 mm plate flat, bore vertical' — the right call. Load is in-plane shear and clamp, so the layers carry it in their strong direction. This is the best-oriented part in the group.
critical_features: Back face flatness and its Ø22 bearing-contact annulus around the Ø19.000 window — the running thrust face.
Ø19.000 window concentric with the hip-roll axis at (17.500, 0.000).
Ear screw centres (8.500, 12.500) and (26.500, 12.500) — must match yaw2roll's ear taps to better than the 0.900 mm ligament allows, i.e. positional error must not eat the crescent.
Servo screw centres (9.500, −22.500) and (25.500, −22.500), 16.000 mm apart = the XL330's lower hole pitch.
Peg root diameter Ø1.800 and their 16.000 mm pitch at z 7.500 — the servo's only angular location.
1.000 mm plate thickness (NOT the 3.000 mm envelope docs/PARTS.md row 7 prints).

parts.part: hip_l (part:microduck-hip-bracket, qty 2 per robot — the SAME print both sides; the mesh is z-symmetric and the MJCF places it in hip_l and hip_l_2 with identical pos/quat, so there is no mirror part)

parts.dims_mm: 32.4500 × 34.5000 × 19.0000 (out/verify/mech_dims.json ref_mm; mech_dims records this mesh as 'rebuilt': false and so omits our rebuild from the 9 it counts). parts.function: The L-bracket that turns the hip-roll axis into the hip-pitch axis. It takes the hip-roll servo's horn on its +Y face, seats that joint's 22×16×4 bearing on the Ø16.000 boss, and presents a second identical Ø16.000 boss on its +X face 90° away for the hip-pitch joint into the thigh. Both legs' entire weight path turns a right angle inside this 4.53 cm³ part. MJCF body mass 5.21 g (SPEC.md §3: 'hip_l 6.19 ×2'). It is the only part in the group with a completed FEA: out/stress/report.json, PASS, SF 6.424, 20 N from roll_boss (fixed) to pitch_boss (loaded).

Both Ø16.000 bearing seats → ISO 286 k6 (+0.001/+0.012 mm) if machined, sourced from ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4 compat.py. ASSIGNED: perpendicularity of the pitch-boss axis to the roll-boss axis ≤0.2° — this is the leg's squareness datum and nothing controls it today.

Title block prints 1.96 × 16.00 × 16.00, 0.30 cm³, 0.4 g. 0.800 mm ANNULUS UNDER BOTH BEARING SEATS — THE GROUP'S THINNEST STRUCTURAL WALL, AND IT IS EXACTLY AT THE TWO MOST LOADED FEATURES. Computed off part.py: BOSS_D 16.0 → R8.000, four Ø2.4 holes on HOLE_PCD 12.000 → outer edge R7.200, wall 0.800 mm. Eight such ligaments (four per boss). docs/DFM.md measures the same 0.80 independently and calls it 'borderline (two perimeters, no margin)'. At a 0.4 mm nozzle it is EXACTLY two perimeters with zero infill, under a steel race.

0.890 mm AT THE COUNTERBORE MOUTHS. The Ø5.22 × 0.55 mouth step on the pitch face sits on the same Ø12 PCD → edge at R8.610 against a plate edge at R9.500 = 0.890 mm. The Ø4.84 counterbores leave 1.080 mm.
THE DENSEST PART IN THE ROBOT: 22 holes, EVERY ONE HORIZONTAL in the print orientation (docs/DFM.md), on two perpendicular axes, so every one bridges at the top and every small one prints undersize.

ZERO DRAFT ON EVERY Z FACE. Both plates are 19.000 mm wide, prismatic in z (±9.500), and the gusset rib flanks are prismatic at z ±5.000 — all parallel to a Y pull. A mould needs ≥1° on all of them plus one X side core for the pitch boss and its counterbores.

ANISOTROPY: printed 'bracket web down, bearing seat vertical'. The bracket's job is to resist the moment that turns the roll axis into the pitch axis, and that moment is carried across the corner where the two plates meet — the corner is exactly where a layer-normal tension appears in this orientation. The R6 inner fillet and R8 outer round help; the FEA that gave SF 6.424 does not model orientation at all.

THREE EXTRA COUNTERBORES IN OUR REBUILD vs the reference (r2 log: extra Ø4.84 at [17.5, −22.25, −6.0], Ø4.84 at [11.5, −22.25, 0.0], Ø5.22 at [34.275, 0.0, 6.0]) — harmless duplicates from the feature detector reading one bore twice, but they must not become holes on the regenerated sheet.
critical_features: Ø16.000 × 1.950 roll bearing seat at (17.500, −17.525, 0) with its Ø19.000 × 0.500 disc, and the Ø6.000 blind recess in it.
Ø16.000 × 1.950 pitch bearing seat at (39.475, 0, 0) with its own Ø19.000 disc and Ø6.000 recess — the boss the thigh hangs on.
The 90.0° between the two axes. This is the single dimension that decides whether the robot stands square, and nothing in the pack controls it.
Two Ø12.000 bolt circles, 4 × Ø2.4 each at 0/90/180/270°, counterbored Ø4.84 from the opposite face.
The R6.000 inner corner fillet (centre 28.000, −13.000) and R8.000 outer round (centre 30.000, −13.500) — the only stress relief in the load path.
The 10.000 mm-wide gusset rib (z ±5.000) with its R2.000 root fillets and R1.000 top rounds.

parts.process: FDM print, cavity opening up, supports enabled (out/print/PRINT.md flags 'floating cantilever - enable supports'). Of the whole group this is the part that would tool most easily if volume ever justified it, because it already carries 3.000° of draft.
parts.dims_mm: 28.0000 × 47.6594 × 60.9966 (out/verify/mech_dims.json ref_mm); our rebuild 28.0000 × 47.6608 × 60.9911, delta [0.0000, +0.0014, −0.0055] mm, max 0.0055, dim_verdict PASS. refcheck r1: p95 0.200 mm both ways, median 0.002, max 0.881/1.780, 6/6 features, VOLUME RATIO 0.9247. 3.84 cm³ (drawing), 4.67 g, 15m16s.
parts.function: The left thigh: a one-sided 1.000 mm-walled cup holding the hip-pitch and knee XL330s back to back on axes 42.000 mm apart (SPEC.md §3, and A0 (0,0) → A1 (22.000, 35.777) computes to 42.0000 mm). It is the longest lever in the leg — every gait moment about the knee reacts through this cup's single side wall and its 1.000 mm back plate. MJCF body mass 43.15 g including two servos; SPEC.md quotes 48.2 g ×2.
parts.material: PETG (Bambu PETG Basic). The 1.000 mm wall makes the material choice sharper here than anywhere else in the group: at 1.000 mm there is no infill, only skin, so the part IS its Z-bond. PETG's sourced Z allowable of 35 ± 6 MPa is the number to design to.
parts.tolerance_class: General: ISO 2768-m ASSIGNED BY THIS REVIEW (bands CANNOT DETERMINE from repo). ASSIGNED critical: 42.000 mm axis-to-axis ±0.10 mm (it sets the shank length and therefore the whole gait); Ø5.371 counterbore and Ø7.268 boss concentric to their axis within 0.05 mm. The four Ø1.600→1.800 locating pins have no declared fit against the XL330's measured Ø2.000 holes — see dfm_issues.
dfm_issues: NO STRUCTURAL VERDICT EXISTS FOR THE LONGEST LEVER IN THE LEG. out/stress/report.json returns CANNOT DETERMINE for microduck-upper-leg-left: 'gmsh failed … Invalid boundary mesh (overlapping facets) on surface 350 … Warning: No elements in volume 1 … worst distortion = −5.4665 … 48 elements with jac. < 0'. The shin (SF 7.51), ankle (2.02) and hip bracket (6.42) all solved; the thigh did not. I verified separately that the RELEASE STL is clean (closed 2-manifold, 22172 tris / 33258 edges each used twice, 0 degenerate, 0 duplicate), so this is a CAD-surface tessellation defect at the lofted rim, not a bad print file — but the part still has no strength answer.

THE REBUILD IS MISSING 7.5 % OF THE REFERENCE'S VOLUME, AND IT IS THE FILLETS THAT MATTER. Volume ratio 0.9247 (out/refcheck/ul_r1.log); component.json names the cause: 'the reference's sub-mm inner fillets (rim base, plate-to-wall) are not modelled'. Those are precisely the radii at the root of every 1.000 mm wall — the stress concentrations that decide whether a 1 mm PETG wall cracks. Print the model as-is and you print the sharp-cornered version of Pollen's part.

0.9485 mm ANNULUS AROUND THE AXLE COUNTERBORE, ON BOTH JOINT AXES. Computed off part.py: BOSS_BIG_D 7.268 with a Ø5.371 counterbore driven 2.500 mm in from the back face → (7.268 − 5.371)/2 = 0.9485 mm of wall over 1.800 mm of length, at the hip-pitch axis AND the knee axis. Deeper in, the Ø4.417 boss around the Ø2.4→2.8 axle hole leaves (4.417 − 2.800)/2 = 0.8085 mm at the floor end. These two annuli, not the 1.000 mm wall, are the part's governing sections — and the drawing dimensions only '1.00 WALL'.

0.800 mm '+' BOSS ARMS. Four cross bosses (hub Ø1.900, arms 0.800 wide × 2.900 long, standing 3.300 mm off the plate) sit exactly on the two-perimeter floor with zero margin. docs/DFM.md's measured 0.024 mm is a knife-edge, not these.

LOCATING-PIN FIT IS UNDECLARED AND TIGHT. Ø1.600 tip → Ø1.800 root (2.8624° per side) entering the XL330's Ø2.000 × 23 through-holes, measured off xl330.stl (cad/interfaces.json). Diametral clearance is 0.400 mm at the tip and 0.200 mm at the root. An FDM pin printed vertically routinely comes out +0.10 to +0.20 mm on diameter, which consumes the root clearance entirely and stops the servo seating. Control the root diameter or open the pin to Ø1.700.
THE HIP-PIVOT BORES BRIDGE. docs/DFM.md: '2× Ø5.37 on X bridge (hip pivot — ream)'. A bridged Ø5.371 comes out oval and undersize at the top, in the one bore that locates the joint.

DRAFT IS PARTLY THERE ALREADY — a genuinely useful measurement. part.py DRAFT = tan(3.0°) = 0.052408/mm, read off the mesh as 1.252 mm of wall movement over 23.9 mm of depth (probe D/E), on the side wall AND the top flange, plus a 1.86° flange tilt in y. The rim wall (x 66.5→69.5), the Ø7.268/Ø4.417 bosses and the '+' arms are all 0° and would need it. So the thigh is the one part in the group already drawn as if for a mould.

ANISOTROPY AND SUPPORTS: printed 'servo cavity opening up' with 'floating cantilever - enable supports'. The build axis is then the cup depth, so the single 1.000 mm side wall is built as a 61 mm-tall stack of thin layers and the knee moment loads it partly across those layers. The slicer preset used for the 218.29 g figure slices WITHOUT supports (out/print/PRINT.md flags); production plates must turn them on, which changes both mass and time.

THE SHEET IS BELOW THE HOUSE STANDARD. out/drawings/microduck-upper-leg-left/result.json reports holes: 2 on a part with 6 matched reference features plus 4 locating pins and 4 cross bosses, and the only wall dimensioned is '1.00 WALL'. docs/MANUFACTURING-REQUIREMENTS.md §A item 6 requires 'rib thickness and pitch, wall thickness, boss height … and every radius dimensioned'. Neither 0.9485 nor 0.8085 nor the 0.800 arms appear.
critical_features: 42.000 mm hip-pitch to knee axis distance — A0 (y 0, z 0) to A1 (y 22.000, z 35.777). The one dimension that sets the robot's gait.
Ø5.371 × 2.500 axle counterbore and the Ø2.4→2.8 through hole on each axis (the 0.9485 mm annulus).
Ø7.268 (x 67.0→69.5) and Ø4.417 (x 64.7→67.0) stepped servo-seat bosses on each axis.
The four locating pins at (−0.500, 43.777), (−0.500, 27.777), (−8.000, 22.500), (8.000, 22.500) — root diameter Ø1.800 and their 16.000 mm pitches, which are the servos' only angular location.
1.000 mm wall thickness on the back plate, rim, side wall and top flange, plus the 3.000° draft that must be preserved.
The R4.000 quarter-round on the whole outer edge and the sub-mm inner fillets that are currently MISSING from the model.

parts.process: FDM print, identical setup to the left. A mirrored cup is a different print, not the left one turned over: the single side wall stays on −y in both and the open face is at x = −42.5.

parts.part: upper_leg_rigidity_plate (part:microduck-upper-leg-rigidity-plate, qty 2 per robot — one geometry serves both thighs)
parts.process: TODAY: FDM print, dead flat on the bed (1.000 mm = 5 layers at 0.20 mm), brim. RECOMMENDED CHANGE: cut it from 1.000 mm sheet. It is a flat prism with every feature on one axis — waterjet, fibre laser or CNC router, no tool, no minimum order, and it removes the group's most warp-prone print. docs/PARTS.md row 11 already flags 'printed (or sheet — CANNOT DETERMINE; 1 mm is thin for FDM)'.
parts.dims_mm: CONFLICTED — THIS IS THE FINDING. Reference 1.0000 × 44.9965 × 58.0577. out/verify/mech_dims.json (the designated dimensional truth, regenerated 2026-09-02 21:05) records our rebuild at 1.0000 × 45.5000 × 58.7770, delta [0.0000, +0.5035, +0.7193], verdict PASS. The part's own evidence and ledger (out/refcheck/plate_r3.log and plate_ev.log, 02:48) record 1.000 × 44.999 × 58.060, delta [0.0, 0.003, 0.002], p95 0.008 mm both ways, 6/6 features. The released drawing (02:21) prints 1.00 × 45.00 × 58.06. Two of three released records disagree by 0.7193 mm on a 58 mm part. 0.74 cm³, 1.00 g/piece, 3m23s/piece.
parts.function: The 1.000 mm side plate that closes the open face of each thigh cup and stiffens it. Its R12 bend nests 0.45 mm inside the housing's inner bend; its two Ø19.000 windows sit on the hip-pitch and knee axes; its four Ø2.2 clearance holes sit exactly over the housing's four locating pins so the screws pass through into the servos. It converts the thigh from an open C-section into a closed box — which is the whole reason the thigh is stiff enough to work.
parts.material: CHANGE RECOMMENDED. As a print: PETG (Bambu PETG Basic). As a sheet, and this is the better answer: 1.000 mm AL6061-T6 — yield 276 MPa and E 68.9 GPa against printed PLA's 50 MPa / 3.5 GPa (ce-cad/cecad/fits.py MATERIALS), i.e. 19.69× the modulus in a part whose entire job is stiffness. Mass cost computed from the measured 0.74 cm³: 0.74 × 2.70 = 2.00 g in aluminium against 0.9 g printed = +1.10 g per plate, +2.20 g per robot = +0.298 % of the 737.2 g budget (SPEC.md §2). Two grams for twenty times the stiffness in the one part that exists only to be stiff.
parts.tolerance_class: General: ISO 2768-m ASSIGNED BY THIS REVIEW (bands CANNOT DETERMINE from repo). ASSIGNED: flatness ≤0.30 mm over the 58 mm length (a 1 mm printed plate warps and a warped stiffener pre-loads the thigh). If cut from sheet, the profile tolerance is the cutter's — typically tighter than anything FDM will hold, which is a second argument for sheet.
dfm_issues: BLOCKING — THE PART HAS THREE DIFFERENT LENGTHS IN THREE RELEASED RECORDS. See dims_mm. The 0.7193 mm spread is 48.0 % of the part's smallest structural ligament (1.499 mm, measured below). No plate may be cut until one number wins and drives mech_dims, the drawing and the STL together. History explains but does not excuse it: r1 PASSed at p95 0.256/0.279 mm but with bbox +0.504 y / +0.719 z because the web discs stood outside the R11 outline; r2 FAILED at p95 5.498 mm when the A1 arc walked the wrong way and the outline self-intersected (bbox y collapsed to 34.0, all 6 features unmatched); r3 fixed it to +0.003/+0.002. mech_dims.json is still reporting r1's numbers.

BLOCKING — THE RELEASED PRINT STL IS POLLEN'S VENDOR MESH. out/print/stl_manifest.json: src reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/upper_leg_rigidity_plate.stl, 3600 triangles, 'vendor mesh (Pollen reference asset, loaded as-is)'. CC BY-SA-NC — out/print/PRINT.md: 'fine to print, NOT licensed for sale'. The r3 rebuild passes at p95 0.008 mm and is not being used.

1.499 mm MINIMUM IN-PLANE LIGAMENT, MEASURED. I ran a numeric polygon-distance scan of the r3 outline against both Ø19.000 windows: the minimum wall from window rim to outline is 1.4990 mm at BOTH the hip-pitch and knee axes (R_OUT 11.000 − 9.500). The tightest screw-hole ligaments are 1.895 mm at (8.000, 22.500) and 1.971 mm at (−0.500, 43.777). The drawing prints '1.49 WALL', which confirms the scan. Governing cross-section is therefore 1.499 × 1.000 = 1.499 mm² — and that ring is what carries the reaction at each servo axis.

1.000 mm IS AT OR BELOW EVERY POWDER PROCESS'S FLOOR. docs/PRODUCTION.md §2.2: 'thinnest 1 mm (rigidity plate) — marginal at MJF/SLS's 1 mm minimum wall [JC2]'. So the MJF route costed at ≈ €57 grey per robot cannot make this part without a thickness change. Sheet or FDM only.

ORIENTATION IS THE WHOLE PRINT. docs/DFM.md: 'MUST lay flat (1 mm thick) … do NOT print it standing on edge (291 layers of a 1 mm wall on its side — it would fail)'. Five layers laid flat means the plate has essentially no Z-strength and its stiffness comes entirely from the in-plane skin — which is exactly the argument for cutting it from sheet instead.
WARP. A 45 × 58 × 1 mm flat plate is the classic warp geometry; brim required, and any bow pre-loads the thigh it is supposed to stiffen.

A PHANTOM FEATURE IN THE DETECTOR OUTPUT: 'extra in ours: hole Ø19.12 at [43.0, 0.0, 13.611]' appears in r1 and r3 alike. component.json explains it as the detector reading W2's R11.5 arc bottom as a hole. It is not a hole and must not become one on the regenerated sheet.
critical_features: Two Ø19.000 windows on the hip-pitch axis (0, 0) and knee axis (22.000, 35.777) — and the 1.499 mm ring of material outside each of them.

Four Ø2.2 clearance holes at (−0.500, 43.777), (−0.500, 27.777), (−8.000, 22.500), (8.000, 22.500) — must sit over the thigh's four locating pins to the same (y, z) within 0.01 mm, which is what makes the screws reach the servos.

parts.function: The whole neck. These two straps carry EVERYTHING above the neck-pitch axis: neck 36.8 g + neck_pitch 5.72 g + yaw_roll_motion 48.6 g + head (jaw_soft body) 188.8 g = 279.92 g = 2.7460 N static (masses [M] from docs/PARTS.md sec.6).

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: 2.0 mm laser-cut or stamped sheet. It is a plain flat blank - 4 holes, R2 corners, zero 3D features - and images/CATALOG.md reads the product photos as 'grey folded-sheet brackets' on the neck. dfm_issues: FATAL AS DRAWN IN PLA: the hole-to-edge ligament is 0.8500 mm, i.e. edge distance 2.0000 mm from hole centre = 0.87 x hole diameter. The usual convention for a bolted plate is e >= 1.5d (~3.45 mm here); this is 58% of that. Convention, not a standard I can cite from this repo - but the geometry is measured. At a 0.4 mm nozzle 0.85 mm is 2.125 extrusion widths: the slicer lays two perimeters and nothing else, so the ligament that resists screw tear-out of the entire 279.92 g head stack is two beads of plastic with a fusion line down the middle.

docs/DFM.md already reports this number ('neck-plate ... 0.850') but files it under a table row rather than as a defect. I re-measured it off the mesh and confirm it is a real structural wall, NOT a knife-edge sliver: material runs -32.0000..-31.1500 with a flat face at each end.

docs/DFM.md's risk column says '4x D2.3 on X bridge'. That is derived from the natural upright orientation and does NOT apply as sliced: ce-slice laid the plate flat, which puts all four hole axes along build Z. Flat is correct and the holes print clean. State the orientation on the drawing as MANDATORY - printed on edge the part is 10 layers of a 2 mm wall standing 20 mm tall and the 0.85 mm ligament becomes a single interlayer fracture plane.

Anisotropy: laid flat, the screw bearing load is in-plane (good). The out-of-plane bending the head applies is resisted only by layer adhesion across 10 layers. No published interlayer figure exists in this repo, so the margin is CANNOT DETERMINE.

NO FEA. out/stress/report.json covers only shin (SF 7.51), ankle (2.02), hip-bracket (6.42) and upper-leg (CANNOT DETERMINE). The neck plate - the thinnest loaded part on the robot - has never been analysed. Two 2.0 x 11.0 mm sections = 44.00 mm2 total. Static 2.7460 N is trivial; the real case is the head whipping during balance recovery (images/gallery_balance-recovery.mp4 is a published behaviour), and that load case is undefined.
No trapped volume, no undercut, no draft issue: it is a flat blank.

Heat-set inserts are not an option at 2 mm thickness with a 0.85 mm ligament - the boss would burst. The screws must be through-bolts into the servo case threads, which is what the XL330 case pattern implies.
parts.wall_note: 0.8500 mm is the measured hole-to-edge ligament, not the plate thickness (2.0000 mm).

The roller_blade's axle is a screw of shank D2.0500 / D2.7000. That leaves 3.55 mm of radial slop on a wheel. Nothing in Pollen's asset set is D9.8 or D12.2: the two declared bearings are 22x16x4 and 15x10x3 (docs/PARTS.md sec.3), neither of which fits either bore. A bush or bearing of OD 9.8 or 12.2 is implied by the geometry and does not exist in any source. This is the single blocking unknown for the roller wheel and no drawing can be released without it. CANNOT DETERMINE.

AXIAL FLOAT 2.4000 mm. The rim is 7.6000 mm wide and the roller_blade's wheel slot is 10.0000 mm (side-plate inner faces at x 45.0000 and 55.0000). The blade's inward bosses are D7.5/D5.5 at radii up to 3.750, which sit INSIDE the rim's D12.2 bore (r 6.100) and therefore never touch the rim's faces. Nothing constrains the wheel axially. Either spacers/washers are missing from the model or the wheel rattles 2.4 mm side to side.

Flange thickness 1.2000 mm is the min wall - three perimeters at a 0.4 mm nozzle. It is the feature that retains a tire under 24.7% hoop pre-strain (see the tire row). A flange that shears off releases the tire mid-skate.

Printed axis-vertical, the two 1.2 mm flanges are unsupported 2.0 mm radial overhangs off the D16.2 barrel - a 90 deg overhang on both faces of both flanges. They need either supports or a redesign to a 45 deg chamfered flange root.

Anisotropy: printed axis-vertical, the layers are annular. Hoop stress from the stretched tire is in-layer (good). The flange's retaining load is a bending moment about a layer line at the flange root (bad) - this is where it will fail.
No draft, no trapped volume as printed. Moulded, the D16.2 grooves between D20.2 flanges are axial undercuts requiring an axis-parallel split.

dfm_issues: ASSEMBLY IS AN INTERFERENCE PROBLEM, NOT A SLIP-ON. The tire is one continuous body whose CENTRAL bead (x 48.7000..51.3000, root D16.2000) sits between the rim's two D20.2000 flanges. To get it there the bead must stretch over a flange: 20.2 / 16.2 - 1 = 24.69% hoop strain, sustained during assembly. That is fine for a soft TPU and impossible for anything rigid. It also means the tire CANNOT be assembled by any axial slide, and it means a two-shot/overmould onto the rim is the alternative production route. Nothing in any source says which. This is the assembly-critical fact for the whole roller accessory and it has never been written down.

Knife-edge sidewall. The outer surface meets the bead root at exactly D16.2000 at x 46.2000 and 53.8000, so the section tapers to zero at both axial extremes. The thinnest finite section I could measure is 1.3422 mm at 0.05 mm in from the edge (x 46.25: r 8.100..9.4422). A mould fills this as a flash-prone feather edge; a 0.4 mm FDM nozzle simply cannot print it and the slicer will round it off, changing the bead geometry that retains the tire.

Printed TPU: the internal bead form is an overhanging undercut on the inside of an annulus. Axis-vertical it prints as a series of unsupported inward overhangs. Supports inside a TPU torus are close to unremovable. This part wants a mould.
The rim's 2.4000 mm axial float (see the rim row) is the tire's problem too - the contact patch wanders 2.4 mm across the wheel slot.

The tire is the ONLY collision geom in the roller MJCF, so every roller-mode policy (roller.onnx, roller_crouch.onnx, action_scale 0.8 - docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md) was trained against this exact profile. Change the tread crown and the trained policy is against a different robot.
Ground clearance is set here: tire bottom sits 11.0022 mm below the roller_blade's lowest point (tire centre z -38.7229 minus r 15.000 = -53.7229 vs blade bbox z min -42.7207).
NO FEA, no durometer, no wear or rolling-resistance data. Nothing.

MIN WALL 1.7678 mm - the true normal thickness of the 45 deg yoke arms (2.5000 mm measured horizontally x cos 45 deg). Those two arms are the entire load path from the ankle to the wheels. Printed with a layer plane crossing them they are two 1.77 mm cantilevers loaded in bending across their layer lines: the classic FDM failure. Orientation is not advice here, it is a specification.

The two axle bores are horizontal in every sensible print orientation and will bridge - undersize and oval at the top. They set the wheel axis. Ream both to a gauged size, or drill through both plates in one setup after printing so coaxiality survives.

The right plate's D5.0 head counterbore runs the FULL 2.5000 mm plate thickness (x 55.0000..57.5000), so the screw head bears on nothing but the 2.5 mm plate's outer chamfer at D5.4000. There is no seat depth left. Use a washer or the head will pull through PLA.

Left/right asymmetry unresolved in the source. In the MJCF the left blade's geom sits at (-0.022, 0.00622291, -0.0647) and the right at (0.022, 0.00622291, 0.0355181) - a 100.2 mm difference in the mesh z with different quaternions - and the left wheel bodies sit at z -0.0147 against the right at -0.0144819 (a 0.2181 mm difference). Whether those resolve to a genuine left/right ride-height mismatch or are an artefact of the different parent frames is CANNOT DETERMINE without resolving the full kinematic chain. It must be resolved before either blade is cut, because a 0.2 mm ride-height split across a 65 mm wheelbase is a permanent lean.
