Gauge 5 rings per lot: bore, OD, width to 0.001 mm - no vendor sheet exists for either ring (ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4/connection.json rating.grip_N = null), so the incoming gauge IS the tolerance record.

Gauge the NP-F550 pack against the cradle: the mesh the power_support cradle was measured from is named np_f970 and measures 38.6085 x 20.5755 x 70.8086 mm (out/verify/mech_dims.json). Product spec says NP-F550. Reject the lot if the pack exceeds the cradle envelope.
Boards (Radxa Zero 3W, Robot HAT, imu_to_dxl v2, banana contact PCB) stay in shielded bags; bags are opened only inside the EPA at Station 9.
tools: Ø15.00 / Ø16.00 / Ø10.00 / Ø22.00 go-no-go plug and ring gauges
risks: Wrong ankle revision reaching Station 5: the leg is 9.9981 mm long in Y and the sole contact point moves. Found only at the walk test in Station 13 - FULL LEG DISASSEMBLY.
Obsolete trunk_shell_* parts reaching Station 12: they carry no neck-mount cluster, so the neck-pitch reaction has nowhere to go.

The three custom PCBs (Robot HAT, imu_to_dxl v2, banana contact) have NO published design files. Until they are designed and fabbed, Stations 9, 11 and 13 CANNOT run. This is the critical path for the whole line.

stations.name: Printed-part preparation - ream / drill / tap / heat-set
operations: REAM every bore that carries a bearing or a press-fit. docs/DFM.md: 'Horizontal bores that carry a bearing or press-fit must be reamed - a bridged bore is oval and undersize at the top.' The list: ankle Ø15.0 pocket x2 and its Ø14.0 window; upper-leg Ø5.37 axle bores x4 (2 per thigh); bearing_roll Ø19.0 x2; upper_leg_rigidity_plate Ø19.0 x2; trunk_base Ø19.0 x2; shin/hip pivots.

Ream the ankle pocket to Ø15.0 H7 FROM THE OUTBOARD FACE through the Ø16 x 0.5 45-deg lead-in at x 35.3; stop collar at 2.30 + 0.10 mm; the Ø14.0 window at x 32.5 is the back stop (ce-parts/microduck-ankle-left/iterations/v0.0.1/cad/interfaces.json).

DRILL AND FORM-TAP every M2 pilot. docs/DFM.md: 'Every Ø1.55 / Ø1.60 (M2) and Ø2.05-Ø2.3 hole prints undersize and, when horizontal, bridges... drill to tapping size and form-tap after printing.' 20 measured Ø1.6 tap positions: power_support 8 (of which 2 are Ø1.55 x 7.8 deep), face_part 4, right_shell 1, remainder per docs/PARTS.md §5.

FIT M2 brass heat-set inserts at every position where the thread is LOADED (SPEC.md §6). Installation temperature = the filament's own print temperature + 10-20 degC (Prusa published rule, prusa3d.com M2-short insert page, read 2026-09-02). The absolute number is CANNOT DETERMINE here: out/print/slice.json records the preset name ('Bambu PLA Basic @BBL H2S') but no nozzle temperature.

Gauge the Ø16.0 x 1.95 inner-race bosses (yaw2roll, hip-bracket x2, neck-pitch-bracket at 1.9) and the Ø16.0 x 4.0 boss (yaw-roll-motion) with a Ø16.00 ring gauge. A boss that fails the gauge is scrapped here, never pressed.
Deburr the power_support sprung latch tongue by hand only. docs/DFM.md calls it 'the one genuinely fragile, moving printed feature in the set'; the slit measures 0.4885 mm (part.py SLIT_W 0.466).
Set aside the 1.000 mm upper_leg_rigidity_plate and the 2.000 mm neck plates flat - both are laid-flat prints and will take a set if stacked on edge.
tools: drill press with fine-feed and depth stop
Ø15.0 H7, Ø19.0, Ø5.37, Ø10.0 machine reamers with stop collars
M2 form tap (roll tap) + Ø1.70 tap drill
temperature-controlled heat-set press with M2 insert tip and Z stop
Ø16.00 ring gauge, Ø15.00 plug gauge
risks: THIS IS THE LINE'S BOTTLENECK at 12.6-24.4 min, and it is why this plan totals 70-140 min/unit against docs/PRODUCTION.md's 36-101 min - that DFA count charged only 'heat-set inserts, if used: 0-60' and no reaming or tapping time. Duplicate this station before any other.
A bore reamed oversize is scrap - a printed PLA seat has no second chance and no ISO class (ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4/connection.json: interference CANNOT DETERMINE).
An insert set crooked or too deep cracks the boss. PLA 'is stiff and can crack if the hole is too tight, the boss is too thin, or the insert is overheated'. On a shell that is cosmetic scrap.
Skipping the tap on power_support's 2 x Ø1.55 x 7.8 deep holes: they are the battery cradle's own mounts and the failure shows up only when the pack is loaded.

stations.name: Servo ID + EEPROM programming (ONE servo at a time)
operations: Take ONE XL330 from the kit. Every servo ships ID = 1, baud = 57600 bps (value 1), Return Delay Time = 250 (500 us) - emanual.robotis.com/docs/en/dxl/x/xl330-m288/, read 2026-09-02.
Seat it in the SVO-ID-01 cradle. Plug the single JST EH 3-pin lead. THERE IS EXACTLY ONE SOCKET ON THIS BENCH - two servos cannot be connected at once, by construction.
Disable torque before writing EEPROM ('data in the EEPROM area can only be modified when torque is disabled' - emanual).

Write, in this order: ID, then baud_rate = 3 (1 Mbps), return_delay_time = 0, pwm_slope = 255, shutdown = 52. These are the four values robotd asserts at boot (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §3.3, model.rs:82-94, bus.rs:122-140) - writing them here saves the correction pass and proves the servo takes them.

Drive the servo to position 2048 (= 0 rad, 12-bit encoder; bus.rs:31) and LEAVE IT THERE. Every horn bracket in Stations 5-8 is bolted on at 2048. A servo bolted up off-zero clips its own range and the fix is 4 M2 screws down a counterbore.
Read back every written register. Any mismatch = the servo goes to the reject bin, not back into the tray.
Apply a 6 x 12 mm laser-printed polyester label with the ID on the case flat, then lay the servo in ITS OWN slot in the 15-slot tray: 10,11,12,13,14 / 20,21,22,23,24 / 30,31,32,33,34.

Repeat 15 times. IDs and joints per docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §3.2: 20 L-hip-yaw, 21 L-hip-roll, 22 L-hip-pitch, 23 L-knee, 24 L-ankle, 10-14 the right mirror, 30 neck-pitch, 31 head-pitch, 32 head-yaw, 33 head-roll, 34 mouth.
tools: U2D2 or equivalent half-duplex TTL adapter, ONE port
SVO-ID-01 cradle with a single JST EH 3-pin socket
bench PC running Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 tooling
risks: DUPLICATE ID IS THE SINGLE WORST DEFECT ON THIS ROBOT. There is one bus and one port ('There is no second bus and no second port', rdesign:23-38). Two servos answering to the same ID make sync_read return garbage and make the servo unaddressable - you cannot write a new ID to either one while both are on the chain. The fix is to split the chain physically, i.e. DISASSEMBLE the limb that holds the offender. That is why programming happens on a one-socket bench, before installation, and why the tray is slotted.
Un-programmed servo (still ID 1 @ 57600): it is invisible to a 1 Mbps scan, so the unit reads as 'servo missing' at Station 11 and the operator hunts the wrong fault.
Servo not left at 2048: every downstream horn joint inherits the error. Requires disassembly of that joint.
The label is the only human-readable ID. An unlabelled servo mixed back into the tray poisons the batch.

stations.name: Harness cut, crimp and label
operations: Cut the 20 determinate Dynamixel/loom lengths on the HARN-01 board, exactly as wiring/CABLES.md gives them (route floor + stated slack): 35, 60, 50, 165, 35, 120, 40, 65, 125, 20, 95 (left chain) and 40, 65, 125, 20, 95 (right chain), plus tof-hat 35, spk-hat 70, csi-radxa-camera 15, bat-hat 340 mm. Total 1615 mm over 21 cables.

Conductor: AWG 21. wiring/drop.json: at AWG 21 the worst HAT-to-farthest-ankle drop is 0.550 V (PASS at both 8.2 V and 6.6 V pack extremes). AWG 22 gives 0.694 V - still PASS but 26 % worse; do not substitute without re-running the check.
Crimp JST EH 3-pin both ends (EHR-03 housing, SEH-001T-P0.6 contact) - ROBOTIS' 'X3P' lead. Pinout 1 GND, 2 VDD, 3 DATA.

Label EVERY cable at both ends with its id from wiring/CABLES.md (dxl-hat-id34, dxl-id34-id33, ... dxl-id13-id14, tof-hat, spk-hat, csi-radxa-camera, bat-hat). The chain order is not recoverable by inspection once the shells are on.
Pull-test 3 crimps per shift to destruction; log the force. No published retention figure exists for this connector in any repo source, so the shift log IS the record.
mic-hat: CANNOT DETERMINE - part and placement unknown (wiring/CABLES.md row 19). Leave the position open; do not guess a length.
hat-radxa-40pin is NOT a cable: 2x20 0.1 in board-to-board, mated at Station 9.
tools: HARN-01 cut-and-crimp board with 22 labelled lanes at the exact lengths
risks: dxl-id32-id31 at 165 mm is the cable that decides the robot. It crosses head_yaw (+-170 deg) AND head_pitch (+-90 deg) = 520 deg of span, and 90.8 mm of its 165 mm is slack paying out that sweep. Cut it short and it tears at the first full yaw sweep; cut it long and it snags. Measure this one twice.
bat-hat at 340 mm crosses 720 deg of joints (neck_pitch, head_pitch, head_yaw, head_roll) - 125.7 mm of slack. It is the most-crossed cable in the robot and it carries pack current.
A mislabelled cable is discovered at Station 11 as a missing device, after the harness has been dressed through the neck.

stations.name: Leg sub-assembly, left and right (2 per robot)
operations: Set the LEG-01 nest for the side being built. Datum the upper leg on its two Ø5.37 axle bores - hip-pitch at mesh (70.5, 0.0, 0.0) and knee at (70.5, 22.0, 35.777), 42.000 mm apart (ce-parts/microduck-upper-leg-left interfaces.json; SPEC.md §3 'Thigh hip-pitch->knee 42.0 mm sagittal').

Drop the hip-pitch servo (ID 22 left / 12 right) and the knee servo (ID 23 / 13) into the thigh cups, each onto its stepped Ø7.27 servo_rear_seat boss standing 4.8 mm off the inner face. Verify the labels before the plate goes on.

Press ONE 22x16x4 bearing at upper_leg body (22.0, 35.777, -4.0) - the knee idler. PRESS ON THE INNER RING ONLY (punch P1). See the bearing note in the summary: every measured 22x16x4 seat on this robot is a Ø16.0 INNER-race boss; no Ø22 outer-race housing exists anywhere on the shelf.

Screw the 1.000 mm upper_leg_rigidity_plate across the thigh - 4 x Ø2.2 M2 clearance [community, docs/PARTS.md §5]. It is a 1 mm plate: use a flanged head or a washer, and torque LAST after the servos are seated.
Fit the ankle servo (ID 24 / 14) into the shin (the 8.0 x 20.0 x 58.0 mm stepped plate). Shin carries 6 x Ø2.2 clearance + 6 counterbores [community].

Join shin to knee: 4 x M2 through the shin's 'knee' horn face - Ø15.9 disc with Ø6 bore and 4 x Ø2.2 on an 8.486 mm square (= the Ø12.000 bolt circle at 45 deg; 8.486 x sqrt(2) = 12.001, ce-connections/spline-xl330-horn). Idler side onto the thigh's bearing.

Press the 15x10x3 bearing into the ankle bracket's Ø15.0 x 2.3 pocket - PRESS ON THE OUTER RING (punch P2), from the outboard face through the Ø16 x 0.5 lead-in. The ring is 3.000 mm in a 2.300 mm pocket: 0.700 mm stands proud BY DESIGN, to clear the shin's Ø10.0 x 3.2 boss. Do not press it flush.
Fix ankle to the ankle servo horn - 5 x Ø2.2 clearance + 5 counterbores [community]; the horn face is 4 x Ø2.2 at (dy,dz) = (0,+-6) and (+-6,0).
Screw the hard foot to the ankle: one M2 through the ankle's Ø2.2 foot_screw at (50.0, 4.502) with a Ø4.4 x 1.0 counterbore, plus the two 5.0000 mm indexing spigot blocks at y 33.663.

Push the TPU sole onto the foot LAST. Zero-clearance prismatic plug, section 36.8000 x 49.8000 mm, engagement 7.9170 mm at the toe to 10.6550 mm at the heel, no fastener, no barb, no adhesive (ce-connections/press-fit-sole-foot). Pull-off force: CANNOT DETERMINE - nobody has pulled one on a gauge.
tools: BRG-PR-01 arbor press with punches P1 and P2 and a 0-1000 N load cell
preset torque screwdriver 0.02-0.5 N.m, hex 1.5 mm
risks: Pressing the 22x16x4 on the OUTER ring drives the load through the balls and brinells the races (ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4: 'pressing on the wrong ring drives the load through the balls'). The bearing still turns, so the defect ships.

The 22x16x4 sits on a 1.95 mm boss and is 4.0 mm wide - 48.75 % engagement. 2.05 mm of ring overhangs unsupported. If the press does not bottom on the shoulder, the ring cocks and the joint runs eccentric.
Removing a pressed bearing from printed PLA 'is likelier to yield the plastic than the ring' - the part is scrap. Every press is one-shot.
Bolting the shin to a knee servo that is NOT at 2048 clips the +-90 deg knee range. Requires unbolting 4 M2 down counterbores - DISASSEMBLY.
The sole is a zero-clearance TPU interference. Once on, taking it off stretches it; a sole fitted before the foot screw is torqued means pulling it again.

stations.name: Trunk & hip sub-assembly
operations: Mount trunk_base on the TRK-01 fixture. NOTE THE THICKNESS: the structural plate is 1.000 mm, not 3.000 mm. Direct probe of trunk_base.stl at (x -28.000, y 0.000) reads material z 16.500-17.500 = 1.000 mm; at a pin location (-25.500, -9.500) it reads 16.500-19.500 = 3.000 mm. The 3.0000 in out/verify/mech_dims.json is the BOUNDING BOX over four 2.000 mm locating pins. The fixture must support the whole 57.000 x 36.000 mm footprint or the plate bows under the screwdriver.
Fit the two hip-yaw servos (ID 20 left, ID 10 right) hanging from trunk_base, horns down (-z), horn hubs through the two Ø19.0 holes at mesh (+-17.5, -2.0). Joint axes at world (6.0, +-17.5, 115.0).

DO NOT press a bearing into trunk_base. The manual step 'Press the two 22x16x4 hip-yaw idler bearings into trunk_base' cannot be executed as written: the only measured feature on that axis is a Ø19.0 horn-clearance hole (ce-parts/microduck-trunk-base interfaces.json, MEASURED 2026-09-01; re-probed this session - material along x at y -2.0, z 17.0 shows a void x 8.0..27.0 = 19.000 mm centred on 17.5, and along y at x 17.5 a void y -11.5..7.5 = 19.000 mm centred on -2.0). A Ø22 ring cannot enter a Ø19 hole. The hip-yaw bearings seat on yaw2roll's / bearing_roll's Ø16.0 x 1.95 boss and are fitted at the step below.

Bolt power_support (the 54.5 x 17.0 x 83.5 mm battery cradle) to trunk_base - 8 x M2 into the prepared inserts; the trunk_base inner screw pair at (+-9.5, 20.5) lines up with power_support's Ø2.5 flange holes.
Clamp the banana contact PCB onto power_support's Ø3.9 pins with banana_pcb_locker - 2 x M2 through its Ø2.17 eyes. The locker's eye annulus is 0.950 mm at its modal wall (p1 0.9204) - torque it low.

Press one 22x16x4 onto yaw2roll's Ø16.0 x 1.95 boss (left) and bearing_roll's identical boss (right) at body (0.0, 16.5, 12.5). The Ø19.0 x 0.5 shoulder at z 12.0..12.5 is the thrust face and the hard stop; the ring must then occupy z 12.5..16.5. Verify with a depth gauge.
Fix yaw2roll to the left hip-yaw horn and bearing_roll to the right - 4 x M2 on the Ø12.000 bolt circle at (+-6, 0) and (0, +-6).

Mount the hip-roll servos (ID 21 left, ID 11 right) into yaw2roll / bearing_roll: 2 x Ø2.4 servo_screw with Ø4.84 x 2.2 counterbores at (+-9.5 from centre, y 9.5, z 7.5), plus the 2 x Ø2.05 x 4.0 ear taps. Roll axes +x at world (22.5, +-17.5, 102.5).
Press one 22x16x4 onto each hip bracket's Ø16.0 x 1.95 boss - roll_bearing_seat at (17.5, -16.55, 0) and pitch_bearing_seat at (40.45, 0, 0), 90 deg apart on the same part (nest N2 indexes both).
Fix hip_l / hip_l_2 to the hip-roll horns - Ø19 disc face, Ø6 blind recess, 4 x Ø2.4 on a Ø12 bolt circle, counterbored Ø4.84. Hip-pitch axes +y at world (4.0, +-42.5, 102.5).
Hang the two leg sub-assemblies from the hip brackets: horn side to the hip-pitch servo, idler side onto the bracket's pitch bearing.
DO NOT fit the battery yet.
tools: TRK-01 fixture with four Ø1.9 x 2.1 pin sockets
BRG-PR-01 with punch P1 and nests N1, N2
risks: The four trunk_base locating pins are printed, Ø1.80 tapering to Ø1.59 over 2.0 mm. They shear if a mating part is forced over them out of square, and the mating part itself is CANNOT DETERMINE (not one of this group's meshes).
A 22x16x4 pressed without bottoming on the Ø19.0 x 0.5 shoulder leaves the ring proud and the whole leg runs 0.5 mm low on that side.

The hip-yaw bearing's OUTER race is radially unhoused - no Ø22 pocket exists on any part. Whether that is Pollen's intent or a decimation artefact is CANNOT DETERMINE; it must be settled on a real unit before the fixture is frozen.
power_support's modal wall is 0.950-2.050 mm with p1 = 0.7675 mm and a 0.4885 mm latch slit. Over-torque here splits the cradle and the battery falls out in service.
A hip servo fitted before its bearing is pressed means removing the servo (4 M2 in counterbores) to reach the boss - DISASSEMBLY.

stations.name: Neck sub-assembly
operations: Bolt the ID-30 (neck_pitch) servo to the trunk. Axis -y at world (26.0, 14.5, 152.421); range -90 ... +60 deg.

Span the 50.000 mm neck with the two 2.000 mm neck plates (2.0 x 20.0 x 11.0 mm each), a servo at each end - 4 x Ø2.3 M2 clearance per plate [community]. Neck-pitch to head-pitch centre distance is 50.000 mm exactly (SPEC.md §3).
Bolt the ID-31 (head_pitch) servo at the top of the plates. Axis +y at world (26.0, 14.5, 202.421); range +-90 deg.
Press one 22x16x4 onto neck_pitch's Ø16.0 x 1.9 boss at body (0.0, 20.793, -14.5) - this is the HEAD-YAW idler, fitted now because it is unreachable once the head is on.

Fix the neck_pitch bracket to the ID-31 horn - the bracket carries 12 x Ø2.2 clearance + 4 counterbores [community]: yaw_horn_top 4 on a Ø12 circle, pitch_horn_right 4 and pitch_horn_left 4 at (+-17.5, 0, -28.793).
tools: 50.000 mm setting gauge across the neck plates
risks: Forgetting the head-yaw bearing at neck_pitch (0.0, 20.793, -14.5) is only discovered when the head is fitted at Station 10 - the whole head and neck come apart to fix it.
The neck plates are 2.000 mm thick with a 0.850 mm minimum wall (docs/DFM.md). They are the most over-torque-sensitive plate in the robot.
The neck-pitch joint axis at world (26.0, 14.5, 152.4) is the SAME axis the two show shells react into - see Station 12. If the shells' mount cluster is not aligned here, the shells will not close.

stations.name: Head mechanism sub-assembly
operations: Press TWO 22x16x4 bearings into yaw_roll_motion at body x = -16.0 and +18.0, z 14.5 - straddling the head-roll axis. The -16 seat is the Ø16.0 x 4.0 boss with a Ø12 through bore (the only FULL-WIDTH seat in the robot: 4.0 mm boss for a 4.0 mm ring, 100 % engagement).

Fit yaw_roll_motion onto the head-yaw axis: ID-32 horn below, neck_pitch's bearing above. Head-yaw axis +z at world (26.0, 0.0, 221.115), range +-170 deg. 4 x Ø2.5 case screws at (-22.5, +-8) and (7.5, +-8) plus 4 x Ø2.2 on the Ø12 horn circle.
Mount the ID-33 head-roll servo in yaw_roll_motion. Roll axis -x at world (8.1, 0.0, 235.615), range +-25 deg.

Fix motor_support (73.5 x 54.2 x 18.8 mm) to the ID-33 horn. NOTE: out/verify/mech_dims.json records motor_support as rebuilt:false and is STALE - ce-parts/microduck-motor-support/component.json is v0.1.0 verdict PASS (refcheck r6 p95 0.363/0.456 mm, median 0.013/0.017 mm, bbox delta 0.00 mm per axis, 6/6 reference holes and bosses matched, 0 unmatched, evidence/refcheck/2026-09-01T19-55-33Z). Build to v0.1.0 and re-run the verify pass.

Mount the ID-34 mouth servo in motor_support's south saddle (arch shell r 12.7/11.1 over the wall band y -20.35..-15.95). Modal wall of motor_support is 1.750 mm (2575 of 4827 intervals), median 1.8123, p5 1.7000, p1 1.0000.
Press the third 15x10x3 bearing for the mouth hinge at jaw_soft body (3.2, -40.0, -18.0) - PRESS ON THE RING THAT IS BEING FITTED, punch P2.
Mount the jaw on the ID-34 horn plus that bearing - 5 x Ø2.2 clearance [community]. Mouth range -5 deg (closed) to +30 deg (open); it is NOT in any policy (MOUTH_INDEX = 9, model.rs:31).
tools: BRG-PR-01 punches P1, P2 and nest N4
risks: motor_support built to the stale v0.0.1 geometry rather than the PASSed v0.1.0.

The two yaw_roll_motion bearings straddle the roll axis at -16.0 and +18.0 - they are NOT symmetric (34.000 mm apart on a 34.000 mm part). Pressing them in the mirrored positions puts the head-roll axis 2.000 mm out and the fault only shows as a head that leans.
Both head bearings are unreachable once motor_support and the electronics are on. A missed press = full head teardown.

stations.name: Head electronics (EPA - ESD-controlled)
operations: ENTER THE EPA. Wrist strap on and verified; boards out of their shielded bags only on the dissipative mat; ionizer running over the bench because the head shell is an unearthable insulator.

Screw the M12 lens holder to the IMX219 board - 3 x M2. Thread the lens into the holder. Set the holder into motor_support's Ø15.0 open-arch CRADLE on the -x face, axis x through (y 0.0000, z 7.4995); the cradle measures Ø14.9938 / 14.9954 / 14.9978 at three stations (residual mean < 0.0036 mm), ring bands at x -39.5000..-37.5000 (2.0000 mm) and -36.5000..-35.5000 (1.0000 mm).
The camera sits behind face_part at world (81.4, 0.0, 251.1) and is MOUNTED UPSIDE DOWN (rotation 180 in the overlay). Get this wrong and the image is inverted in every policy and every recording.
Fit the ToF module at world (81.4, 22.4, 249.1) - 22.4 mm to the LEFT of the camera. I2C3, address 0x29. Connect tof-hat: JST-SH 4-pin 1.0 mm (Stemma/Qwiic) at the HAT's J5, 35 mm.

Stack the Robot HAT on the Radxa Zero 3W 40-pin header. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-CONSEQUENCE MATE IN THE ROBOT: a 2x20 0.1 in board-to-board offset by one row or one column destroys both boards. Use a keyed alignment shim.

COMPATIBILITY FLAG: the compute mesh in the reference set is pcb__raspberry_pi_zero_2_w (65.000 x 1.600 x 30.000 mm) - a Pi Zero 2 W placeholder. The documented host is a Radxa Zero 3W at the same 65 x 30 mm footprint, but its mounting-hole pattern, connector positions and Z height are CANNOT DETERMINE. The head-electronics fit is UNVERIFIED until a real Radxa is offered into a real motor_support.
Fit the speaker (35.0 x 25.0 x 7.0 mm placeholder envelope; exact part CANNOT DETERMINE) and run spk-hat, 70 mm.
Fit the CSI ribbon Radxa->camera, 22-pin 0.5 mm FFC, 15 mm floor. The camera-board end is CANNOT DETERMINE (22-pin 0.5 mm or 15-pin 1.0 mm + adapter).
Fit eye-ring into face_part - 10 x Ø2.2 clearance + 4 x Ø1.6 tap [community]. Fit noenoeil (29.9 x 9.5 x 29.9 mm).
Fit the TPU lips: jaw_soft (8.4376 mm) on the jaw, soft_mouth_top (3.2762 mm) under the top shell.
The mic loom is CANNOT DETERMINE (part and placement unknown, wiring/CABLES.md row 19). Do not improvise a route.
tools: ESD EPA: dissipative mat, wrist strap, ionizer, ESD-safe hex drivers
M12 lens focus target at 1.0 m
risks: Every semiconductor in the head is HBM 2 kV - the LOWER boundary of ANSI/ESDA/JEDEC JS-001 Class 2, i.e. the least robust class this line will see: TLV320AIC3104 HBM +-2000 V and CDM +-1500 V (SLAS510G §8.2 p.7), VL53L5CX HBM +-2 kV (DS13754 Table 13 p.17), BMI088 HBM 2 kV (Table 7 p.12), LSM6DSV16X HBM 2 kV (§4.5 Table 9 p.19). The CDM +-1500 V on the codec is the one that governs BOARD handling: it is the charged board touching ground that kills it, not the operator.
40-pin header misalignment: both boards scrap, and the fault is silent until Station 11.
Camera fitted right way up: the whole vision stack is wrong and it is behind face_part, eye-ring and the head shell - DISASSEMBLY.
The Robot HAT does not exist as a design. Until it does, this station cannot be released.

stations.name: Final marriage and harness routing - SHELLS STILL OFF
operations: Mount the trunk/hip/leg assembly on the STAND-01 post, feet 60 mm clear of the bench, legs hanging free.
Join neck to trunk (ID-30 horn to the neck plates) and head to neck (yaw_roll_motion onto neck_pitch's head-yaw bearing).

Build the ONE Dynamixel chain in this exact order (wiring/CABLES.md): HAT -> id34 (35 mm) -> id33 (60) -> id32 (50) -> id31 (165) -> id30 (35) -> imu200 (120) -> then it SPLITS: imu200 -> id20 (40) -> id21 (65) -> id22 (125) -> id23 (20) -> id24 (95); and imu200 -> id10 (40) -> id11 (65) -> id12 (125) -> id13 (20) -> id14 (95).

ROUTE dxl-id32-id31 (165 mm) AT THE SERVO FLANK, not across the joint face. It crosses head_yaw (+-170 deg) and head_pitch (+-90 deg) = 520 deg, and 90.8 mm of its length is the slack that pays out that sweep. Coil the slack as a single loose service loop on the flank; do not tie it down inside the sweep.

ROUTE bat-hat (340 mm) WITH the bus loom. It crosses neck_pitch, head_pitch, head_yaw and head_roll = 720 deg, with 125.7 mm of slack, and it carries pack current. This is the hardest route in the robot.

STRAIN RELIEF: a tie-down within 15 mm of every JST EH connector, on the STATIC side of each joint, so the connector never takes the bending load. No published retention figure exists for these housings in any source here - the tie-down is the retention.
Every cable that crosses a joint gets its service loop on the PARENT-body side, and the loop's plane must be perpendicular to the joint axis so the loop winds and unwinds rather than twisting.

Fit the imu_to_dxl v2 board (ID 200) at the trunk site, world (-21, 0, 105.3), mount quaternion [0.7071, 0, 0.7071, 0] = +90 deg about Y. The board's orientation IS a calibration constant (imu.rs:76-83) - fitting it rotated silently breaks fall detection.
Dress the whole loom, then hand-cycle EVERY joint to both MJCF limits before anything is closed.
tools: STAND-01 assembly post with magnetic head arms
risks: A cable routed on the wrong side of a joint wraps at the head-yaw +-170 deg sweep and tears its own conductors. Discovered at the range test - if the shells are already on, that is a full head teardown.

Chain order wrong: the bus still enumerates (Dynamixel is a multidrop bus, order is electrically irrelevant) but the CABLE LENGTHS no longer fit the geometry, so the loom is under tension somewhere. The failure is a slow one, in the field.
imu_to_dxl fitted rotated: robotd's fall detection uses trunk = [+raw_z, +raw_y, -raw_x]. A rotated board means the robot limps when it is upright and stands when it is falling.
This is the LAST station at which anything inside is reachable without disassembly. Nothing may proceed to Station 12 until Station 11 passes.

stations.name: Electrical bring-up, bus scan and calibration - SHELLS STILL OFF
operations: Power from the BUS-01 bench supply at 7.4 V with a 3 A limit FIRST, not from a pack. If the unit draws over the limit, nothing is destroyed.
SCAN THE BUS at 1 Mbps, Protocol 2.0, /dev/ttyS2. Expect EXACTLY: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34 and 200. Sixteen devices, no more, no fewer, no ID 1.
STOP THE UNIT on any duplicate, any missing device, or any device answering at 57600. A duplicate ID here means a servo skipped Station 3, and the offending limb must be opened to isolate it.
Confirm the runtime's four asserted registers took: return_delay_time = 0, baud_rate = 3, pwm_slope = 255, shutdown = 52 (model.rs:82-94).

Read present_input_voltage on every device (address 144, u16, 0.1 V/count). The farthest ankle must sit within 0.550 V of the HAT - that is the AWG 21 figure from wiring/drop.json. A larger drop means a bad crimp; find it now.

Verify the imu_to_dxl block at register 124: 12 bytes, gyro x/y/z i16 LE at +-500 dps / 17.5 mdps LSB, then the SFLP quaternion. An all-zero quaternion means the SFLP table has not been written yet - wait, do not reset.
Flash the eMMC image, bring up Wi-Fi/BT, seed the voice bank.

Run ROM-01: drive every joint to both MJCF limits and confirm no cable binds. Hip yaw -25...+30 (left) / -30...+25 (right); hip roll +-22; hip pitch +-90; knee +-90; ankle +-90; neck pitch -90...+60; head pitch +-90; head yaw +-170; head roll +-25; mouth -5...+30.
Run the head-yaw +-170 deg sweep TWICE while watching the 165 mm id32->id31 cable. This is the acceptance test for the hardest route in the robot.
Camera focus and ToF range check against the 1.0 m target.
tools: BUS-01 bench rig: 7.4 V / 3 A limited supply with shunt, 16-device scan script
risks: THIS IS THE LAST GATE BEFORE THE SHELLS. Every fault found after this point costs a shell removal at minimum and a full teardown at worst.
A duplicate ID discovered here cannot be fixed on the bus - the chain must be split. Budget a limb teardown when it happens.
A far-ankle voltage more than 0.550 V below the HAT is a crimp, not a design fault; do not accept it as normal.

The XL330 datasheet input range is 3.7-6.0 V and this robot runs the servos at a 6.6-8.2 V pack. Whether that is a stock part over-spec, a regulated bus or a custom variant is CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §3.4). Put a meter on a servo VDD pin on the first article and record what you see.

stations.name: Shell close (cosmetic and structural)
operations: Fit left_shell and right_shell in the SHL-01 clamshell, which holds them at their placement offsets (left pos (4.000, 0.000, -17.579), right (4.000, -0.500, -17.500), both quat wxyz 0.707107 about +z, spec/mesh-placements.json).

TORQUE THE NECK-REACTION CLUSTER FIRST, and to the shell schedule. Both shells carry an identical mount cluster centred at mesh (+-16.250, -22.000, 50.000): four Ø2.200 clearance holes on a 12.000 mm cross (y -16/-22/-28, z 44/50/56), each with a Ø5.008-5.035 boss standing 1.006 mm proud, four Ø1.48 x 1.01 locating pips on a Ø6.14 diamond, and a Ø9.9-10.1 central relief. Transformed, that lands at world (26.0, +16.5, 152.42) and (26.0, -16.75, 152.50) - the SAME x and z as the neck_pitch joint axis (26.0, 14.5, 152.4) to 0.02 mm. THE SHOW SHELLS CARRY THE NECK AND HEAD MASS through 2.250 mm walls and four M2 screws per side.
FLAG: the y offset differs by 1.75 / 2.25 mm between the cluster and the published joint axis. Confirm on a real unit before any shell tooling is cut.

Join the two halves: ONE screw. left_shell has Ø2.200 x 2.000 clearance at (1.000, 42.000, 52.500); right_shell has Ø1.600 x 4.700 self-tap at (-2.650, 42.000, 52.500) - same y, same z. That is the ONLY shell-to-shell fastener in either feature file. Alignment is a single ~1.0 mm wide tongue on the left shell crossing the split by 1.950 mm.
Close the head: bottom_head_shell 4 x M2, top_head_shell 3 x M2 [community].
HOLD: top_head_shell is quarantined at Station 1. Do not close a head with a shell made from the 91.7595 x 122.6900 x 46.3361 mm simulation mesh.

Shell walls measured this session: left_shell median 2.2522 mm, modal 2.250 (2387 of 5659 thin intervals), p5 1.4335, p1 1.1139; right_shell median 2.2617, modal 2.250 (2352/5710), p5 1.4289, p1 1.1054. These are the walls the neck reacts into.
tools: hex 1.5 mm ball driver for the buried shell screws
risks: ONE SCREW AND ONE 1 mm TONGUE hold the two body halves together. There is no second fastener. Over-torque that screw and the Ø1.600 self-tap in a 2.250 mm wall strips - and the shell is the cosmetic face of the product.

M2 pull-out in printed PLA is CANNOT DETERMINE by this repo's own record: ce-connections/threaded-m2/iterations/v0.0.1/connection.json carries 'pla_pullout_N': null. The shell joint is therefore unqualified until the Station-2 coupon test runs.

The colourway shells are STRUCTURAL, not decorative. Treating them as trim - handling them loose, torquing them by feel, allowing a cracked boss to ship - puts the head-and-neck load path in the hands of a part nobody is inspecting.
Closing the shells before Station 11 passes is the most expensive mistake on the line.

stations.name: Final functional test, state-of-charge and pack-out
operations: Fit the NP-F550 into the power_support cradle against the banana contacts. Servo bus VDD is battery-direct through the HAT.

Re-scan the bus on pack power. Confirm all 16 devices and the 6.6-8.2 V mapping to 0-100 %. Note that at a 6.6 V pack the farthest ankle reads 6.050 V - 0.550 V below the empty threshold robotd reads FROM the servos, so the far ankle trips 'empty' first by that margin (wiring/drop.json). That is expected, not a fault.
Run the STAND keyframe: trunk z = 120 mm; hip_roll -5 deg, hip_pitch -26.24 deg, knee -0.28 deg, ankle +25.95 deg, neck_pitch +20 deg, head_pitch +20 deg, both legs mirrored (SPEC.md §2).
Run a walk test. Reference: out/sim/report.md records 0.79 m in 8 s with no fall on the stock policy.
Weigh the unit. Target 737.2 g summed MJCF inertial mass; product spec 780 g store / 'under 800 g' press kit.
Measure the zero-pose envelope: 144.1 x 141.0 x 264.0 mm (x x y x z), feet 13.5 mm above ground.
Set the pack to <= 30 % SoC for shipping and pack out.

Battery compliance: the pack is 7.2 V x 2.6 Ah = 18.72 Wh, i.e. <= 20 Wh per cell and <= 100 Wh per battery - 'small' in every transport regime; ship under UN3481 PI967 Section II (docs/PRODUCTION.md §3.1).
tools: walk test lane with a 1.0 m marked run
risks: A fault found here is a shell-off event at best.

MATERIAL VERDICT, unresolved: out/stress/report.json's PASS results (shin SF 7.510634, ankle SF 2.021028, hip-bracket SF 6.424036 at 20 N) all rest on a CLASS-TIER PLA allowable. cecad/data/materials.json's own rule is that 'a class figure may FAIL a check but may NOT PASS one', and it warns that 'PLA CREEPS under sustained load at ROOM temperature. A static FEA says nothing about a bracket that has held 3 kg for a month.' Every structural part in this robot is under permanent static load. These PASS verdicts are NOT releasable as PASS.
microduck-upper-leg-left FEA is CANNOT DETERMINE (gmsh failed: invalid boundary mesh, overlapping facets on surface 350). The thigh - which carries the entire leg - has no stress result at all.
No FEA exists for trunk_base, power_support, motor_support or either show shell. The shells carry the head; the FEA set does not include them.

jigs.name: SVO-ID-01 - single-servo ID programming cradle
jigs.purpose: Make a duplicate Dynamixel ID physically impossible to create. Every XL330 ships as ID 1 at 57600 bps; two on one port cannot be told apart or reprogrammed.
jigs.description: A milled or printed block with one 20.2 x 34.2 x 26.2 mm pocket (XL330 case is 20.0 x 34.0 x 26.0 mm per the ROBOTIS emanual), back face down, with a 2.0 mm relief under the Ø16.0 x 3.0 horn boss. A spring toggle clamp bears on the case top through a 25 mm nylon pad at roughly 20 N - enough to free both the operator's hands, not enough to load the case. The bench carries EXACTLY ONE JST EH 3-pin socket on a 150 mm pigtail to a single U2D2-class half-duplex TTL adapter: there is no second socket, so a second servo cannot be connected. Downstream of the cradle is a 15-slot closed-cell foam tray, each slot silk-screened with its ID and joint name (10 R-hip-yaw ... 34 mouth). A programmed servo is labelled with a 6 x 12 mm polyester ID label and may only be laid in its own slot. The tray is the poka-yoke; the single socket is the interlock.

jigs.name: BRG-PR-01 - bearing press set (press, 2 punches, 4 nests)
jigs.purpose: Seat 11 x 22x16x4 and 3 x 15x10x3 bearings into printed seats without loading the balls, without cocking a ring that is only 48.75 % supported, and with a recorded force for every press.
jigs.description: A 1-tonne arbor press with a 0-1000 N load cell in the ram and a data-logging readout. PUNCH P1 (inner-race driver, 22x16x4): hardened steel tube, OD 17.80 +-0.02, ID 16.40 +-0.02, length 25 mm, face flat to 0.01 mm - it contacts only the inner ring (bore Ø16.0, race OD 18.0 per ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4) and its bore clears the Ø16.0 boss it is pressing onto. PUNCH P2 (outer-race driver, 15x10x3): tube OD 14.80 +-0.02, length 25 mm; its ID must be set from the measured outer-race land on the first physical ring - that land is CANNOT DETERMINE from the decimated mesh, starting value 13.00 mm. NEST N1 (yaw2roll / bearing_roll): cradles the part with the Ø16.0 x 1.95 boss vertical and uses the part's own Ø19.0 x 0.5 shoulder as the hard stop; a dial indicator on a 25 mm arm confirms the ring's far face lands at boss root + 4.000 mm. NEST N2 (hip-bracket): two seats 90 deg apart, roll_bearing_seat at mesh (17.5, -16.55, 0) and pitch_bearing_seat at (40.45, 0, 0), both Ø16.0 x 1.95. NEST N3 (ankle): presents the Ø15.0 x 2.3 pocket upward through its Ø16 x 0.5 45-deg lead-in, with the Ø14.0 window shoulder at x 32.5 as the stop - and a mechanical limit that STOPS the ram once the ring is 0.700 mm proud, because a 3.000 mm ring in a 2.300 mm pocket is meant to stand proud to clear the shin's Ø10.0 x 3.2 boss. NEST N4 (yaw-roll-motion): the Ø16.0 x 4.0 boss, the one full-width seat. PRESS FORCE IS CANNOT DETERMINE and must not be guessed: both connection records carry grip_N = null and the interference is unmeasured on both sides (printed seat, unnamed ring). The press is therefore run to a DISPLACEMENT stop, and the load cell RECORDS rather than commands. The first 30 units set the +-3 sigma control limits.

jigs.name: REAM-01 - bore reaming and tapping fixture
jigs.purpose: Bring every bridged, oval, undersize printed bore back to size before anything is pressed into it. docs/DFM.md makes this mandatory, not optional.
jigs.description: A drill-press sub-table with a hardened bushing plate over interchangeable part nests. BUSHING B1: Ø15.0 H7 machine reamer for the ankle pocket, approached from the OUTBOARD face at x 35.3 through the Ø16 x 0.5 lead-in, stop collar at 2.30 +0.10 mm. BUSHING B2: Ø5.37 for the upper-leg hip-pitch and knee axle bores at (70.5, 0, 0) and (70.5, 22.0, 35.777). BUSHING B3: Ø19.0 for the bearing_roll, upper_leg_rigidity_plate and trunk_base windows. BUSHING B4: M2 tap-drill Ø1.70 guide for the 20 measured Ø1.6 tap positions. The nests share the same four-dowel pattern as LEG-01 and TRK-01 so a part is datumed once. The Ø10.0 shin boss is checked with a ring gauge, not reamed - it is a boss, not a bore.

jigs.name: INS-01 - heat-set insert station
jigs.purpose: Put an M2 brass insert into a printed boss square, to depth, without cracking the boss or melting the wall behind it.
jigs.description: A benchtop arbor with a temperature-controlled soldering iron in the ram, an M2 insert tip and a hard Z stop. Temperature setting rule (published, Prusa Research M2-short insert page, read 2026-09-02): 'use the print temperature for the specific filament that was used to print the plastic part increased by 10 degC - 20 degC.' The absolute value is CANNOT DETERMINE from this repo - out/print/slice.json records the preset name ('Bambu PLA Basic @BBL H2S' / 'Bambu TPU 85A @BBL H2S') but no nozzle temperature. Dwell, depth and boss hole diameter are set by a first-article DOE: install 10, section 5, measure the melt collar, and pull/torque the other 5 on TQ-01. The station shares REAM-01's nest plate. It is a hard requirement for power_support (thinnest structural walls in the robot: modal bins 0.950 / 1.450 / 1.850 / 1.950 / 2.050 mm, p1 0.7675) - an insert set too hot there will blow through the wall.

jigs.name: LEG-01 - leg build nest, left and right
jigs.purpose: Hold the thigh datumed on its own two axle bores for the whole leg sequence, so the operator never re-datums between the servo drop-in, the bearing press, the rigidity plate and the shin joint.
jigs.description: A machined-aluminium or printed-PETG nest holding the upper leg with its servo cavity opening upward (the same orientation it printed in). Two Ø5.35 dowels pick up the reamed Ø5.37 axle bores - hip-pitch at mesh (70.5, 0.0, 0.0) and knee at (70.5, 22.0, 35.777), 42.000 mm apart, which is the thigh's own measured link length. A third and fourth dowel pick up pin_3 / pin_4 at (64.5, +-8.0, 22.5) to fix rotation. One quarter-turn toggle clamps the back plate. A hinged sub-arm swings in to hold the shin at the knee axis while its 4 horn screws go in. Left and right nests are mirror parts and are colour-coded, because upper_leg_left and upper_leg_right are dimensionally identical (28.0000 x 47.6594 x 60.9966 mm both) and cannot be told apart by measurement.

jigs.name: TRK-01 - trunk build fixture
jigs.purpose: Support a 1.000 mm plate over its whole footprint while four servos, a battery cradle and a PCB are screwed to it.
jigs.description: A flat plate with a 57.000 x 36.000 mm pocket that carries trunk_base face up and supports it EVERYWHERE, because the structural plate is 1.000 mm thick - the 3.0000 mm in out/verify/mech_dims.json is the bounding box over four 2.000 mm locating pins (direct probe this session: material along z at (x -28.000, y 0.000) runs 16.500-17.500; at (-25.500, -9.500) it runs 16.500-19.500). Four Ø1.9 blind sockets 2.1 mm deep at (+-9.5, -9.5) and (+-25.5, -9.5) receive the printed Ø1.80->1.59 pins so they are SUPPORTED, never loaded. Two Ø19.0 reliefs under the hip-yaw holes let the servo horn hubs pass. A hinged upper arm holds the hip-yaw servos while their screws go in. NOTE: docs/PARTS.md row 1 and SPEC.md §4.1 both call this a '3 mm plate' and both should be corrected to '1.000 mm plate, 3.000 mm bbox over the pins'.

jigs.name: HEAD-01 - head mechanism turntable
jigs.purpose: Present motor_support at any angle so the camera, ToF, HAT, Radxa and speaker can all be reached without lifting or re-clamping the sub-assembly.
jigs.description: A 360-degree turntable with 30-degree detents carrying a plate that picks up motor_support's own four Ø2.7 base_screws pattern at (-30, 23), (9.35, -23), (-30, -16) and (19, 19.5). A Ø15.0 half-round cradle on a stand-off supports the lens tube at (y 0.0000, z 7.4995) so the M12 holder is never cantilevered off the arch while the camera board is screwed to it. The whole plate is ESD-dissipative and bonded to the mat, because this fixture lives inside the EPA.

jigs.name: STAND-01 - final assembly stand
jigs.purpose: Hold the robot by its chassis, not by its show shells, with the legs free to hang and the head free to be posed.
jigs.description: A post with a saddle that grips the trunk structure between the hip-yaw axes at world z ~115 mm, holding the feet 60 mm clear of the bench so the legs hang and the ankle/knee joints can be cycled. Two articulated magnetic arms hold the head at any pitch while head cables are dressed. HARD RULE built into the fixture geometry: nothing clamps the shells. The shells are the load path for the whole neck and head (their mount clusters land within 0.02 mm of the neck_pitch axis in x and z) and a fixture that grips them is loading the exact feature the product depends on.

jigs.name: HARN-01 - harness cut, crimp and label board
jigs.purpose: Cut 21 cables to 21 measured lengths that are not interchangeable, and label them so the chain order is recoverable after the shells go on.
jigs.description: A 600 x 400 mm board with pin-pairs set at the exact cut lengths from wiring/CABLES.md: 35, 60, 50, 165, 35, 120, 40, 65, 125, 20, 95, 40, 65, 125, 20, 95, 35, 70, 15 and 340 mm - 1615 mm total. Each lane is silk-screened with the cable id (dxl-hat-id34 ... dxl-id13-id14, tof-hat, spk-hat, csi-radxa-camera, bat-hat), the conductor (AWG 21) and the connector (JST EH 3-pin, EHR-03 housing, SEH-001T-P0.6 contact; JST-SH 4-pin 1.0 mm for tof-hat). The 165 mm lane (dxl-id32-id31) and the 340 mm lane (bat-hat) are marked in red - they are the two cables that cross 520 and 720 degrees of joint rotation respectively. A crimp pull-tester sits at the end of the board: 3 crimps per shift pulled to destruction and logged, because no retention figure for this housing exists in any source here. The mic-hat lane is left EMPTY and labelled CANNOT DETERMINE.

jigs.name: BUS-01 - Dynamixel bus test and EEPROM rig
jigs.purpose: Prove the chain before a single shell screw goes in, and catch the duplicate-ID and bad-crimp faults while they are still cheap.
jigs.description: A bench supply set to 7.4 V with a 3 A current limit and a series shunt, plus a host running the scan. The scan asserts EXACTLY sixteen devices - 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 200 - at 1 Mbps Protocol 2.0 on /dev/ttyS2, and STOPS THE UNIT on any duplicate, any absentee, or any device still answering at 57600. It then reads back return_delay_time = 0, baud_rate = 3, pwm_slope = 255, shutdown = 52 on all fifteen servos, and logs present_input_voltage (address 144, u16, 0.1 V/count) per device - the farthest ankle must sit within 0.550 V of the HAT, which is the AWG 21 result in wiring/drop.json. It also reads the imu_to_dxl 12-byte block at register 124 and refuses an all-zero quaternion as 'not ready' rather than as a fault.

jigs.name: ROM-01 - range-of-motion and cable-sweep gauge
jigs.purpose: Drive every joint to its published MJCF limit with the robot still open, and watch the two cables that will otherwise fail in the field.
jigs.description: A set of printed protractor plates and hard stops, one per axis, that clip to the link and read against a pointer on the parent body. Limits, from SPEC.md §3: hip yaw -25...+30 (left) and -30...+25 (right); hip roll +-22; hip pitch +-90; knee +-90; ankle +-90; neck pitch -90...+60; head pitch +-90; head yaw +-170; head roll +-25; mouth -5...+30. The head-yaw plate is the important one: the +-170 degree sweep is run TWICE with the operator's eyes on the 165 mm dxl-id32-id31 cable, which carries 90.8 mm of slack across 520 degrees of crossed rotation, and once with the 340 mm bat-hat lead watched across its 720 degrees. Passing this gauge is the gate to Station 12.

jigs.name: TQ-01 - torque calibration and coupon station
jigs.purpose: Replace the derived M2 torque recommendation with a measured one, and keep it measured every shift.
jigs.description: A rotary torque transducer (0.02-1.0 N.m, 1 % FS) with a motorised driver, plus a coupon rack. Coupons are printed on the SAME machine, preset and orientation as production (Bambu H2S 0.4 nozzle, 0.20 mm Standard) in each material, and reproduce each real boss geometry: the shell's Ø1.600 x 4.700 self-tap in a 2.250 mm wall; power_support's Ø1.55 x 7.8 and Ø1.60 x 4.0 taps in a 0.950-2.050 mm wall; a heat-set insert boss; and a scrap XL330 horn. Every shift: drive 5 coupons of each class to failure, record the STRIPPING torque, and confirm every preset driver on the line is set at or below 50 % of the LOWEST value of the shift. Log it. Until this station has run, every torque figure in the fastener schedule is a derivation, not a measurement, and it is labelled as such.

jigs.name: SHL-01 - shell close fixture
jigs.purpose: Give the two body halves the second datum the parts themselves do not have, and get the neck-reaction cluster torqued before the single joining screw.
jigs.description: A clamshell that holds left_shell and right_shell at their true relative placement - left at (4.000, 0.000, -17.579), right at (4.000, -0.500, -17.500), both quat wxyz 0.707107 about +z (spec/mesh-placements.json) - and closes them on a linear slide so the halves meet parallel. This matters because the ONLY alignment feature between them is a single ~1.0 mm wide tongue on the left shell that crosses the mesh x = 0 split by 1.950 mm, and the ONLY fastener is one screw: left_shell Ø2.200 x 2.000 clearance at (1.000, 42.000, 52.500) into right_shell Ø1.600 x 4.700 self-tap at (-2.650, 42.000, 52.500). The fixture sequences the operator: the four neck-reaction screws per shell go in FIRST (the cluster at mesh (+-16.250, -22.000, 50.000), four Ø2.200 on a 12.000 mm cross with Ø5.008-5.035 bosses standing 1.006 mm proud), then the single joining screw. It also gauges the 1.75 / 2.25 mm y discrepancy between that cluster and the published neck_pitch axis - a discrepancy that must be resolved on a real unit before any shell tooling is cut.

fasteners.spec: M2x6 socket head cap, ISO 4762 (or the ROBOTIS M2x6 TAP shipped in the servo box)
fasteners.location: Servo horn joint - bracket to XL330 horn face, 4 per joint on the Ø12.000 mm bolt circle at (+-6, 0) and (0, +-6). 15 horn joints: L/R hip yaw, hip roll, hip pitch, knee, ankle; neck pitch, head pitch, head yaw, head roll, mouth.
fasteners.basis: PATTERN MEASURED: cecad.meshfeatures on reference/pollen-microduck-rl/assets/xl330.stl, 2026-09-01 - Ø16.0 x 3.0 discs both faces, 4 x Ø1.6 x 6.0 tapped on a Ø12.000 PCD; brackets carry the mirror pattern (shin 4 x Ø2.2 on an 8.486 mm square = 8.486 x sqrt(2) = 12.001 mm circle). SCREW SUPPLY: ROBOTIS ships 6 x M2x6 TAP with every XL330, so 15 servos give 90 free. TORQUE: no ROBOTIS figure exists - emanual.robotis.com/docs/en/dxl/x/xl330-m288/ carries no tightening-torque spec (read 2026-09-02); ce-connections/spline-xl330-horn records clamp_torque_Nm: null. 0.15 N.m is DERIVED, not measured - see the M2-into-printed-boss row for the derivation - and must be replaced by the TQ-01 coupon result on a scrap horn.

fasteners.spec: M2x8 socket head cap (or the ROBOTIS M2x8 TAP shipped in the servo box)
fasteners.location: XL330 case through its own 4 x Ø2.0 through-holes into the printed housing - upper leg cups, shin, yaw2roll/bearing_roll (via Ø2.4 + Ø4.84 x 2.2 counterbore), neck plates, yaw_roll_motion (4 x Ø2.5 at (-22.5, +-8) and (7.5, +-8)), motor_support saddles.
fasteners.basis: MEASURED: xl330.stl carries 4 x Ø2.0 case holes per servo (community hole-fit, research/raw/community/replica_fastener-reconstruction.en.md, cross-checked against the servo's own M2 mounting pattern). 15 x 4 = 60. SUPPLY: ROBOTIS ships 10 x M2x8 TAP per servo = 150 free per robot-set. Torque as above - DERIVED.

fasteners.location: Structural positions 0-3 mm deep - the shallow end of the 79 measured Ø2.2 clearance holes.
fasteners.basis: [COMMUNITY, mesh-derived, flagged] research/raw/community/replica_fastener-reconstruction.en.md: 'Depths: 51 at 0-3 mm, 24 at 3-5 mm, 4 at 8-12 mm.' Lengths are INFERRED FROM HOLE DEPTH, not measured - the source flags this itself ('Screw lengths are ranges inferred from hole depth, not measured values'). Pollen publishes no screw list. Corroboration only: the Dev Pack contains '1 x Screw Pack' and '1 x Screwdriver' - one screw family.
[COMMUNITY, flagged] Same depth histogram as above: 24 holes at 3-5 mm.
[COMMUNITY, flagged] Same depth histogram: 4 holes at 8-12 mm.

fasteners.location: The 20 measured Ø2.7 / Ø2.8 positions. Identified ones: upper-leg hip_pitch_axle and knee_axle (Ø5.37 x 2.5 counterbore over Ø2.4->2.8 through) x2 per thigh = 4; shin 'ankle' Ø2.7 through with Ø5.5 counterbore for the ankle axle x2; motor_support base_screws 4 x Ø2.7 through the 1.7 mm base plate at (-30,23), (9.35,-23), (-30,-16), (19,19.5). Remaining 10: CANNOT DETERMINE.
fasteners.basis: [COMMUNITY, flagged] docs/PARTS.md §5: 'Ø2.7 / 2.8 | 20 | M2.5 clearance'. CAPPED AT 0.30 N.m because at M2 THE SCREW, NOT THE INSERT, BECOMES THE LIMIT - general electronics practice puts M2 machine screws at 0.15-0.30 N.m (low-authority corroboration only). No published M2-into-plastic torque table exists: Tappex's own 'Application Torque' page publishes no numbers, EJOT publishes no public M2 table, and ce-connections/threaded-m2 records tightening_torque_Nm: null and pla_pullout_N: null. results.summary:
MICRODUCK PRODUCTION ASSEMBLY LINE — 13 stations, 70–140 min attended per unit (midpoint 98.8 min), bottleneck at Station 2.

REPO: /Users/leifrydenfalk/dev/ce-workshop/ce-designs/microduck. Primary sources read: out/verify/mech_dims.json (47 meshes, bbox truth), out/stress/report.json, out/print/PRINT.md + out/print/slice.json (real BambuStudio 02.08.02.61 numbers: PLA 218.29 g / 9.93 h over 32 pieces, TPU 26.20 g / 2.41 h over 4), docs/PARTS.md, docs/BOM.md, docs/PRODUCTION.md, docs/DFM.md, docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md, SPEC.md, spec/mesh-placements.json, wiring/CABLES.md + drop.json, ce-connections/{press-fit-bearing-22x16x4, press-fit-bearing-15x10x3, threaded-m2, spline-xl330-horn, press-fit-sole-foot}/connection.json, ce-parts/*/iterations/*/cad/interfaces.json, ce-assemblies/microduck/iterations/v0.0.1/{manual/MANUAL.md, joints.json}, /Users/leifrydenfalk/dev/ce-workshop/ce-cad/cecad/data/materials.json.

THE LINE. 1 Incoming inspection & kitting (4.0 min) · 2 Printed-part preparation: ream/drill/tap/heat-set (18.5) · 3 Servo ID + EEPROM, one servo at a time (8.0) · 4 Harness cut & crimp (6.0) · 5 Leg sub-assembly ×2 (9.6) · 6 Trunk & hip (10.8) · 7 Neck (3.9) · 8 Head mechanism (4.4) · 9 Head electronics, in an EPA (3.9) · 10 Final marriage & harness routing (13.0) · 11 Electrical bring-up + bus scan + ROM, SHELLS OFF (5.5) · 12 Shell close (3.2) · 13 Final test, SoC, pack-out (8.0).

CYCLE-TIME BASIS AND WHY IT EXCEEDS THE REPO'S OWN NUMBER. Times are built from the Boothroyd-Dewhurst element bands already used in docs/production/compliance-and-assembly.md §"assembly labour" — handling 1.5–4.0 s/part, non-screw insertion 2.0–3.0 s, bearing press 2.0–3.0 s, machine screw 5.0–8.0 s, heat-set insert 10 s, cable end 6–10 s, harness routing 3–8 min, all ÷ 0.85 plant efficiency [S43][S44] — applied to this line's own per-station part and screw counts. My total is 70–140 min against docs/PRODUCTION.md's 36–101 min, and the whole difference is Station 2: that DFA count charged only "heat-set inserts, if used: 0–60" and no reaming, drilling or tapping time at all. Post-processing printed parts is the single largest station on this line at 12.6–24.4 min, it sets the takt, and it is the strongest quantitative argument in the repo for either moulding the shells or redesigning the press-fit and tapped features out.

SCREW COUNT RECONCILED. I recounted the community per-part table (research/raw/community/replica_fastener-reconstruction.en.md) and get 138 structural Ø2.2 clearance positions against their stated ~146. Add the 60 XL330 case screws (4 × Ø2.0 per servo) and the build is ≈198 screws, which lands on docs/PRODUCTION.md's 206 figure. The 60 horn screws are already inside the 138 — do not add them twice. ROBOTIS ships 6 × M2×6 TAP and 10 × M2×8 TAP with every XL330, so 15 servos supply 90 + 150 screws free, covering most of the build.

TORQUE — THE HONEST ANSWER. No published M2-into-plastic torque table exists. I checked: Tappex's own "Application Torque" page publishes no numbers; EJOT publishes no public M2 table; the ROBOTIS XL330-M288-T emanual carries no tightening-torque spec (read 2026-09-02); and this repo's own ce-connections/threaded-m2 records tightening_torque_Nm: null and pla_pullout_N: null. My recommendation is DERIVED and labelled as such: anchor on CNC Kitchen's instrumented M3-in-PETG torque-out (heat-set insert 3.0 N·m, direct screw into printed plastic 1.0 N·m, Helicoil 1.0 N·m; pull-out 119 kg ≈ 1167 N), scale M3→M2 by d²·Lₑ with engagement scaled to diameter ((2/3)³ = 0.296), then apply the 50 %-of-stripping rule. That gives 0.15 N·m into a printed PETG boss and 0.44 N·m into a heat-set insert, the latter CAPPED AT 0.30 N·m because at M2 the screw becomes the limit before the insert does. PLA stays CANNOT DETERMINE — no PLA figure exists anywhere I could source. Station TQ-01 replaces all of this with a measured stripping torque every shift on coupons printed on the production machine, and the line's preset drivers are held at ≤ 50 % of the lowest value of the shift.

BEARINGS — PRESS DIRECTION IS THE FINDING. Press force is CANNOT DETERMINE and stays null: both connection records carry grip_N: null, the printed seats have no ISO class and neither ring has a vendor sheet. But the DIRECTION is fully determined and it contradicts the current manual. All eight measured 22×16×4 seats on the shelf are Ø16.0 INNER-RACE BOSSES; no Ø22 outer-race housing exists on any part. I re-probed trunk_base.stl this session and the hip-yaw feature is a Ø19.000 mm hole centred at mesh (17.5, −2.0) — a Ø22 ring cannot enter it, so MANUAL.md Step 1.1 ("Press the two 22×16×4 hip-yaw idler bearings into trunk_base") is not executable as written; those rings seat on yaw2roll's / bearing_roll's Ø16.0 × 1.95 boss against its Ø19.0 × 0.5 shoulder. Press on the inner ring, always, for the 22×16×4 — and on the OUTER ring for the 15×10×3 at the ankle, whose seat is a Ø15.0 × 2.3 pocket. Engagement is 48.75 % on the 22×16×4 (1.95 mm boss, 4.0 mm ring, 2.05 mm overhanging) and 76.7 % at the ankle, where 0.700 mm of proud ring is deliberate clearance for the shin's Ø10.0 × 3.2 boss.

TRUNK_BASE THICKNESS RESOLVED. Direct probe: material along z at (x −28.000, y 0.000) runs 16.500–17.500 = 1.000 mm; at a pin location (−25.500, −9.500) it runs 16.500–19.500 = 3.000 mm. The structural plate is 1.000 mm; the 3.0000 in mech_dims.json is the bounding box over four 2.000 mm locating pins. docs/PARTS.md row 1 and SPEC.md §4.1 both say "3 mm plate" and both should be corrected. The TRK-01 fixture must support the full 57 × 36 mm footprint accordingly.

SERVO IDs AND THE DUPLICATE-ID RISK. Every XL330 ships as ID 1 at 57600 bps with Return Delay Time 250 (emanual, read 2026-09-02), and EEPROM writes require torque disabled. There is one bus and one port ("There is no second bus and no second port", rdesign:23-38). Two servos answering to one ID make sync_read return garbage and make neither addressable — you cannot rename either while both are on the chain, so the fix is to split the chain physically, i.e. disassemble the limb. Station 3 therefore programs one servo at a time on a bench with exactly ONE socket (interlock by construction), writes ID + baud_rate 3 + return_delay_time 0 + pwm_slope 255 + shutdown 52, reads every register back, drives the servo to position 2048 and leaves it there, labels the case, and lays it in its own slot in a 15-slot silk-screened tray (poka-yoke). A servo bolted to a horn while off 2048 clips that joint's range and costs four M2 down a counterbore to fix.

CABLES. One chain, 1 Mbps, 16 devices: HAT→id34(35)→id33(60)→id32(50)→id31(165)→id30(35)→imu200(120)→ splits to id20(40)→id21(65)→id22(125)→id23(20)→id24(95) and id10(40)→id11(65)→id12(125)→id13(20)→id14(95); plus tof-hat 35, spk-hat 70, csi 15, bat-hat 340. 1615 mm total, AWG 21 (worst HAT→ankle drop 0.550 V, PASS at both 8.2 V and 6.6 V). The two cables that decide the robot are dxl-id32-id31 at 165 mm (crosses head_yaw ±170° + head_pitch ±90° = 520°, of which 90.8 mm is slack) and bat-hat at 340 mm (crosses 720° of neck/head joints, 125.7 mm slack, carrying pack current). Strain relief: a tie-down within 15 mm of every JST EH connector on the STATIC side of each joint, service loops on the parent-body side with the loop plane perpendicular to the joint axis. mic-hat is CANNOT DETERMINE and stays an empty lane on the harness board.

ESD. Every semiconductor in the head is HBM 2 kV — the lower boundary of ANSI/ESDA/JEDEC JS-001 Class 2: TLV320AIC3104 HBM ±2000 V and CDM ±1500 V (SLAS510G §8.2 p.7), VL53L5CX HBM ±2 kV (DS13754 Table 13 p.17), BMI088 HBM 2 kV (Table 7 p.12), LSM6DSV16X HBM 2 kV (§4.5 Table 9 p.19) — all transcribed verbatim in this repo's own ce-parts ledgers. Run Stations 9, 11 and 13 inside an EPA per ANSI/ESD S20.20: wrist-strap system 0.8–1.2 × 10⁶ Ω (Table 3), verified and logged daily per ESD TR53; dissipative worksurface 1 × 10⁶ to 1 × 10⁹ Ω; boards in shielded bags until they are on the mat; no tape peeling, compressed air, PS foam or common bubble wrap inside; 30–70 % RH logged. An IONIZER over the head bench is not optional — the shells and brackets are printed insulators that cannot be grounded, and the CDM ±1500 V on the codec means it is the charged board touching ground that kills it, not the operator's finger.

FOURTEEN STEPS WHERE A MISTAKE COSTS DISASSEMBLY. (1) Duplicate or unset servo ID — split the chain, open the limb. (2) Servo bolted to a horn while off position 2048. (3) Bearing pressed on the wrong ring — brinelled races, and it still turns so it ships. (4) Bearing pressed without bottoming on its shoulder — 2.05 mm of unsupported ring cocks. (5) Bearing omitted at neck_pitch (0, 20.793, −14.5) or at either yaw_roll_motion seat — full head teardown. (6) yaw_roll_motion's two bearings fitted mirrored: they sit at −16.0 and +18.0, NOT symmetric, and 2.000 mm of head-roll axis error reads only as a head that leans. (7) A cable routed on the wrong side of a joint — tears at the first ±170° yaw sweep. (8) bat-hat routed on the wrong path. (9) Shells closed before the Station 11 bus scan and ROM test. (10) Thread stripped by over-torque — on a shell that is cosmetic scrap. (11) trunk_base's Ø1.80→1.59 printed pins sheared by an out-of-square mating part. (12) Wrong ankle revision (ankle_left Y 36.5000 vs ankle_l_v1 Y 46.4981, a 9.9981 mm difference) — found at the walk test. (13) Radxa/HAT 40-pin header mated one row or column off — both boards scrap, silent until Station 11. (14) imu_to_dxl fitted rotated — its mount quaternion [0.7071, 0, 0.7071, 0] is a calibration constant, and a rotated board makes the robot limp when upright.

FIVE THINGS THIS PLAN REFUSES TO PAPER OVER. (a) top_head_shell from the simulation mesh (91.7595 × 122.6900 × 46.3361 mm) does not match the product's domed head — quarantined at Station 1, no tooling released. (b) The battery mesh is np_f970 (38.6085 × 20.5755 × 70.8086) while the documented pack is NP-F550 class — gauge a real cell before freezing the power_support cradle. (c) The compute mesh is a Pi Zero 2 W placeholder; the Radxa Zero 3W shares the 65 × 30 mm footprint but its hole pattern, connector positions and Z height are CANNOT DETERMINE, so the head-electronics fit is UNVERIFIED. (d) The three custom PCBs (Robot HAT, imu_to_dxl v2, banana contact) have no design files — Stations 9, 11 and 13 cannot be released and this is the line's critical path. (e) Materials: out/stress/report.json's PASS verdicts (shin SF 7.510634, ankle SF 2.021028, hip-bracket SF 6.424036 at 20 N) all rest on a class-tier PLA allowable, and materials.json's own rule is that a class figure may FAIL a check but may NOT PASS one; microduck-upper-leg-left is CANNOT DETERMINE (gmsh failed, overlapping facets on surface 350) so the thigh has no stress result at all; and no FEA exists for trunk_base, power_support, motor_support or either show shell — the shells that, by this session's measurement, carry the entire head and neck through 2.250 mm walls and eight M2 screws. Recommendation: PETG (the only grade-tier printed material on the shelf) for every load-path part; PLA only for cosmetics.

TWO REPO CORRECTIONS THIS WORK OWES BACK. out/verify/mech_dims.json is STALE for motor_support (records rebuilt:false; ce-parts/microduck-motor-support/component.json is v0.1.0 verdict PASS, refcheck r6 p95 0.363/0.456 mm, bbox delta 0.00 mm per axis, 6/6 features matched) — re-run the verify pass. And ce-assemblies/.../joints.json resolves only 5 of 14 joints; the nine unresolved sides are the same nine the line's fixtures have to locate by hand.

QUALITY PLAN — Microduck (Pollen Robotics rebuild), rev A, 2026-09-02. Scope: incoming inspection for every bought and printed item, in-process gates at every assembly station, and a 35-test end-of-line functional acceptance sequence with an explicit PASS/FAIL/CANNOT-DETERMINE gate and a named failure action on every line.

SOURCES OF TRUTH. Dimensions: out/verify/mech_dims.json (47 meshes, FreeCAD Mesh.BoundBox, mm to 4 dp). Mass/time per printed piece: out/print/slice.json and out/print/PRINT.md (BambuStudio 02.08.02.61 via ce-slice 0.1.0, the slicer's own result.json — 218.29 g PLA / 9.93 h over 32 pieces, 26.20 g TPU / 2.41 h over 4, grand total 244.49 g / 36 pieces / 12.35 h). Structure: out/stress/report.json (PLA, 20 N design load = 2x the ~9.4 N slow-walk single-leg peak on a 737 g robot; shin SF 7.511 PASS, hip-bracket SF 6.424 PASS, ankle SF 2.021 PASS, upper-leg CANNOT DETERMINE — gmsh "Invalid boundary mesh (overlapping facets) on surface 350", no volume meshed). Joint limits and home pose: ce-assemblies/microduck/current/joints.json and spec/test-plan.json id_map. Registers and gates: spec/test-plan.json (MD-TST-001 rev A) against emanual.robotis.com/docs/en/dxl/x/xl330-m288/ (read 2026-09-02) and Pollen's Apache-2.0 runtime (model.rs, bus.rs, imu.rs, robotd.toml). Jigs: out/jigs/jigs.json. Cables: wiring/CABLES.md (22 cables, 1615 mm over the 21 with a length). Station gates that already exist: MANUFACTURING-PLAYBOOK.html §6.

TOLERANCE BASIS, stated once. (1) Printed parts carry NO drawing tolerance class — the only sourced dimensional acceptance in this repository is SPEC.md §8: bbox within 1.5 mm per axis and p95 two-way surface distance <= 1.0 mm against the reference mesh, and 1.0 mm is explicitly "the decimation error of their export … the floor". Every printed-part bbox gate below is that 1.5 mm/axis band applied to the mech_dims.json reference figure. (2) Bearing seats have NO tolerance class and NO vendor sheet: ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4 records rating.grip_N = null and reference_speed_rpm = null, and the interference is refused as CANNOT DETERMINE ("printed PLA seats have no ISO class and the unnamed ring no vendor sheet"). The incoming gauge reading IS the tolerance record, and the seat is graded functionally (hand to 1 mm, then the press). (3) M2 screw torque into a printed PLA boss: CANNOT DETERMINE — no source states one; the playbook quotes a zinc-plated steel M2 figure only "as the ceiling that proves the point". Torque is set by a calibrated driver whose value is established on scrap bosses at first article and recorded, not asserted here. (4) Servo electrical figures are ROBOTIS vendor values; every gate number in the EOL list is marked in its own text as vendor-derived or as a decision of the plan.

FIVE THINGS THIS PLAN REFUSES TO PAPER OVER. (a) top_head_shell (91.7595 x 122.6900 x 46.3361 mm, out/verify/mech_dims.json) does not match the product's compact domed head in the photographs — it is QUARANTINED at incoming; no head tooling and no head-shell lot is released against this geometry, and EOL test 35 (mass) will read high while it is fitted. (b) The battery mesh is np_f970 (38.6085 x 20.5755 x 70.8086 mm) while every document says NP-F550 class — the cradle gauge, not the name, decides the lot. (c) The compute mesh is pcb__raspberry_pi_zero_2_w (65.0 x 1.6 x 30.0 mm); the documented host is Radxa Zero 3W (also 65 x 30 mm) — incoming verifies the device tree string radxa,zero-3w, not the mesh. (d) Two ankle revisions exist (ankle_left/right Y = 36.5000 vs ankle_l_v1/r_v1 Y = 46.4981/46.4973 mm, delta 9.9981 mm) — a HARD BLOCK at incoming, because the defect surfaces only at the walk test and costs a full leg teardown. (e) Robot HAT, imu_to_dxl v2 and the banana contact PCB have NO published design files: their incoming inspection, and therefore EOL tests 1-7 and 14-20, CANNOT RUN until those boards are designed, fabricated and given a board-level test fixture. That is the critical path for the whole line, and no gate below pretends otherwise.

WHAT THE PLAN CANNOT GATE, AND WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Battery runtime has no numeric gate (published claim is "~1 h", press kit; no measured figure exists — EOL 33 records it and the gate is behavioural). The walk gate 0.594 m in 8.0 s is 75 % of our SIMULATED 0.7925 m (out/sim/report.md, walk_ours, MuJoCo 3.12.0, Pollen's alpha_walking.onnx, vx 0.25 m/s, 50 Hz, max tilt 4.11 deg, no fall) — no real robot has ever been walked in this repository, and the 75 % is a decision, not a measurement; replace it with the measured mean minus three standard deviations after the first five units. Servo supply (raw 6.6-8.2 V pack against the XL330's 3.7-6.0 V rating) is the open question EOL 4 exists to close. Per-joint servo-sign inversion has no published table; EOL 9 is where the first unit produces one.

DC current clamp or shunt, >= 25 A — servo-rail current during walking; 15 x vendor stall at 5.0 V = 22.05 A, so the instrument must not be the limit
Oscilloscope, >= 100 MHz, one 10x probe — bus signal integrity at 1,000,000 bps on a 16-device multidrop line; needed only when the roll-call finds intermittent devices
USB-C 5 V supply with a current readout — EOL 34 (which port powers, whether the pack charges in situ)
I2C host with i2c-tools (the robot's own Radxa serves) — SN-01/02/03 register work at 0x18, 0x19, 0x29, 0x68 on I2C3
White 88 % reflectance target, matte, >= 200 x 200 mm — the ToF gate is stated against ST's own 88 % white target and is invalid against any other surface
Steel rule and/or laser distance meter, 1 mm resolution — ToF reference distances and the walked distance (the +/- 7 % ToF gate at 500 mm is +/- 35 mm, so the reference must be far better)
Digital inclinometer, 0.1 deg — levelling the walk surface; the walk gate is a distance in 8 s and a sloped bench moves it
USB measurement microphone or a laptop mic with an FFT tool — audio loopback; the fitted speaker and microphone have no manufacturer part number in any source, so the gate is functional, not acoustic
Bluetooth gamepad, Xbox-style layout — padd drives whatever pad connects; deadman, walk, get-up and mouth tests

Baud 3 = 1 Mbps and Return Delay 0 are the two that MUST be set: 250 counts x 16 devices = 8 ms = 40 % of a 20 ms tick, so a bus that has not had it cleared cannot hold 50 Hz
