inprocess.check: Battery state of charge set for the shipping configuration; insert seated so the pack cannot contact
inprocess.limit: <= 30 % SoC is MANDATORY where spare packs travel in the same outer box (PI 966 Section II) and RECOMMENDED only for a battery installed in the robot (PI 967 Section II). The insert must hold the pack off its contacts, or the pack ships unseated — the robot has no power switch, so the insert IS the safety measure and it is a regulated part

inprocess.check: Wh marking, labels and paperwork match the configuration; finished box weighed
inprocess.limit: 18.72 Wh (7.2 V x 2.6 Ah), cell 9.36 Wh — small lithium-ion in every regime, above the 2.7 Wh button-cell exemption. Marks per configuration; on a mismatch, DO NOT RELEASE TO THE CARRIER. Target finished-box mass: Pollen's own Shopify shipping weight is 1200 g against a 780 g robot; our target is CANNOT DETERMINE until a box design exists — record the measured mass

eol.test: EB-01 · Pre-power continuity and short check. Four resistances with no power anywhere: BAT+ to GND at the banana contact PCB output; HAT 5V (header pin 2) to GND (pin 6); HAT_3V3 to GND at the Stemma J5; SERVO_V (pin 2) to GND (pin 1) at the HAT's bus header. Servo bus UNPLUGGED, no battery, no supply
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: every measured resistance > 100 ohm. FAIL: any resistance < 10 ohm. CANNOT DETERMINE: 10-100 ohm — a low but non-zero reading is an inrush-capacitor charge path on some rails and a fault on others. The 10/100 ohm split is a DECISION of this plan; no source states an expected cold resistance for these nets, because the Robot HAT and banana PCB are unpublished
eol.on_failure: FAIL: do not power. Trace the short before a 2S pack finds it. CANNOT DETERMINE: identify which net it is from the schematic before applying power — and if there is no schematic, the unit does not proceed

eol.test: EB-02 · First power-on behind a current limit. Bench supply at 7.400 V, limit 0.500 A, in place of the pack at the banana PCB output. Servo bus unplugged, camera and ToF unplugged. Enable and watch 5 s
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: the supply stays in constant-voltage for 5.0 s and the settled current is recorded to 0.001 A. FAIL: the supply enters constant-current at 0.500 A. No quiescent-current figure exists for an assembled Microduck in any source — THIS TEST RECORDS IT FOR THE FIRST TIME. The 0.500 A limit is a decision of the plan, above a booting Radxa (which specifies a 5 V/2 A adapter but states no idle draw) and far below anything that damages a board
eol.method: Bench PSU with current readout; DMM
eol.on_failure: Power down immediately and return to test 1

eol.test: EB-03 · Rail survey. Probe every rail at the pin that needs it, with sensors reconnected one at a time and the current re-checked after each
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: every banded rail inside its band, recorded to 0.001 V. Bands: HAT 5V 4.750-5.250 V (+/- 5 % — a DECISION of this plan; Radxa states only 'DC +5V' / '5V/2A' with no tolerance in any fetched document); HAT_3V3 3.130-3.470 V (tightest fitted part: VL53L8CX AVDD Table 12; BMI088 2.4-3.6 V, TLV320AIC3104 2.7-3.6 V and LSM6DSV16X 1.71-3.6 V are all wider); HAT_1V8 codec DVDD 1.525-1.950 V; ToF CORE_1V8 1.62-1.98 V (VL53L8CX only — N/A, not FAIL, on an L5CX); ToF IOVDD 1.08-1.32 V or 1.62-1.98 V per strapping. FAIL: any banded rail outside. CANNOT DETERMINE: camera-module 3V3 at FPC pin 15 and ToF IOVDD where the module's strapping is unknown — record the value and say so; it is not a pass
eol.on_failure: FAIL: do not fit the pack. KNOWN OPEN on our own reconstruction — in electronics/robot-hat/ the 1.8 V codec rail dead-ends on test point TP1 (decision D5) and no 1.8 V source is designed in, so a board built from our files reads 0 V there. That is a defect of the board design, not of the unit; fix the board

eol.test: EB-04 · SERVO_V — the measurement that settles the open question. With all 16 devices connected and torque off, measure pin 2 (VDD) to pin 1 (GND) at the HAT end of cable 1 (dxl-hat-id34) and at the far ends (id24 and id14), at supply 8.200 V and again at 6.600 V. Compute both drops
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: the measurement is taken at all four points at both settings and recorded to 0.001 V — EITHER RESULT IS A VALID OUTCOME. FAIL: the measurement is not taken, or the HAT-to-farthest-ankle drop exceeds 0.550 V at 8.200 V in. 0.550 V is our own harness model's total drop for AWG 21 at 8.2 V with 1 A per moving servo (wiring/CABLES.md, cecad.harness.check_drop, PASS at every hop) — this test is what checks the model
eol.method: DMM to 0.001 V through the bus-tap harness fixture
eol.on_failure: If SERVO_V tracks the supply, production Microducks run stock XL330s 0.6-2.2 V above the vendor's 6.0 V maximum — consistent with robotd clearing the Input Voltage Error bit of Shutdown(63) — and the servo derating question goes to engineering with the measurement attached. If SERVO_V sits inside 3.7-6.0 V, the HAT regulates and docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §3.4 must be corrected. On an over-limit harness drop, re-check the crimps and the conductor gauge before touching the design

eol.test: EB-05 · Bus standby current. Total input current at 7.400 V with all 16 devices connected and idle, minus the test-2 board-only figure
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: the derived servo-rail standby is >= 0.255 A AND test 6 finds all 16 devices. FAIL: fewer than 16 devices answer. CANNOT DETERMINE: current below 0.255 A while 16 devices answer — the current path and the data path disagree. 0.255 A = 15 x 17 mA vendor Standby Current (no test voltage is stated for it); the imu_to_dxl board's own standby is CANNOT DETERMINE, so this is a floor, not a window
eol.method: Bench PSU readout or DMM in series
eol.on_failure: Do not proceed on a CANNOT DETERMINE. On a missing device, go to test 6 and treat it as a wiring fault

eol.test: SV-03 · Bus roll-call at 1,000,000 bps. robotd STOPPED (two writers on one UART corrupt each other's replies). Broadcast-ping Protocol 2.0 on /dev/ttyS2
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: exactly {10,11,12,13,14,20,21,22,23,24,30,31,32,33,34,200} answer and nothing else. FAIL: any ID missing, any duplicate, or any unexpected ID. CANNOT DETERMINE: an ID that answers intermittently — that is a wiring or bus-integrity fault, not a pass
eol.method: robotd's own init path or a Dynamixel scan tool, daemon stopped
eol.on_failure: Missing or duplicate: back to Station 3 (servo ID). Intermittent: take it to the >= 100 MHz scope on a 16-device multidrop line before anything else is blamed

eol.test: EB-06 · Pack fitted — what the robot reads against what a meter reads. Bench supply removed, a charged pack fitted, robotd running, torque off. Meter the pack terminals; read every servo's Present Input Voltage(144) at 0.1 V per count
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: |V_meter - V_register| <= 0.100 V. FAIL: the difference exceeds 0.100 V. CANNOT DETERMINE: the register reads nothing ('batt not read yet' means no tick has completed). 0.100 V is the register's OWN quantisation — a vendor figure, not a choice. Note there is no fuel gauge and no ADC anywhere on this robot: robotd reads the pack THROUGH the servos
eol.on_failure: FAIL: the robot's only self-knowledge about its battery is wrong — do not ship. Fix the power path before any walk test, because the empty-shutdown behaviour depends entirely on this reading

eol.test: SW-01 · Version agreement. `robotctl version` plus a listing of /opt/robot/daemon/releases/ and /opt/robot/daemon/current
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: every daemon runs the installed release and robotctl version prints no disagreement; current points at the intended release. FAIL: any disagreement
eol.on_failure: Re-run the installer and re-check. A daemon serving old code after an update looks exactly like a bug in the fix you just shipped — never diagnose anything else until this passes

eol.test: SV-05 · Home-pose verification — fifteen joints against fifteen published numbers. `robotctl robot init` ON THE STAND (init moves every joint), settle 3 s, log 100 ticks, compare mean Present Position(132) per joint
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: every joint within +/- 11 counts (+/- 0.967 deg at 0.0879 deg/count) of its expected home count. Expected counts, computed as 2048 + rad x 4096/(2 pi) from DEFAULT_POSITION: ID 20 2048.0, 21 1991.1, 22 1749.5, 23 2044.8, 24 2343.3, 30 2275.6, 31 2275.6, 32 2048.0, 33 2048.0, 34 2048.0, 10 2048.0, 11 2104.9, 12 2346.5, 13 2051.2, 14 1752.7. FAIL: any joint outside +/- 11 counts. CANNOT DETERMINE: a joint that lands the SAME DISTANCE THE WRONG SIDE of 2048 — that is an inversion, not a calibration error. 11 counts = 1.0 deg = the amplitude of the backlash twins the policies were trained against, the tightest published mechanical uncertainty on this joint
eol.method: robotctl robot init; robotctl monitor --json --hz 50 for 100 ticks
eol.on_failure: Outside the band: the horn was fitted at the wrong index (a mis-index is 1024 counts and cannot hide) — go back to Station 5/6/7 and re-index against the horn-zero gauge; robotd NEVER writes Homing Offset, so no register can rescue it. On a suspected inversion: record it, escalate to engineering, and the plan gains a MEASURED per-joint inversion column. No published source gives an inversion table, and this is expected on the first unit

eol.test: SV-04 · Free travel and mechanical stops. Torque off, on the stand, move each joint slowly by hand end to end while logging Present Position(132)
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: every joint reaches both ends of its MJCF range with no hard stop inside it and no discontinuity in the sweep. Ranges in degrees / encoder counts: hip_yaw L -24.981/+30.023 (1764/2390), hip_yaw R -30.023/+24.981 (1706/2332); hip_roll +/-22.002 (1798/2298); hip_pitch, knee, ankle, head_pitch +/-90.012 (1024/3072); neck_pitch -90.012/+59.989 (1024/2731); head_yaw +/-169.997 (114/3982); head_roll +/-24.981 (1764/2332); mouth -5.002/+30.000 (1991/2389). FAIL: a hard stop inside the range, or a discontinuity (a slipping horn or a dead encoder segment)
eol.on_failure: A hard stop inside the range is mechanical: an unreamed pivot, a bearing on the wrong race, or the WRONG ANKLE REVISION. Back to Station 5/6/7 — this is where a v1 ankle that slipped every earlier gate finally shows

eol.test: Powered per-joint range-of-motion sweep. With torque on and the robot ON THE STAND, command each joint individually to its MJCF minimum, hold 1.0 s, then to its maximum, hold 1.0 s, logging Present Position(132) and Present Current(126). Head_yaw is swept last, with the loom watched
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: every joint reaches both commanded ends within +/- 11 counts and no servo's Present Current(126) reaches Current Limit(38) = 1750 mA at either end. FAIL: an end not reached, or current at the limit (the joint is binding), or an Overload latch (Shutdown(63) bit 5). NOTE the software will not protect the joint here: robotd's safety clamps targets to the ACTUATOR's travel (+/- pi), not per-joint limits — the real joint limits live in the MJCF, so this test is the only thing standing between a commanded angle and a printed part
eol.method: Direct Protocol-2 goal-position commands with robotd stopped, or a scripted single-joint sweep; robotctl monitor --json --hz 50 logging
eol.on_failure: Current at the limit: stop the sweep immediately, back the joint off, and treat it as a mechanical bind (unreamed bore, wrong bearing race, pinched loom). Never raise Current Limit(38) to get past it

eol.test: SV-06 · Mouth travel (ID 34). Drive to MOUTH_CLOSED, hold 2 s; to MOUTH_OPEN, hold 2 s; read Present Current(126) at both ends; cycle 10 times
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: -5.000 deg and +30.000 deg both reached within +/- 11 counts, Present Current below 1750 mA at both ends, drift over 10 cycles <= 11 counts. FAIL: either end not reached, or current at the limit (the jaw is binding). MOUTH_CLOSED = -5 deg and MOUTH_OPEN = +30 deg are verbatim runtime constants; the mouth is in NO policy (MOUTH_INDEX = 9 is deliberately skipped in every 14-action alpha net), so nothing else on this line exercises it
eol.on_failure: Binding: the TPU lip is proud — trim or re-print (jaw_soft 8.4376 mm, soft_mouth_top 3.2762 mm). Drift: the horn is slipping — re-index

eol.test: EB-07 · Running current in three states. A: torque off, bus idle, 10 s. B: home pose held, no command, 30 s. C: walking at vx 0.25 m/s for 8.0 s. Pack current and every servo's Present Current(126) logged simultaneously in all three
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: no servo's Present Current(126) reaches Current Limit(38) = 1750 mA in any state, and the pack current mean and peak are RECORDED for all three states (no vendor figure exists between standby 17 mA and stall 1.11/1.47/1.74 A at 3.7/5.0/6.0 V, and above 6.0 V no vendor figure exists at all — which matters directly if test 4 found SERVO_V on the raw pack). FAIL: any servo at 1750 mA, or any Overload latch. CANNOT DETERMINE: the clamp cannot be fitted — then the per-servo register readings stand alone and the pack figure stays unmeasured
eol.method: Current clamp or shunt >= 25 A; robotctl monitor --json --hz 50
eol.on_failure: A servo at the limit is a mechanical bind or a servo fault: identify it by ID from the log and go back to that joint. Until this test runs on real units, EVERY rail budget in this repository rests on an assumption, including the 1 A-per-moving-servo basis behind the harness drop model

eol.test: SN-01 · I2C3 roll-call. `i2cdetect -y -r 3` after the overlays are applied and the board has rebooted
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: 0x18 (codec), 0x19 and 0x68 (BMI088), 0x29 (ToF) all answer. FAIL: 0x18 absent (codec) or 0x29 absent (ToF). CANNOT DETERMINE: 0x19/0x68 absent — the head IMU is a BMI088 on OUR reading of Pollen's overlay, which itself calls it 'dormant', 'unused but still connected'; whether a production head carries it at all is CANNOT DETERMINE. Record the absence; DO NOT fail the unit on it
eol.method: i2c-tools on the robot's own Radxa
eol.on_failure: 0x18 or 0x29 missing: check the Stemma J5 lead and the 10 k pull-up pair R12/R13 before blaming the part. Note 0x52 in Pollen's other documents is the same ToF address written 8-bit

eol.test: SN-02 · BMI088 identity. Read ACC_CHIP_ID at 0x19 register 0x00 and GYRO_CHIP_ID at 0x68 register 0x00
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: 0x1E and 0x0F respectively (BMI088 datasheet BST-BMI088-DS000-19 Rev 1.9 01/2024, §5.3.1 p.26 and §5.5.1 p.37 — reset values). FAIL: either byte differs — a different part is fitted. CANNOT DETERMINE: the addresses did not answer in test 14
eol.on_failure: A different byte means a different part: quarantine the board and identify what is actually fitted before any further sensor test

eol.test: SN-03 · BMI088 self-test, accelerometer and gyroscope, with the robot STATIONARY and LEVEL (the accel self-test superimposes on gravity, so the sheet requires static conditions). ACC_RANGE 0x41 = 0x03 (+/-24 g), ACC_CONF 0x40 = 0xA7, wait > 2 ms; positive 0x0D then negative 0x09 at ACC_SELF_TEST 0x6D with > 50 ms settling; then disable and RESET the device. Gyro: set bite_trig, poll bist_rdy, read bist_fail and the background bit
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: |positive - negative| >= 1000 mg on x, >= 1000 mg on y, >= 500 mg on z; gyro bist_fail = 0 and the continuous background test bit = 1. FAIL: any axis below its minimum, or bist_fail = 1. Every step and every number is the vendor's own procedure and Table 9, BST-BMI088-DS000-19 Rev 1.9 §4.6.1-4.6.2 pp.17-18
eol.on_failure: Replace the board. Reset the device after any self-test, because the self-test response affects interrupt generation

eol.test: SN-04 · Control IMU (imu_to_dxl, ID 200) — behavioural, the only IMU test a finished robot can take. Log 30 s upright and still; lay the robot on its right side, hold 5 s; rotate 90 deg about the trunk yaw axis, hold 5 s; read the stale-read counter
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: upright projected gravity z <= -0.98 with |x|,|y| <= 0.10; gravity follows every imposed rotation; stale reads = 0 over 30 s. FAIL: gravity does not follow a rotation, or the stale-read warning fires (25 identical 12-byte blocks in a row = 0.5 s). CANNOT DETERMINE: an all-zero quaternion at start-up — the SFLP table has not been written yet; robotd keeps the last good value and never snaps to identity, so wait for 25 live blocks (~0.25 s at 100 Hz) before judging. The 0.98/0.10 figures are DECISIONS of this plan; no source states a static-accuracy figure for the assembled robot
eol.on_failure: Replace the imu_to_dxl board. The stale count is the ONLY thing that catches the dangerous failure: a board that has stopped fusing keeps answering the bus, so nothing errors and the gravity vector holds a plausible attitude indefinitely — which is why it is in the gate, not in the notes

eol.test: SN-06 · ToF ranging against an 88 % white matte target normal to the beak at 200, 500 and 1000 mm, room lighting below 5 klx. Record the monitor's ToF header line (it names the sensor generation, the rate, the zones ranged and the near-far span) and the mean of the centre four zones over 30 frames at each distance. Then point at open space
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: at each distance >= 56 of 64 zones ranged and the centre-four mean within +/- 7 % of the reference (at 500 mm that is +/- 35 mm); open space shows '.' (measured, nothing in range), not 'x' (could not measure). FAIL: fewer than 56 zones, or a mean outside +/- 7 %. CANNOT DETERMINE: the header says 'no sensor:' — tofd is up and nothing answered. +/- 7 % = ST's +/- 5 % (8x8, 15 Hz, 201-4000 mm, 88 % white, dark) plus ST's own stated additional 1-2 % for PCB tilt and product housing; BOTH generations publish the same +/- 5 %, so which one ships (CANNOT DETERMINE) does not change the gate. 56/64 is a decision of the plan — Pollen's own example header shows 48/64 ranged in an ordinary room, so a full 64 must not be demanded
eol.method: 88 % white target rig + steel rule/laser; robotctl monitor, key 't'
eol.on_failure: 'no sensor': back to test 14. Zone shortfall: read the per-zone ST status codes from the theremin readout — robotctl monitor's grid is STRICTER than the theremin and marks anything outside status 5/9 as 'x', so a grid full of 'x' does not by itself mean the sensor is broken

eol.test: SN-07 · Camera capture and hardware encode. Confirm the sensor identity in dmesg; find the capture node BY CARD NAME (rkisp_mainpath — node numbers are not stable across boots); capture 10 frames of 720p NV12; encode a test pattern with mpph264enc and read the profile back through h264parse; confirm /dev/mpp_service and /dev/rga at 660 root:video with the user in `video`
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: dmesg reads 'imx219 2-0010: Model ID 0x0219, Lot ID …, Chip ID 0x0773'; the capture is EXACTLY 13,824,000 bytes (10 x 1280 x 720 x 1.5, NV12 — Pollen's own measured figure); h264parse negotiates profile=constrained-baseline. FAIL: any of the three. CANNOT DETERMINE: no /dev/video* at all — which is ALSO exactly what an unattached camera looks like
eol.method: dmesg; v4l2-ctl --stream-mmap --stream-count=10; gst-launch-1.0 with mpph264enc ! h264parse
eol.on_failure: No /dev/video*: check the CSI ribbon latch before blaming the overlay. Wrong byte count: do NOT switch to v4l2src — the rkisp driver hands it a 2-buffer pool, it requeues too slowly and drops every third frame (~20 fps from a 30 fps sensor). Never add videoflip to correct the upside-down mount: it cost 22 fps, 5522 RGA failures and 97 degC in one measured session

eol.test: SN-08 · Audio loopback. Confirm the card; play a 1000 Hz sine for 3 s through the codec; record 3 s from the codec's own capture device while the tone plays; FFT the recording; then ask the robot for its own voice with `robotctl quack`
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: peak within 1000 +/- 10 Hz, peak-to-median >= 20 dB, and `robotctl quack` sounds. FAIL: no peak at 1 kHz, or `robotctl quack` reports no voice bank. CANNOT DETERMINE: the codec answers on I2C but ALSA has no card — the I2S3 side is the suspect, not the I2C side. The 1000 +/- 10 Hz and 20 dB figures are DECISIONS of this plan: the fitted microphone and speaker have NO manufacturer part number in any source, the mic is analog on the codec's Mic3R PGA rather than a digital I2S part, and no amplifier is identified — so NO acoustic figure may be asserted and the gate is deliberately functional
eol.method: aplay -l | grep aic3104; speaker-test -D plughw:aic3104 -t sine -f 1000; arecord -D plughw:aic3104; FFT; robotctl quack
eol.on_failure: No ALSA card: check the I2S3 side — MCLK is a fixed-clock node at 12 MHz and the cpu-dai sysclk is 12.288 MHz (256 x 48 kHz), and whether MCLK comes from a crystal on the HAT or an SoC pin is CANNOT DETERMINE. `robotctl quack` is in the gate because a robot with no voice SAYS SO rather than printing a duck, which makes silence unambiguous

eol.test: SN-09 · NFC — NO TEST EXISTS. This line exists so the absence is on the record rather than missing from it
eol.pass_criterion: CANNOT DETERMINE, and that is the answer, not a gap. The press kit says 'two antennas, one in the head and one in the beak' and Pollen sells NFC tags and an NFC E-Ink 'Polaroid' tapped on the robot's head, but there is NO NFC code in the published runtime: a grep of duck-ipc-proto_lib.rs and research/microduck-elec-grep.txt returns 0 hits for nfc, pn532 and st25. No reader IC, no bus, no antenna geometry. Two candidates are datasheeted on our shelf and neither is confirmed: ST25R3916 (two single-ended antenna drives) and PN7150 (one antenna path)
eol.on_failure: n/a. What would settle it: a teardown identifying the reader IC and its bus, or a later release of pollen-robotics/microduck exposing an NFC service. Until then there is nothing to command and nothing to read back

eol.test: SN-10 · Camera-use indicator (REC) LED — NO TEST EXISTS
eol.pass_criterion: CANNOT DETERMINE. The press kit describes 'a dedicated camera-use indicator inspired by classic REC lights'; a source grep returns 0 hits — no GPIO, no driver, no LED class device is named anywhere in the published runtime
eol.on_failure: n/a. What would settle it: `ls /sys/class/leds` on a production board with the camera streaming, or a teardown tracing the LED to a header pin

eol.test: SW-02 · Health verdict. `robotctl health --json` with the joints POWERED (an unpowered bench board reporting unhealthy is the honest answer, not a failed build). Read the loop section beside the verdict: achieved rate, missed deadlines, bus errors, IMU stale counters, battery, servo and board temperature
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: healthy, with achieved rate >= 45.0 Hz and consecutive bus errors < 10 (robotd's own [update_gate] defaults: 45.0 Hz is 90 % of the 50 Hz target — 'loose enough not to trip on one slow tick, tight enough that a loop dropping every tenth cycle is not called healthy'; 10 errors because 'one dropped transaction is ordinary on a serial bus, a run of them means the bus is gone'). FAIL: unhealthy, or degraded with a reason naming the bus or the loop. CANNOT DETERMINE: degraded on an unpowered board — power the joints and re-run. Battery and motor temperature appear on the report but MUST NOT reach the verdict — Pollen's own rule
eol.on_failure: A reason naming the bus goes back to test 6 and the harness; a reason naming the loop goes to test 24

eol.test: SW-03 · Loop rate over a 300 s window at 50 Hz (~15,000 lines). Compute the achieved-rate distribution and the largest inter-tick gap
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: 5th-percentile achieved rate >= 45.0 Hz AND no inter-tick gap >= 500 ms. FAIL: either. 45.0 Hz is min_achieved_hz; 500 ms is stall_periods = 25 at 50 Hz ('a loop silent that long is genuinely gone'). The 5th percentile is a DECISION of this plan — robotd gates on its own computed achieved rate, and a percentile over a fixed 300 s window is the closest equivalent
eol.on_failure: A loop running at 60 % of target is alive, answers every request, and is badly broken — do not ship it. Check Return Delay Time(9) = 0 on all 16 devices first: 250 counts x 16 = 8 ms = 40 % of a 20 ms tick

eol.test: SW-04 · Policy load. Read the monitor's bottom border — it names the .onnx files loaded and whether a standing network is configured at all; confirm the 61-D alpha observation contract, not the 51-D legacy net (which is refused at load)
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: the border names the configured policies (alpha_walking.onnx, alpha_stand.onnx) and health is healthy. FAIL: the border reports a policy that would not load and health is unhealthy with the searched path named. CANNOT DETERMINE: policy.enabled = false — a LEGITIMATE configuration, healthy, holding whatever pose the robot started in; not a degraded state. Set it true before the walk block
eol.on_failure: A policy that will not load prints its own reason and the path it searched — fix the install, do not substitute a different policy. Note the alpha observation carries joint positions RELATIVE to DEFAULT_POSITION, which is exactly why test 9 must have passed first: a home-pose error is a constant offset on 14 observation slots

eol.test: SW-05 · Deadman. Drive forward on the floor, then kill padd while the stick is held forward; read the reason on the monitor; measure the time from the last pad packet to zero commanded velocity from the log
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: velocity zeroed within 500 ms and the robot is left STANDING, not limp. FAIL: the robot keeps walking, or goes limp. deadman_ms = 500, and Pollen's own reason: 'losing contact with a client should leave a biped standing, because standing is its safe state'. There is no stop button by design
eol.on_failure: A robot that keeps walking when its client dies does not ship. This is a safety gate, not a performance gate

eol.test: WK-01 · Stand and hold. Robot ON THE FLOOR (off the stand) on the levelled acceptance surface, pack charged above 7.500 V. `robotctl robot init`, then 30 s with no command. Mark and measure the mid-foot drift
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: no fall, maximum trunk tilt <= 10.0 deg, drift <= 50 mm over 30 s. FAIL: a fall, or tilt beyond 10.0 deg. SIMULATION REFERENCE (out/sim/report.md, stand_hold_ours, 4 s holding STAND): walked 0.003 m, max tilt 1.4 deg, trunk z 0.115 -> 0.116 m, no fall, 0 self-contacts. The 10.0 deg and 50 mm gates are DECISIONS of this plan, set far outside the simulated figures to leave room for sim-to-real transfer and a real floor; they are NOT measurements of any robot, and the first built unit's figures replace them
eol.method: robotctl robot init; monitor --json --hz 50; inclinometer; steel rule
eol.on_failure: Before suspecting the policy, re-check test 9 (home pose) and test 10 (free travel): a stand that drifts is usually a joint that is not where the policy thinks it is

eol.test: WK-02 · Walk acceptance — the headline test. Mid-foot on the start line of the 1200 mm run, policy enabled, left stick fully forward for 8.0 s at commanded vx 0.25 m/s. Measure the straight-line distance to the mid-foot at stick release; read maximum trunk tilt and the fall flag from the log
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: walked >= 0.594 m in 8.0 s AND no fall AND maximum trunk tilt <= 25.842 deg. FAIL: any of the three. CANNOT DETERMINE: the robot walks but the path curved off the run so the distance cannot be measured — re-run on a longer surface; a curved path is a real result and belongs in the log. BASIS: the 0.594 m gate is 75 % of our SIMULATED 0.7925 m (out/sim/report.md, walk_ours, MuJoCo 3.12.0, Pollen's alpha_walking.onnx, 50 Hz, timestep 0.005 s, decimation 4: 0.7925 m in 8 s, mean 0.1053 m/s, max tilt 4.11 deg, no fall, 0 self-contacts, max joint speed 5.74 rad/s at the left knee). The stock and swapped-mesh models produced BIT-IDENTICAL trajectories, so the reference is Pollen's physics, not ours. THE 75 % IS A DECISION, NOT A MEASUREMENT — no real-robot walk distance exists anywhere in this repository or in Pollen's published material. The 25.842 deg tilt gate IS derived: limp_fall_tilt_z = -0.90 and acos(0.90) = 25.842 deg, the tilt at which the daemon itself decides a fall has started
eol.method: Gamepad; levelled 1200 mm lane; steel rule or laser; robotctl monitor --json --hz 50; current clamp shared with test 13
eol.on_failure: DO NOT re-test at 0.15 m/s to get a pass. Our own velocity sweep on Pollen's stock model measured vx 0.05 -> 0.003 m, 0.10 -> 0.007 m, 0.15 -> 0.008 m, 0.20 -> 0.011 m, 0.25 -> 0.792 m, 0.30 -> 0.940 m, 0.40 -> 1.281 m in 8 s: everything below 0.25 sits inside the walking policy's stand-still band, and a robot that correctly stands still would read as a failure. A short walk goes back to the mechanical stations (home pose, ankle revision, sole friction, harness drag), not to the policy

eol.test: WK-03 · Walk repeatability. Repeat test 28 five times, returning to the start line between runs, WITHOUT recharging, recording pack voltage before each run
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: 5 of 5 runs meet the test-28 gate AND the spread of the five distances <= 0.150 m. FAIL: any fall, or any run below 0.594 m. The 0.150 m spread is a DECISION of this plan — no source publishes run-to-run variance for this robot, and our simulation is deterministic (stock and swapped models bit-identical), so it can offer none
eol.on_failure: A widening spread across the five runs with falling pack voltage is expected physics, not a defect: voltage_adapt is OFF by default, so effective servo stiffness tracks the pack as it sags and a five-run sequence walks progressively softer. Record the voltages; if the spread exceeds 0.150 m, report the voltage trend with it

eol.test: WK-04 · Get up. Sit then stand with DPad-Down, three cycles; lay the robot face down, release, let the standing policy recover it, three attempts; repeat face up, three attempts
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: 9 of 9 recover, each within 6.0 s, ending at trunk height >= 0.100 m and tilt <= 10.0 deg. FAIL: any attempt that does not recover within 6.0 s. SIMULATION REFERENCE: stand_from_sit_ours over 6 s ended at trunk z 0.116 m, max tilt 5.0 deg, no fall; stand_from_fold_ours ended at 0.116 m. The 6.0 s window is the simulated run length; the 0.100 m and 10.0 deg gates are decisions set below and above the simulated 0.116 m and 5.0 deg
eol.on_failure: Pollen's own note applies: the standing policy 'is a good stand-up-er and a bad faller' — from a STILL robot, face down or face up, it gets back on its feet cleanly, which is exactly the condition this test creates. A failure here is mechanical (a joint short of range, a snagged loom), not a policy tuning problem

eol.test: WK-05 · Limp-fall behaviour, over a soft landing area (this test deliberately drops the robot). Walk, tip past the trigger tilt by hand and let go; watch the state stream for safety.limp and the limp_fall / limp_pose labels; let it rest, then watch the pose ramp and the hand-back to the standing policy
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: limp_fall arms BEFORE ground contact, the robot arrives limp, ramps to the standing pose and stands, in 3 of 3 attempts. FAIL: the robot lands stiff (the policy fought the floor), or does not stand afterwards. CANNOT DETERMINE: limp_fall = false on this board — then the test does not apply and behaviour is the prototype's. Thresholds are robotd.toml [safety] verbatim: trigger past limp_fall_tilt_z = -0.90 (25.842 deg), still tipping, with a 300 ms extrapolation landing past -0.5 (60.000 deg), debounce 60 ms (three ticks at 50 Hz); then gain_limp = 50 until still (1.0 rad/s for 200 ms) or 1500 ms, then a 600 ms ramp at gain 160
eol.method: Gamepad; robotctl monitor --json --hz 50; soft landing area
eol.on_failure: Landing stiff means the predictive path did not arm — check that the IMU passed test 17 (a stale but plausible attitude is the failure mode this depends on) before touching [safety] thresholds

eol.test: WK-06 · Post-walk thermal. Immediately after the fifth walk of test 29, read Present Temperature(146) for all fifteen servos and the board temperature; repeat after 5 minutes of standing
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: every servo below 70 degC and no Overheating latch. FAIL: any servo at or above 70 degC, or any servo latched. 70 degC is Temperature Limit(31)'s initial value and the top of the vendor's operating range (-5 to +70 degC); Shutdown(63) = 52 as robotd writes it keeps bit 2 Overheating set, so the servo LATCHES rather than degrading quietly. Board temperature is a DESCRIPTION on the health report and may not reach any verdict
eol.on_failure: Identify the hot servo by ID and treat it as a bind at that joint. Separately record the SoC temperature: Pollen measured 95-97 degC and a throttle to 408 MHz when the camera pipeline did rotation in software, and the NPU duck detector runs at 2 Hz for the same reason — 'a thermal limit, not a preference'

eol.test: Battery runtime to graceful empty-shutdown. Start from a fully charged pack (meter reads 8.200-8.400 V), run a repeating duty cycle of 8.0 s walking at vx 0.25 m/s and 22.0 s standing until the runtime shuts the robot down. Log elapsed time, pack voltage (register 144) and the shutdown behaviour
eol.pass_criterion: PASS (behavioural, and this is the only gate this test can honestly carry): at the 6.60 V EMA (~10 s) the robot SITS DOWN GRACEFULLY and powers the board off — battery_empty_shutdown = true — and Select held 2 s does the same by hand. The elapsed runtime is RECORDED to 1 s. NUMERIC RUNTIME GATE: CANNOT DETERMINE — the only published figure is '~1 h' (press kit) with no duty cycle, no temperature and no method attached, and no measured runtime for any built unit exists. FAIL: the robot does not sit down and power off at the empty threshold, or it browns out and drops mid-stride (a hard reset instead of a controlled sit is a safety failure, whatever the runtime was)
eol.method: Charged pack; robotctl monitor --json --hz 50 logging register 144; stopwatch
eol.on_failure: A brown-out instead of a controlled sit points at the power path (test 3 rails, test 4 SERVO_V) or at register 144 disagreeing with the meter (test 7). What settles the runtime figure: the measured mean over the first five units under this stated duty cycle — then this line gains a real numeric gate and the '~1 h' claim can be checked

eol.test: EB-08 · USB-C behaviour with the pack fitted. With the pack fitted and the robot off, apply 5 V to the USB 2.0 OTG Type-C port; record VBUS, current drawn, and whether pack voltage rises over 10 min. Repeat on the USB 3.0 HOST Type-C port. Repeat both with the pack removed
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: all four cases measured and recorded (VBUS to 0.001 V, current to 0.001 A, pack voltage before and after 10 min to 0.001 V). FAIL: the board draws current on a port and does not come up. CANNOT DETERMINE: whether the robot charges in situ — this IS the expected verdict until a unit is measured. The overlay disables the PD controller at /i2c@fe5c0000/fusb302@22; its power-on defaults present Rd on both CC lines so any charger still gives 5 V
eol.method: USB-C 5 V supply with current readout; DMM
eol.on_failure: Record and escalate; do not design a charging claim around an unmeasured port. Note the shelf's reference 2S charger (MCP73213) needs roughly 8.7 V or more at its input, which 5 V USB cannot supply without a boost stage nobody has seen — so an in-robot 2S charge from USB-C is not supported by anything on the record

eol.test: Unit record and mass. Weigh the finished robot without packaging; confirm the log set under logs/<serial>/ is complete — every one of lines 1-34 has a recorded verdict (including every CANNOT DETERMINE), the 15 servo horn-zero offsets from Station 3, the bearing lot gauge record, the plate mass record and the printed-part slug/revision record
eol.pass_criterion: PASS: complete log set with a signed verdict on every line, AND finished robot mass < 800 g. FAIL: any missing line, or mass >= 800 g. BASIS for the mass bound: 'under 800 g' is the press kit's own published bound; the two other published figures are 780 g (store) and 737.2 g summed over the 15 MJCF inertial bodies. A precise target mass for OUR build is CANNOT DETERMINE (our printed set alone is 244.49 g sliced, plus 15 x 18 g servos = 270 g, plus battery, boards, bearings and fasteners — none of them weighed), so the reading is RECORDED against the 800 g bound and becomes the fleet's own record
eol.method: Bench scale 0.1 g; log audit against the test-plan line list
eol.on_failure: A missing line is not a pass by omission — the unit does not ship until the line is run or its CANNOT DETERMINE is recorded with what would settle it. Mass at or above 800 g: check first whether the quarantined simulation head shell (34.6097 g sliced, and the wrong geometry) has reached the unit

lines.item: Smart servo actuator, all 15 joints (hip yaw/roll/pitch, knee, ankle x2 legs; neck pitch, head pitch, head yaw, head roll, mouth)
lines.risk: HIGH — SINGLE SOURCE AND LONG LEAD. (a) ROBOTIS is the only manufacturer of the X330 family; there is no second-source drop-in at this 20.0 x 34.0 x 26.0 mm envelope with a 1 Mbps TTL half-duplex Protocol-2 bus. (b) The manufacturer's own shop publishes 'Lead Time: 40 days' (en.robotis.com XL Series listing, fetched 2026-09-02). (c) The largest EU stockist is on backorder — MyBotShop: 'Goods ordered. 144 expected on 02.10.2026', 11-13 workdays (fetched 2026-09-02). (d) NO distributor publishes a qty-100 or qty-1000 break, so the cost of 1,500 pcs (100 robots) or 15,000 pcs (1,000 robots) is CANNOT DETERMINE — this line was 49% of the ancestor Open Duck Mini v2 BOM (docs/BOM.md 5.2) and is the dominant cost unknown. (e) ELECTRICAL RISK: datasheet operating range is 3.7-6.0 V (emanual, fetched 2026-09-02) but SPEC.md 5 records the NP-F550 pack window as 6.6-8.2 V; a regulated 5.0 V servo rail is therefore mandatory. Whether Pollen regulates on the Robot HAT is CANNOT DETERMINE (no design files, docs/BOM.md P1). (f) Sub-variant risk: Pollen never names M288 vs M077; M288-T is a COMMUNITY assumption (SPEC.md 5, docs/PARTS.md row 32). Buying M077 by mistake gives 41% of the torque.
lines.alternate: ROBOTIS XC330-M288-T (item 902-0173-000) — the only mechanically and electrically drop-in alternate. IDENTICAL 20.0 x 34.0 x 26.0 mm body, identical 3.7-6.0 V window, identical Ø16 horn/idler face, same TTL bus. TRADE-OFF: stall torque 0.93 N.m @ 5.0 V vs 0.52 N.m (+79%, buys margin on the ankle whose FEA safety factor is the lowest at 2.02, out/stress/report.json); full metal gear + 2 bearings vs engineering-plastic case (better life against the printed-PLA horn bracket); BUT no-load speed drops 103 -> 81 rev/min (-21%, slows the gait), mass rises 18 g -> 23 g each = +75 g/robot = +10.2% on the 737.2 g MJCF mass (SPEC.md 2) which INVALIDATES the 20 N / 737 g load basis of out/stress/report.json and forces a re-run; and unit price rises $27.49 -> $103.39 at robotis.us = +$1,138.50 per robot over 15 joints. VERDICT: qualified as a fix for a torque or gear-wear failure found on test, NOT as a baseline. // SECONDARY, REJECTED: XL330-M077-T (902-0162-000, same $23.90/$27.49, same envelope, 77.5:1) — stall 0.215 N.m @ 5.0 V is 41% of M288; FAIL for hip/knee/ankle, defensible only for the mouth (ID 34). // TERTIARY, REJECTED: Feetech STS3215 (the Open Duck Mini v2 servo, EUR 14 ea, docs/BOM.md 5.2) — ~3.5x cheaper but body is ~40 x 20 x 35 mm against the XL330's 20 x 34 x 26 mm, so it fits NONE of the 9 printed servo pockets; requires a full mechanical redesign of trunk_base, yaw2roll, hip_l, upper_leg L/R, leg, neck, yaw_roll_motion and motor_support.

lines.mpn: MR1622-ZZ / ET2216 / ET2216ZZ / A2216 / SET2216 / DDA2216 (NMB) — all the same 16 x 22 x 4 ring; NO single ISO designation exists. Pollen's Onshape name is 'seeed_bearing configuration 22x16x4'; the actual vendor MPN Pollen buys is CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/PARTS.md row 33, section 3).
lines.risk: HIGH — NON-ISO SIZE. 16 x 22 x 4 is NOT a member of the ISO 6700/61700 series (6702 = 15x21x4, 6703 = 17x23x4); it is a specials size with no SKF / NSK / FAG / NTN catalogue listing found in this search. Every QUALIFIED stockist located is a miniature-bearing specialist in the UK or NZ; the only VOLUME price found is from an unqualified Chinese manufacturer at MOQ 1,000. At 11 per robot that is 1,100 pcs for 100 robots and 11,000 for 1,000 robots from a thin supply base. SECOND RISK — UNDEFINED FIT: measured OD 22.0000 x W 4.0000 mm (out/verify/mech_dims.json, mesh seeed_bearing__configuration__22x16x4, FreeCAD Mesh.BoundBox, 4 dp) and bore 16 from the Onshape configuration name. The XL330 horn/idler disc measures Ø16.0000 x 3.0000 mm with 4 x M2 taps on a Ø12.0000 PCD (ce-connections/spline-xl330-horn/connection.json, cecad.meshfeatures on xl330.stl, 2026-09-01). Bore 16 and disc Ø16.0 are the SAME NOMINAL — zero designed clearance — and NEITHER side carries an ISO 286 class, so the interference and the press force are CANNOT DETERMINE until calipers touch a real ring and a real as-printed seat (ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-22x16x4). Also note ring width 4.0 mm against a 3.0 mm disc land: 1.0 mm of the ring is unsupported.
lines.alternate: PRIMARY (drop-in): the SHIELDED build of the same ring — ET2216ZZ / MR1622-ZZ. Identical 16 x 22 x 4 envelope, adds two metal shields against PLA print dust and swarf. TRADE-OFF: slightly higher running drag and a small price premium; no geometry change. Stocked by NZ Miniature Bearings (NZD 5.90 + GST). // SECONDARY (geometry change, buys real supply security): ISO 6703 / 61703, 17 x 23 x 4 — the nearest CATALOGUED ISO size, second-sourced from NSK (via MISUMI), FAG, and US stock at Bearings Direct ($7.89 ea, https://bearingsdirect.com/6703-zz-ball-bearing-17x23x4-shielded-61703-2z1/). TRADE-OFF: +1.000 mm on bore and +1.000 mm on OD means every one of the 8 printed parts carrying a 22x16x4 seat must have its pocket and boss re-cut (trunk_base, yaw2roll, bearing_roll, hip_l, upper_leg L/R, neck_pitch, yaw_roll_motion), and because the XL330 idler disc is Ø16.0 a 17 mm bore needs a 0.5 mm-wall adapter sleeve or a redesigned idler boss. Buys multi-brand, multi-continent availability and published ISO 286 tolerance classes in exchange for a CAD change and a re-run of the refcheck (SPEC.md 8: p95 <= 1.0 mm, bbox within 1.5 mm/axis).

lines.mpn: 61700 (ISO) — also sold as 6700, MR6700, 61700J1, 61700R, 6700E, BA10-15, A-1510. Pollen's Onshape name is 'seeed_bearing configuration default'; the vendor MPN Pollen buys is CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/PARTS.md row 34).
lines.risk: MEDIUM. Supply itself is LOW risk: this IS a catalogued ISO size, stocked in the US (Bearings Direct, 722 pcs on hand, ships within 24 h) and the UK (Simply Bearings) with published qty ladders — 300 pcs for 100 robots is unremarkable. The risk is on OUR side, in three parts. (1) DESIGNATION AMBIGUITY: vendors disagree on the width behind the number '6700' — Bearings Direct sells '6700 ... 10x15x3 Open', while 123bearing lists '61700-2RS 10x15x4'. Adding seals can add 1 mm. THE PURCHASE ORDER MUST STATE 10.000 x 15.000 x 3.000 mm EXPLICITLY, not a part number alone. (2) THE SEAT WILL NOT ACCEPT THE RING AS PRINTED: docs/DFM.md lines 209-211 measures the ankle's Ø15 + Ø14 bearing seat as running ACROSS the layers (+Y build, 36.5 mm, 183 layers, 163 mm2 bridged) and reads it as 'bridged, oval, undersize at the top', verdict PRINTABLE-WITH-CARE, with the instruction verbatim: 'Ream it, or the 15x10x3 bearing will not seat.' Budget one Ø15.0 H7 reaming operation per ankle (x2 per robot) in the process plan. (3) REVISION AMBIGUITY: two ankle revisions exist in the reference set — ankle_left/right measure Y = 36.5000 mm while ankle_l_v1/ankle_r_v1 measure Y = 46.4981 / 46.4973 mm (out/verify/mech_dims.json, 4 dp). Which revision ships is undecided, and the bearing pocket sits in that dimension. Confirm the revision BEFORE the seat is toleranced. FIT: the reference pocket is Ø15.0 x 2.3 deep against a 3.0 mm ring = 77% engagement (deliberate, the proud 0.7 mm clears the shin boss); whether 77% holds the press is a bench question and is CANNOT DETERMINE (ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-15x10x3/connection.json).

lines.risk: MEDIUM — WEAR AND UNQUANTIFIED PRELOAD. The reference design bolts printed PLA brackets straight onto the XL330's own engineering-plastic horn with 4 x M2 cap screws; there is no metal horn in the loop. Three things are CANNOT DETERMINE and are named as such in ce-connections/spline-xl330-horn: (a) the CLAMP/STRIP TORQUE of 4 x M2 into tapped plastic — nothing has been twisted off on this bench, and the vendor's 0.52 N.m stall is the LOAD TO BEAT, not evidence; (b) the horn's CENTRE HUB, absent from Pollen's decimated mesh (cecad.meshslice, axis probe solid, 2026-09-02) while every consuming bracket carries a Ø5-6 mm centre bore — so the pilot diameter is unknown; (c) the internal output-spline CLOCKING. Bolt-pattern agreement between the two spellings on the consumer side is exact: the shin's 4 x Ø2.2 holes on an 8.486 mm square give a bolt circle of 8.486 x sqrt(2) = 12.001 mm against the horn's Ø12.000 — agreement to 0.001 mm. SUPPLY RISK: none as a separate line (it ships inside the servo); it inherits the XL330's 40-day lead time.
lines.alternate: ROBOTIS HNX330-N101 metal horn set (item 903-0314-000; 1 x metal horn + 6 x PHS M2x4 bolts; fits XL330 AND XC330). COST: $17.14 per joint at robotis.us; fitting all 15 joints costs $257.10 per robot, which is 72% of the entire servo line — so fit it selectively, on evidence from a torque/wear test, not by default. It does NOT change the Ø12.0 PCD or the M2 thread, so no bracket change is needed.

lines.risk: LOW — this line is priced for the DECISION, not the build. Quantity per robot in the reference design is ZERO: docs/PARTS.md and spec/mesh-placements.json show every joint bracket is a printed custom part (yaw2roll, bearing_roll, hip_l, upper_leg L/R, leg, ankle L/R, neck, neck_pitch, yaw_roll_motion) and the idler side is a 22 x 16 x 4 ball bearing, not the ROBOTIS plastic idler. (c) Bus-level risk: one 1 Mbps TTL half-duplex bus on /dev/ttyS2 carries all 15 servos plus the IMU slave (SPEC.md 5) — a single cable or connector failure anywhere on the chain takes the whole robot down. results.notes:
CURRENCY CONVENTION — READ FIRST. The schema's price fields carry no currency, so every distributor's `name` string states its currency and VAT basis explicitly, and the numbers are the PUBLISHED figures in that currency, unconverted. NO FX conversion has been applied anywhere in this document, because no dated FX rate was sourced and inventing one would break the measure/cite rule. Consequence: group_cost_qty1_usd and group_cost_qty100_usd are both null = CANNOT DETERMINE. See the roll-up below for exactly what IS and IS NOT priced.

ROLL-UP, qty 1 (one robot, single-unit prices, lowest published USD source per line):
- XL330-M288-T x15 @ $23.90 (ROBOTIS e-Shop) = $358.50
- Robot Cable-X3P 180 mm: 15 cables arrive inside the servo boxes at no extra cost; 1 spare needed for imu_to_dxl -> minimum buy is one 10-pack @ $19.00 = $19.00
- Bearing 10x15x3 x3 @ $4.86 (Bearings Direct) = $14.58
- Servo horns: $0 (integrated in the servo)
- FPX330-H101: $0 (qty 0 as designed)
- Bearing 16x22x4 x11 = CANNOT DETERMINE IN USD. No qualified distributor publishes this size in USD. In GBP ex-VAT it is 11 x GBP 10.44 = GBP 114.84 (Simply Bearings ET.2216-MB).
=> USD-PRICED SUBTOTAL, 5 of 6 lines: $392.08 per robot, PLUS 11 bearings priced only in GBP/NZD. The group total is therefore CANNOT DETERMINE, not $392.08.

ROLL-UP, qty 100 robots: CANNOT DETERMINE, and the reason is structural, not clerical. The dominant line — 1,500 XL330-M288-T — has NO published quantity break at any of the four distributors located. That single gap is worth ~91% of the group's qty-1 cost. What settles it: a written OEM/bulk quote from ROBOTIS. Per the brief no supplier has been contacted, so it stays null. The two bearing lines DO have published ladders and can be costed at volume today: 1,100 x 16x22x4 falls in Simply Bearings' 999+ tier at GBP 7.31 ex-VAT (GBP 8,041 for 100 robots, GBP 80.41/robot); 300 x 10x15x3 falls in Bearings Direct's deepest published tier, 50+ at -15% = $4.131 ($1,239.30 for 100 robots, $12.39/robot).

QUANTITY-PER-ROBOT PROVENANCE (all from the repo, not assumed): XL330 x15 — docs/PARTS.md row 32 and docs/BOM.md B1 and SPEC.md 5, cross-checked against the 15 joint IDs in SPEC.md 3 (10-14, 20-24, 30-34). Bearing 22x16x4 x11 — docs/PARTS.md row 33 and section 3, with all eleven placements named. Bearing 15x10x3 x3 — docs/PARTS.md row 34 and section 3 (ankle_left, ankle_right, jaw_soft). Cables 15-16 — docs/BOM.md B2 and docs/PARTS.md line 124; taken as 16 here. Horn faces 15 driven (30 discs total: the XL330 carries an identical Ø16 disc on both the horn and the idler side).

DIMENSIONAL TRUTH USED (out/verify/mech_dims.json, generated 2026-09-02, FreeCAD Mesh.BoundBox, reference metres x1000, quoted to 4 dp):
- mesh `xl330`: 29.0000 x 20.0000 x 34.0000 mm. The datasheet BODY is 20.0 x 34.0 x 26.0 mm (emanual, fetched 2026-09-02); the 29.0000 mm axis is the 26.0 mm body plus the two Ø16 horn/idler discs. The two do not contradict — do NOT design a pocket to 29 mm and expect a 26 mm body to fill it.
- mesh `seeed_bearing__configuration__22x16x4`: 22.0000 x 22.0000 x 4.0000 mm (OD and width measured; bore 16 comes from the Onshape configuration NAME, not from the mesh).
- mesh `seeed_bearing__configuration_default`: 15.0000 x 15.0000 x 3.0000 mm; bore Ø10.0000 measured separately by cecad.meshfeatures and frozen in evidence/bearing-15x10x3-geometry.json.
- XL330 horn face (cecad.meshfeatures on xl330.stl, 2026-09-01): disc Ø16.0000 x 3.0000 mm at x = ±13.0000; 8 tapped holes Ø1.6000 x 6.0000 deep on a Ø12.0000 PCD, 4 per face.
TOLERANCE BASIS: none of these carry a tolerance. They are bounding-box and feature measurements off Pollen's own DECIMATED meshes, and the decimation error is the floor — SPEC.md 8 sets the project's acceptance at p95 surface distance <= 1.0 mm both ways and bbox within 1.5 mm per axis, and that 1.0 mm floor is the honest uncertainty on every dimension above. NO bought part in this group carries a declared ISO 286 fit class on either side of any seat (ce-connections/press-fit-bearing-15x10x3 and press-fit-bearing-22x16x4 both record this as CANNOT DETERMINE), so press force, grip and retention are unmeasured. ISO 286-1/-2 grading is available in ce-cad's compat.py the moment a class is declared; declaring those classes is a REQUIRED action before any bearing is ordered in volume.

FIVE THINGS THE TEAM MUST DECIDE BEFORE ANY MONEY IS COMMITTED ON THIS GROUP:
1. XL330 SUB-VARIANT. M288 vs M077 is a COMMUNITY assumption, never stated by Pollen (SPEC.md 5, docs/PARTS.md row 32). Both cost the same and look identical. M077 delivers 0.215 N.m against M288's 0.52 N.m at 5.0 V. Ordering 1,500 of the wrong one is a $35,850 mistake. Settle it by reading the label on a production unit's servo.
2. SERVO SUPPLY RAIL. Datasheet max is 6.0 V; the NP-F550 pack window recorded in SPEC.md 5 is 6.6-8.2 V. A regulated 5.0 V rail is mandatory and it must carry 15 servos' stall current (1.47 A each at 5.0 V per the datasheet = 22.05 A worst case, all-stall). Whether the Pollen Robot HAT does this is CANNOT DETERMINE — that board has no published design files (docs/BOM.md P1), so this regulator is a board WE must design, and it belongs on the critical path.
3. THE 16x22x4 BEARING IS A SPECIALS SIZE. Decide now, before the printed parts are frozen, whether to accept a thin non-ISO supply base or spend the CAD change to move 8 parts onto ISO 6703 (17x23x4). The change is cheapest today and most expensive after tooling.
4. THE ANKLE REVISION. ankle_left/right (Y = 36.5000 mm) vs ankle_l_v1/ankle_r_v1 (Y = 46.4981 / 46.4973 mm) — a 9.998 mm difference in the axis the 15x10x3 pocket lives in. Nothing in the repo says which ships. Freeze it before the seat is toleranced.
5. THE ANKLE SEAT MUST BE REAMED. docs/DFM.md 209-211, verbatim: 'Ream it, or the 15x10x3 bearing will not seat.' Two reaming operations per robot (Ø15.0 H7) must appear in the process plan and the cycle-time budget. They are not currently in out/print/ (218 g PLA / 9.9 h + 26 g TPU / 2.4 h across 30 printed parts covers printing only).

RESPECTED, NOT PAPERED OVER: this group does not touch the head shell, the battery or the compute, but note that the ankle FEA (SF 2.02, the lowest PASS in out/stress/report.json) is the joint whose bearing seat is the one the DFM says will not seat as printed — the weakest structural link and the least reliable feature are the same part. Also note out/stress/report.json's upper-leg verdict is CANNOT DETERMINE (gmsh: 'Invalid boundary mesh (overlapping facets) on surface 350'), and the upper legs carry two XL330s each (hip pitch + knee) — the heaviest servo load in the robot sits in the one link with no valid stress result. Neither is a sourcing blocker, but both are reasons not to order 1,500 servos before the mesh is repaired and the ankle is re-run.

DISTRIBUTORS ATTEMPTED AND BLOCKED (recorded so no one repeats the work): robotis.co.uk / Robosavvy HTTP 403; RobotShop HTTP 403 (they list the XC330-M288-T and the X3P cable but the XL330-M288-T listing was not found); McMaster-Carr HTTP 403; accu-components.com HTTP 403; bearingbasement.com HTTP 403 (FAG 61700-2Z-HLC price therefore unasserted); Simply Bearings W61700 stainless page HTTP 404; Amazon ET2216ZZ listing HTTP 500 twice; smbbearings.com search HTTP 404 (they publish an ET2216 datasheet PDF at https://www.smbbearings.com/firebrick/ckeditor/plugins/upload/Uploads/Documents/bearingpdfs/ET2216-thin-section-bearing-16x22x4mm.pdf but no price). 123bearing lists both sizes (et2216-ezo, 61700, s6700) but publishes no price in the fetched page. No supplier, factory or person was contacted, per the brief — every figure above is a published web page, fetched and dated 2026-09-02.

DATASHEET FIGURES USED (https://emanual.robotis.com/docs/en/dxl/x/xl330-m288/, https://emanual.robotis.com/docs/en/dxl/x/xl330-m077/, https://emanual.robotis.com/docs/en/dxl/x/xc330-m288/, all fetched 2026-09-02): XL330-M288-T 20.0 x 34.0 x 26.0 mm, 18 g, 288.4:1, 3.7-6.0 V (rec 5.0 V), stall 0.42 / 0.52 / 0.60 N.m and no-load 76 / 103 / 123 rev/min at 3.7 / 5.0 / 6.0 V, 1.47 A at stall at 5.0 V, 12-bit contactless absolute encoder, 0.088 deg over 4096 steps. XL330-M077-T same body and mass, 77.5:1, stall 0.180 / 0.215 / 0.228 N.m, no-load 278 / 383 / 456 rev/min. XC330-M288-T same 20.0 x 34.0 x 26.0 mm body, 23 g, 288.35:1, stall 0.69 / 0.93 / 1.10 N.m, no-load 59 / 81 / 97 rev/min, full metal gear + 2 bearings.

lines.alternate: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, MPN SC1176. Digi-Key $15.00 @ qty 1, stock 0, MOQ 1, standard lead time 54 weeks, Part Status Active (https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/raspberry-pi/SC1176/15298147, read 2026-09-02). The Pi Hut GBP 14.40, SKU SC1176, available:false (https://thepihut.com/products/raspberry-pi-zero-2, read 2026-09-02). FOR: the footprint is already proven — the repo's own compute mesh IS a Pi Zero 2 W, `pcb__raspberry_pi_zero_2_w` measuring 65.0000 x 1.6000 x 30.0000 mm in out/verify/mech_dims.json, identical in plan to the Robot HAT mesh `elec_rpi_robot_hat_pcb` at 65.0250 x 30.0250 x 0.8400 mm, so the head's motor_support (73.5000 x 54.2000 x 18.8000 mm) needs no change; and robotd.toml records the 50 Hz control loop was "inherited from the prototype, where it was chosen on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2W", so the compute budget is demonstrated on this exact part. AGAINST: 512 MB vs 1 GB LPDDR4; NO eMMC — it boots microSD, and the Radxa has no SD slot, so a card aperture must be cut in the head shell; no 0.8 TOPS NPU; Wi-Fi 4 / BT 4.2 vs Wi-Fi 6 / BT 5.4; and the entire published device tree has to be re-derived — `compatible = "radxa,zero-3w"`, `/dev/ttyS2` for the 1 Mbps half-duplex Dynamixel bus, `i2s3_2ch` at 12.288 MHz sysclk for the aic3104, and the I2C3-to-M0 remux overlay (i2c3.dts, aic.dts) are all Radxa-specific. lines.risk: CRITICAL — WORST RISK IN THE GROUP, ON TWO COUNTS. (1) ZERO STOCK, NO CHANNEL DEPTH: every one of the three distributors that carry the part is out of stock on 2026-09-02 (32 variant records checked, all OutOfStock), none publishes a lead time, none publishes a volume price break, and searches of Digi-Key and Mouser returned no Radxa ZERO 3W listing at all — there is no broadline distributor to fall back on and no quotable lead time for a production run. (2) THE SPECIFIED SKU MAY NOT EXIST: the documented 1 GB + 32 GB eMMC build appears in no distributor's variant table. ACTION BEFORE ANY BUILD COMMITMENT: (a) settle the SKU with `lsblk` on a production robot; (b) get a written lead time and a qty-1000 price directly from Radxa/ALLNET — this is the one line in the group where a supplier quote, not a web price, is the deliverable; (c) qualify the Pi Zero 2 W path in parallel, accepting that it too shows Digi-Key stock 0 and a 54-week lead time, i.e. the whole 65 x 30 mm SBC class is supply-constrained on 2026-09-02.

The lens holder itself is also internally inconsistent in the repo: SPEC.md §4.3 records m12_lens_holder as 23.1 x 14.8 x 16.0 mm, while out/verify/mech_dims.json — the stated dimensional truth — reads 24.0000 x 14.8000 x 16.0000 mm, a 0.9 mm disagreement on X that must be resolved before a holder is printed or moulded.

Note also that the vision stack constrains the answer more than the lens catalogue does — the sensor is pinned to 1920x1080@30 with the ISP scaling to a 720p30 H.264 default (robotd.toml [media]; media:313, 449), and the ToF's own 45 deg x 45 deg cone sits 22.4 mm to the camera's left at world (81.4, 22.4, 249.1), so the sensible design rule is to choose the lens so the camera frame contains the ToF cone. ACTION: buy one LK005 kit ($99.99), fit it to a B0103, and settle the FOV against the ToF cone before this line is priced.

results.notes:
SCOPE, METHOD AND DATE. Group: "Compute, sensors & boards" for the Microduck rebuild. Every price, stock figure and lead time below was read live on 2026-09-02 and each carries the URL it came from. Quantities per robot are taken from docs/BOM.md §1 (B3 Radxa x1, B6 IMX219 camera board x1, B7 M12 lens x1, B9 ToF x1) and from the custom-PCB table (P1 Robot HAT carries the TLV320AIC3104 and the dormant BMI088; P2 imu_to_dxl v2 carries the LSM6DSV16X) — one of each per robot.

DISTRIBUTOR ACCESS, STATED HONESTLY. Digi-Key, LCSC, Pololu, SparkFun, UCTRONICS, Welectron, The Pi Hut, ALLNET China, Arace and ameriDroid all returned live pages and are quoted verbatim. Mouser, Newark/element14, Arrow, TME, RS, Future and Avnet all refused automated access on 2026-09-02 (Mouser and Newark returned bot-block pages; Arrow and TME timed out or 403'd). They are therefore NOT quoted — no price in this document is a guess, a conversion or an aggregator figure. Where a distributor publishes only GBP or EUR, price_1 is left null and the foreign figure is carried in the distributor's name field rather than converted at an unstated rate.

GROUP COST ROLL-UP: CANNOT DETERMINE, deliberately, at both qty 1 and qty 100. Three lines block it — the M12 lens has no specification so no part number (FOV "still being finalised"), the NFC controller has neither a confirmed part nor a confirmed quantity, and the Radxa's specified 1 GB/32 GB SKU does not exist at any distributor. What CAN be stated is the priced subset, cheapest-channel, per robot: camera module $35.00 (UCTRONICS) + VL53L8CX $8.77 (DK) + LSM6DSV16X $3.6298 (LCSC) + BMI088 $5.92 (DK) + TLV320AIC3104 $2.2518 (LCSC) = $55.5716 at qty 1, EXCLUDING compute, lens and NFC. The four chips alone at qty 100, cheapest channel: $6.72 + $2.6084 + $4.49 + $1.3890 = $15.2074 per robot. Add the Radxa at its nearest orderable SKU ($22.00 for 1 GB/8 GB eMMC at ALLNET, currently out of stock) and the qty-1 figure becomes $77.5716 — but that substitutes an 8 GB eMMC for the documented 32 GB, so it is not the robot's cost, and it is not carried into the structured totals.

THE THREE FINDINGS THAT GOVERN THIS GROUP, none of them papered over.
1. THE COMPUTE BOARD IS THE PROGRAMME RISK. All 32 Radxa ZERO 3W variant records across three distributors read OutOfStock/available:false on 2026-09-02; no lead time and no volume price is published anywhere; and Digi-Key and Mouser searches return no Radxa ZERO 3W listing at all, so there is no broadline fallback. On top of that the documented 1 GB + 32 GB eMMC configuration has no SKU in any variant table (the eMMC pairing runs 1->8, 2->16, 4->32, 8->32/64 GB), which independently confirms the CANNOT DETERMINE already standing in ce-parts/radxa-zero-3w. The obvious alternate is no better today: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (SC1176) is $15.00 at Digi-Key with stock 0 and a 54-week lead time, and sold out at The Pi Hut. Nothing else in this group should be ordered before this is resolved with a direct written quote.
2. THE HEAD IS NOT YET TOOLABLE, AND FOUR OF THESE LINES LIVE IN IT. The camera at world (81.4, 0, 251.1), the ToF at (81.4, 22.4, 249.1), the head IMU at (59.2, 0, 250.8) and the compute board itself all sit inside a head whose simulation mesh top_head_shell measures 91.7595 x 122.6900 x 46.3361 mm (out/verify/mech_dims.json, 47 meshes, 4 dp) and DOES NOT MATCH the compact domed head in the product photographs. Lens aperture, M12 holder boss and ToF window cannot be positioned from this mesh. A second, smaller dimensional conflict sits on the same assembly: SPEC.md §4.3 gives m12_lens_holder as 23.1 x 14.8 x 16.0 mm while out/verify/mech_dims.json — the stated dimensional truth — reads 24.0000 x 14.8000 x 16.0000 mm, a 0.9000 mm disagreement on X. Resolve both before any head tooling or lens selection.
3. TWO OF THESE CHIPS HAVE NO BOARD TO GO ON. The TLV320AIC3104 and the BMI088 belong to the Robot HAT and the LSM6DSV16X to imu_to_dxl v2; docs/BOM.md P1-P3 records that all three custom PCBs — Robot HAT, imu_to_dxl, banana contact — have NO published design files. These lines are buyable but not yet assemblable; PCB design is on the critical path ahead of the component buy.

LEAD-TIME AND SINGLE-SOURCE LEDGER (Digi-Key standard lead times, read 2026-09-02): FUSB302BMPX 56 weeks (longest — and it should never be a BOM line, see that entry); Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W 54 weeks; PN7150 30 weeks; LSM6DSV16X and LSM6DSV16BX 24 weeks; VL53L8CX and VL53L5CX 22 weeks; TLV320AIC3104 and BMI088 16 weeks; Radxa ZERO 3W CANNOT DETERMINE (no distributor publishes one). Every semiconductor in this group is single-manufacturer — ST for the ToF and the control IMU, TI for the codec, Bosch for the head IMU, NXP for the NFC candidate — so second-sourcing here means a second PART, not a second maker. Only the ToF has a genuine drop-in second part today: Pollen's own driver supports BOTH the VL53L8CX and the VL53L5CX ("Both sensor generations are supported", tof:83-85), so dual-qualifying them removes that line's risk almost entirely and should be done.

TIGHTEST STOCK: TLV320AIC3104IRHBR, 64 pieces at Digi-Key plus 418 at LCSC = 482 visible against 1 per robot. A 1,000-robot build cannot be covered from catalogue stock; the reel is a 16-week long-lead buy and Digi-Key's T&R MOQ of 3,000 is 3x the need. BMI088 shows Digi-Key stock 0 with 5,000 due 08-Sep-2026.

CHANNEL ARBITRAGE, WORTH REAL MONEY AND NOT UNIFORM IN DIRECTION. At qty 1000 LCSC beats Digi-Key on LSM6DSV16X ($2.4445 vs $4.13, -40.8%), TLV320AIC3104 ($1.2288 vs a Digi-Key ladder with no 1000 break at all) and PN7150 ($3.6339 vs $8.03, -54.7%). But LCSC is DEARER on BMI088 ($6.8317 vs $4.49 at qty 100, +52%) and on VL53L8CX ($7.4363 vs $6.72 at qty 100, +10.7%). Buy per part, not per distributor. Combined at qty 1000 the cheapest-channel split saves roughly $6.20 per robot on these four chips versus buying everything from one house.

TWO COST DELETIONS ALREADY AVAILABLE. (a) The BMI088 is dormant in Pollen's own device tree and read by no shipped code — omitting it saves $4.07-$5.92 per robot and $4,070 at 1,000 units, at zero functional cost. (b) Moving the ToF from a plug-in carrier ($19.43-$27.63) to the bare LGA-16 on the Robot HAT ($6.06-$6.72) saves roughly $13-$21 per robot and deletes a connector and a cable from a machine that walks; the HAT must then supply the sensor's 1.2/1.8 V IOVDD rail, which the carrier currently hides.

NO SUPPLIER, FACTORY OR PERSON WAS CONTACTED. This is a document produced from published distributor pages and the repository's own measured files only. Where the brief asked for two distributors and only brokers exist — the bare Sony IMX219PQH5-C — the answer is CANNOT DETERMINE with null and an explicit recommendation to buy the camera as a module rather than quote a broker price for a bare CMOS imager.

ROBOTIS' own connector table states 'Wire Gauge for DYNAMIXEL — 21 AWG', yet the crimp terminal that same table specifies is rated 22–26 AWG by DigiKey and 0.05–0.33 mm² / 22–30 AWG by LCSC. 21 AWG is 0.410 mm² — it EXCEEDS the terminal's 0.33 mm² published maximum. You cannot build a compliant crimp at 21 AWG with SEH-001T-P0.6. RESOLUTION: build the loom in 22 AWG. This is already proven adequate in this design — wiring/CABLES.md runs the drop analysis at AWG 22 and returns PASS at both ends of the pack window: at 8.2 V the farthest ankle (id24/id14) receives 7.506 V, total drop HAT→ankle 0.694 V; at 6.6 V it receives 5.906 V. The 6.6 V case is worth stating plainly: a far ankle servo reads 694 mV below the 6.6 V threshold robotd uses for 'empty', so the farthest device on the chain trips empty first by that margin — that is a firmware-threshold decision, not a wire fault. results.notes:
SCOPE, DATE AND METHOD. All distributor prices below were read on 2026-09-02. A price is recorded only where a page was actually fetched and returned it; where a figure came from a search-result snippet without the page rendering, it is labelled as such in the distributor's lead_time field and the numeric fields are left null. Nothing is estimated, converted between currencies without a rate source, or interpolated between published tiers. Quantities per robot come from the repo, cited per line.

=== THE ONE CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF ===
This group was scoped as a "wiring/JST-GH harness". JST-GH is used in exactly ONE net in this robot. The authority is ROBOTIS' own e-Manual include _includes/en/dxl/jst_ttl.md, which specifies the XL330-M288-T TTL port as: Pinout 1 GND / 2 VDD / 3 DATA; Housing JST EHR-03; PCB Header JST B3B-EH-A; Crimp Terminal JST SEH-001T-P0.6; Wire Gauge for DYNAMIXEL 21 AWG. That is JST EH at 2.50 mm pitch, and it confirms wiring/CABLES.md exactly. The harness therefore breaks down as: sixteen servo-bus leads in JST EH 2.50 mm; one ToF lead in JST SH 1.00 mm (Stemma/Qwiic); one speaker lead in JST GH 1.25 mm — the only GH in the robot; one 22-pin 0.50 mm FFC for the camera; one battery run. Sourcing this group as GH throughout would have bought the wrong connector for 16 of 20 cables.

=== THE HARD CONFLICT YOU MUST RESOLVE BEFORE CUTTING WIRE ===
ROBOTIS' table says 21 AWG. The crimp terminal in that same table, SEH-001T-P0.6, is rated 22–26 AWG by DigiKey and 0.05–0.33 mm² / 22–30 AWG by LCSC. 21 AWG is 0.410 mm² and EXCEEDS the 0.33 mm² published maximum — you cannot build a compliant crimp at 21 AWG with the terminal ROBOTIS specifies. Build the loom in 22 AWG. This is already proven adequate for this design: wiring/CABLES.md runs the drop analysis at AWG 22 and returns PASS at both ends of the pack window. At 8.2 V the farthest ankle servo (id24 / id14) receives 7.506 V, total drop HAT→ankle 0.694 V. At 6.6 V it receives 5.906 V — 694 mV below the 6.6 V "empty" threshold that robotd reads from the servos (model.rs:99-128), so the farthest device on the chain trips empty first by that margin. That is a firmware-threshold decision, not a wire fault, and it should be written into the acceptance criteria. Basis of the drop model, stated so it is not mistaken for measurement: 1 A per moving servo applied to every servo downstream of each hop, an assumption sitting between the vendor's published 17 mA standby and 1.47 A stall at 5.0 V, because ROBOTIS publishes no running current.

=== SUPPLY RISKS, RANKED ===
1. NP-F550 PACK — no volume price exists anywhere. Every reachable seller is a photo-accessory retailer; two pages state outright that they publish no bulk pricing, and Neewer's own store had both the single and the 2-pack SOLD OUT on the day of research. qty-100 and qty-1000 are CANNOT DETERMINE. Compounding it: EU Batteries Regulation 2023/1542 labelling obligations began 18 Aug 2026, fifteen days before this document, with end-user removability from 18 Feb 2027 (the removable NP-F550 passes that by design); and air freight needs a UN 38.3 test summary from the pack maker, which no retail seller publishes. The robot has no power switch, so the shipping insert must isolate the contacts or the pack must ship unseated.
2. GHR-02V-S — ZERO STOCK at DigiKey today, restock quoted 2026-12-16, behind a 16-week factory lead. It is also the least important part in the group (one speaker connector), so the fix is to design the HAT footprint to also accept Molex PicoBlade 51021-0200, not to expedite JST.
3. THE 16-WEEK JST LEAD, GROUP-WIDE — DigiKey states "Manufacturer Standard Lead Time: 16 weeks" on EHR-3, SEH-001T-P0.6, B3B-EH-A, GHR-02V-S and SSHL-002T-P0.2 alike. Distributor stock is deep today (76,945 EHR-3; 777,956 SEH crimps), so this bites only on a step change in volume — but a 100-robot build consumes 3,200 housings and 9,600 crimps, and a 1,000-robot build 32,000 and 96,000. Order a quarter ahead of need. By contrast the Alpha Wire spool is 4 weeks, the shortest lead in the group.
4. HEAT-SET INSERTS ARE A SINGLE SOURCE IN DISGUISE — three distributors (CNCKitchen DE, Vector 3D UK, Prusa), one manufacturer. Prusa's own page names CNC Kitchen as the maker. The 21% spread across them (€0.0990 / £0.0974 / $0.1199 each) is channel margin, not competition. No 1,000-piece tier exists at any of them. Closing this with a standard industrial insert (Böllhoff IUB/IUC, PEM SI-M2, Tappex Multisert) is the highest-value sourcing action remaining in this group.
5. TPU PRICE DISPERSION — the identical MPN U00-K0-1.75-1000-SPL is $33.80 at 3DJake and $55.99 at MatterHackers, a 66% spread and a $0.581/robot swing on a $0.886 line.
6. FASTENER PRICE DISCOVERY IS NIL — not one of the M2, M2.5 or M2-nut distributors reached publishes a qty-100 or qty-1000 break. Accu, the one distributor that does publish full tier ladders, returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch; McMaster-Carr likewise. Someone with a browser should read Accu's ladder for SSCF-M2-4-A2, SSCF-M2-6-A2, SSC-M2-8-A2, SSC-M2-12-A2 and HPN-M2-A2 — that single session would close five CANNOT DETERMINEs.

=== THE BOUGHT-CABLE vs SELF-CRIMPED DECISION, WITH THE ARITHMETIC ===
Bought: ROBOTIS X3P 180 mm at $19.00/10 (ROBOTIS international) = $1.900 per cable; 16 cables needs 2 packs = $38.00 per robot with 4 spares. Only ONE length is priced in this family, and the design needs nine distinct lengths (20, 35, 40, 50, 60, 65, 95, 120, 125, 165 mm; 1155 mm consumed in total). Twelve of the sixteen links would carry 55–160 mm of surplus wire, in a robot whose zero-pose envelope is 144.1 × 141.0 × 264.0 mm, routed through hinges spanning up to 520°. The shorter ROBOTIS cables in the same catalogue (36/56/81 mm) are X335-series with HRS connectors — wrong family — and carry a stated 56-day lead time.
Self-crimped: 2 × EHR-3 + 6 × SEH-001T-P0.6 per lead = $0.0786 at the LCSC qty-1000 tiers, a 24× reduction on connector cost, and you get the exact lengths. But the wire inverts it: at the only fetched 22 AWG price (Alpha Wire 3051 WU005, $84.15 per 30.5 m spool = $2.759/m), the 3.465 m of bus conductor per robot costs $9.56 — more than the connectors it saves. The self-crimp route only wins on a commodity spool, and no commodity 22 AWG price was obtainable from a fetched page. DO NOT BOOK THE CRIMPING SAVING until that price exists.

=== COST ROLL-UP AND WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT INCLUDE ===
group_cost_qty1_usd = $70.24 per robot, composed of exactly seven priced lines: NP-F550 pack + dual-charger share $14.995 (half of the Wasabi WSB-KIT-BB-NPF550 kit at $29.99, the same half-of-a-2-pack-plus-charger method the repo uses for its NextBatteries line); 2 × ROBOTIS X3P 10-packs $38.00; 80 × M2×6 at $0.0400 (U-Turn M26D912A2) $3.20; 60 × M2 heat-set inserts at $0.1199 (Prusa) $7.194; 218.295 g PLA at $22.99/kg (GigaParts) $5.018; 26.203 g TPU at $33.80/kg (3DJake) $0.886; 1 × 22-pin FFC $0.95 (Adafruit 6035).

=== KNOWN CRITICAL FINDINGS — HOW EACH LANDS IN THIS GROUP ===
FINDING 2 (battery mesh mislabelled) is confirmed and load-bearing here: the mesh named np_f970 measures 38.6085 × 20.5755 × 70.8086 mm (out/verify/mech_dims.json), which is the NP-F550 envelope, not an F970. The docs are right and the file name is wrong. Anyone sizing the cradle from the file name would buy the wrong pack. The parts that constrain it are measured and PASS: power_support reference 54.5000 × 17.0000 × 83.4898 mm against rebuild 54.4660 × 17.0000 × 83.1302 mm, max deviation 0.3596 mm; banana_pcb_locker reference 54.0501 × 3.8000 × 6.6524 mm against rebuild 54.0153 × 3.8000 × 6.6260 mm, max deviation 0.0348 mm. Tolerance basis for all of these: FreeCAD Mesh.BoundBox bounding-box comparison, reference meshes in metres scaled ×1000, rebuilds native mm; surface-distance p95 ≤ 1.0 mm is a separate check that lives in the refcheck ledger, not in this file.
FINDING 3 (Pi Zero 2 W placeholder vs Radxa Zero 3W) directly blocks the camera FFC line: both are 65 × 30 mm, so the outline is no help, and the placeholder cannot settle either the FFC contact orientation (A-A vs A-B) or the camera-board connector (22-pin 0.5 mm vs 15-pin 1.0 mm). Both are CANNOT DETERMINE and both must be resolved before an FFC part number is committed.
FINDING 5 (three custom PCBs with no design files) is why the B3B-EH-A quantity per robot is CANNOT DETERMINE and why the banana contact block has no distributor at all. These are parts to be designed, not bought.
FINDING 1 (head mesh does not match the product photographs) and FINDING 4 (two ankle revisions, ankle_left Y = 36.500 vs ankle_l_v1 Y = 46.500 mm) do not touch any line in this group directly, but FINDING 4 is worth flagging to whoever orders fasteners: the ankle carries 5 M2 clearance holes and 5 counterbores, and the two revisions differ by 10.000 mm in Y — confirm which revision the fastener count was taken from before ordering.
